title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄序
嘉靖戊子爲天下大比之期
先是輔臣議諸藩科目貢非
其人維司文柄者弗稱厥職
請以近臣若科若部寺屬易
之
上曰可届期禮部量地遠近先後
===
疏名以
請
上命署員外郎臣銓主事臣以達
往柄福建試事維時巡按監
察御史臣豹先以禮聘教授
臣善學正臣前教諭臣鉄臣
文彬臣璧臣秀春訓導臣大
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄序

嘉靖戊子，爲天下大比之期。先是，輔臣議諸藩科目貢非其人，維司文柄者弗稱厥職，請以近臣若科若部寺屬易之。上曰：「可。」届期，禮部量地遠近，先後疏名以請。上命署員外郎臣銓、主事臣以達往柄福建試事。維時，巡按監察御史臣豹先以禮聘教授臣善、學正臣前、教諭臣鉄、臣文彬、臣璧、臣秀春、訓導臣大
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

The wuzi year of Jiajing [1528] was the year appointed for the triennial examinations throughout the realm. Previously, the grand secretaries had argued that the provincial examinations were recommending unsuitable men because those entrusted with judging literary merit were failing to discharge their duties adequately. They requested that these examiners be replaced by officials serving close to the throne, drawn from the Offices of Scrutiny, the ministries, and the courts. His Majesty said, “Approved.” As the appointed time approached, the Ministry of Rites, taking account of the distances involved, submitted names in successive memorials for imperial approval. His Majesty ordered your servants Quan, Acting Vice Director, and Yida, Secretary, to go and take charge of the Fujian examination. At that time, your servant Bao, Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, had already formally invited your servants Shan, Prefectural School Instructor; Qian, Subprefectural School Instructor; Tie, Wenbin, Bi, and Xiuchun, County School Instructors; and Da…, Assistant Instructor…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
本臣文臣鈞爲同考試比臣
等偕至移檄藩臬提調則左
布政使臣約右布政使臣馴
監試則按察使臣用副使臣
持平其餘百執事皆慎選以
充而御史臣豹實監臨之乃
更相戒誓入院合董學副使
===
臣吳仕所選士貳千陸百有
奇如故事三試之取其雋九
十人倂刻文若干篇遵
定制也而士以數遺文以額拘
者多矣事且竣臣銓以職事
當序諸首簡以告諸士竊惟
士之以文就試若輸約於上
punctuated:
本、臣文、臣鈞爲同考試。比臣等偕至，移檄藩臬，提調則左布政使臣約、右布政使臣馴，監試則按察使臣用、副使臣持平。其餘百執事皆慎選以充，而御史臣豹實監臨之。乃更相戒誓，入院，合董學副使臣吳仕所選士貳千陸百有奇，如故事三試之，取其雋九十人，倂刻文若干篇，遵定制也。而士以數遺、文以額拘者多矣。
事且竣，臣銓以職事當序諸首簡，以告諸士。竊惟士之以文就試，若輸約於上
translation_en:
…Daben, Wen, and Jun as Associate Examiners. When we had all arrived, official communications were sent to the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions. The Proctors were Yue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Xun, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; those overseeing the examination were Yong, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Chiping, Surveillance Vice Commissioner. All the other functionaries were carefully selected to fill their posts, while Bao, the Censor, served as Supervising Official. We then admonished one another and exchanged pledges before entering the examination compound. We assembled the more than 2,600 candidates selected by Wu Shi, the Surveillance Vice Commissioner supervising education, and examined them in three sessions according to established practice. We selected ninety of the outstanding candidates and had a number of their essays printed together, in accordance with the prescribed regulations. Yet many candidates were excluded by the numerical limit, and many essays were kept out by the quota.
As the proceedings approached completion, I, Quan, was obliged by my office to write a preface on the opening leaves, addressing the candidates. I humbly consider that when scholars present themselves for examination through their writings, it is as though they submit a pledge to their superiors…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
也有司刊文以爲錄若識約
以要之於後也大而非誇遠
而有徴言斯踐矣踐斯實矣
而豈徒爲文具乎哉在昔傅
說載見高宗式陳說命卒佐
理中興以光昭商祚諸葛孔
明論天下事於草廬落落難
===
合及出而疏附昭烈撫荆定
益以鼎立天下雖邂逅之言
若符節然古之君子言不易
志行不食言矧曰載在簡書
布傳遐邇對揚
殿陛將以永徴于辭而顧有貳
心哉
punctuated: 也。有司刊文以爲錄，若識約以要之於後也。大而非誇，遠而有徴，言斯踐矣，踐斯實矣，而豈徒爲文具乎哉？在昔傅說載見高宗，式陳《說命》，卒佐理中興，以光昭商祚。諸葛孔明論天下事於草廬，落落難合；及出而疏附昭烈，撫荆定益，以鼎立天下。雖邂逅之言，若符節然。古之君子，言不易志，行不食言。矧曰載在簡書，布傳遐邇，對揚殿陛，將以永徴于辭，而顧有貳心哉？
translation_en:
… The responsible officials print the compositions as an examination record, as though recording a compact by which to hold the candidates accountable thereafter. Grand without exaggeration, far-reaching yet supported by evidence: what is said must be put into practice, and what is practiced must be made real. How could this be merely a matter of literary formality?

In antiquity, Fu Yue met Gaozong, and the Charge to Yue (Yue ming) set forth their counsels. He ultimately assisted in governing and restoring the dynasty, bringing glory to the Shang imperial line. Zhuge Kongming discussed the affairs of the realm in his thatched cottage; his ideas stood far apart from prevailing views and were difficult to reconcile with them. Yet when he emerged into public service, he rallied support for Emperor Zhaolie, pacified Jing and secured Yi, and established one of the three powers dividing the realm. Though spoken at a chance encounter, his words matched his deeds like the two halves of a tally.

The gentlemen of antiquity did not alter their resolve after speaking, nor did their conduct belie their words. How much more must this hold when their words are entered into written records, circulated far and near, and presented in grateful response before the throne, to stand forever as testimony! Could they then harbor a divided purpose?

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上御極以來激勵士氣丕顯人
文玆又愼擇主試
分遣近臣申飭令甲曰必錄實
毋示人以飾必根理切事毋
惑於浮靡以喪眞詭異以壞
習惟朴惟庬才罔眩蔽所以
振作鼓舞之典益重且切矣
===
以今試文觀之皆簡明純正
通達典雅彬彬乎有賈董之
風蓋
德意所向士咸祓除舊習以望迎
休美而
神機速化有不知所以爲之者矣
然亦自誓無負於斯言否乎
punctuated:
皇上御極以來，激勵士氣，丕顯人文。玆又愼擇主試，分遣近臣，申飭令甲曰：「必錄實，毋示人以飾；必根理切事，毋惑於浮靡以喪眞、詭異以壞習。惟朴惟庬，才罔眩蔽。」所以振作鼓舞之典，益重且切矣。
以今試文觀之，皆簡明純正，通達典雅，彬彬乎有賈董之風。蓋德意所向，士咸祓除舊習，以望迎休美，而神機速化，有不知所以爲之者矣。然亦自誓無負於斯言否乎？
translation_en:
Since His Majesty ascended the throne, he has encouraged the spirit of scholars and splendidly promoted literary culture. Now he has again carefully selected the presiding Examiners and dispatched his close ministers to their respective assignments, reiterating the regulations: “You must select for substance; do not teach men to rely on embellishment. Their writing must be grounded in principle and pertinent to affairs. Do not be beguiled by superficial elegance that sacrifices authenticity, or by eccentricity that corrupts scholarly habits. Favor simplicity and substance, so that talent is neither dazzlingly misrepresented nor obscured.” The measures for rousing and encouraging scholars have thus become still more weighty and urgent.
Judging by the essays in this examination, all are concise and clear, pure and correct, lucid and refined. In their cultivated balance, they possess the manner of Jia Yi and Dong Zhongshu. Guided by His Majesty’s virtuous intentions, the scholars have all purged their old habits, hoping to welcome what is excellent. His wondrous efficacy has transformed them so swiftly that they themselves do not understand how it has come about. Yet have they also sworn to themselves not to fall short of these words?

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫雕鏤絺繪澆漓道體斲損
元氣士實恥之然使返朴就
厖亦不過空言附會無所於
用
國家將何賴焉我
皇上銳意政紀一時
德令之和布
===
戒諭之播告誠心實政必行弗
返亦既以
身率之諸士絃誦之餘慶幸遭逢
引領北望豈不曰庶幾
紹復堯舜禹湯之盛以覆育天下
至私為身圖豈其無所典刑
以求奮効于
punctuated: 夫雕鏤絺繪，澆漓道體，斲損元氣，士實恥之。然使返朴就厖，亦不過空言附會，無所於用，國家將何賴焉？我皇上銳意政紀，一時德令之和布、戒諭之播告，誠心實政，必行弗返，亦既以身率之。諸士絃誦之餘，慶幸遭逢，引領北望，豈不曰：「庶幾紹復堯舜禹湯之盛，以覆育天下！」至私為身圖，豈其無所典刑，以求奮効于
translation_en: Elaborate carving and embroidered ornament dilute the substance of the Way and impair its vital energy: scholars are indeed ashamed of these things. Yet if their return to simplicity and substance amounts merely to empty words and forced associations, with no practical use, on what will the state be able to rely? Our Emperor is intent upon putting government in order. His beneficent commands are graciously promulgated, and his admonitions proclaimed throughout the realm. With sincere purpose and substantive measures, he is determined to carry them through without turning back; he has already led by personal example. Amid their studies, accompanied by strings and recitation, the scholars rejoice in their good fortune to have encountered such a time. Craning their necks to gaze northward, would they not say: “May he carry on and restore the flourishing rule of Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang, sheltering and nurturing all under Heaven!” And when they privately consider their own course, surely they have models to follow, that they may strive to render service in…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
旹玆風簷寸晷之下露鋒脫穎
旁無忌諱嘉樂三五貶斥唐
漢縱橫溢發周旋道義使能
强志而力行守信而終業毋
震懾險難以渝節毋饜飫利
慾以侈心雖詩書所稱臯夔
伊傅之勳其何足讓夫農夫
===
之治田織婦之浴蠶竭終歲
之力然後享布帛菽粟之利
大賈操竒贏以遊都市反邀
天下之貨利而若身有之銓
實懼士之以賈而文也不以
農也不然文者志之華也行
者文之實也古之人有言曰
punctuated: 旹，玆風簷寸晷之下，露鋒脫穎，旁無忌諱，嘉樂三五，貶斥唐漢，縱橫溢發，周旋道義。使能强志而力行，守信而終業，毋震懾險難以渝節，毋饜飫利慾以侈心，雖詩書所稱臯夔伊傅之勳，其何足讓？夫農夫之治田，織婦之浴蠶，竭終歲之力，然後享布帛菽粟之利。大賈操竒贏以遊都市，反邀天下之貨利，而若身有之。銓實懼士之以賈而文也，不以農也。不然，文者志之華也，行者文之實也。古之人有言曰：
translation_en:
…at such a time. Here, beneath the wind-swept eaves, in the brief time allotted, they reveal their sharpness and display their talents, with no inhibitions on any side. They praise the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and disparage the Tang and Han; their words flow freely and abundantly, always moving within the bounds of the Way and righteousness. If they can strengthen their resolve and earnestly put it into practice, remain faithful and complete their undertaking, neither letting fear of danger and hardship compromise their integrity nor letting indulgence in profit and desire inflate their ambitions, why should they yield even to the achievements of Gao, Kui, Yi, and Fu, celebrated in the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents?

Now, the farmer tending his fields and the weaving woman bathing her silkworms exhaust a whole year’s strength before enjoying the benefits of cloth, silk, beans, and grain. The great merchant, carrying surplus goods and capital, travels through the cities and markets, yet gathers in the goods and profits of the world as though they were his own. I, Quan, truly fear that scholars approach literary composition as merchants do, rather than as farmers do. Otherwise, literary expression is the flowering of aspiration, and conduct is the fruit of literary expression. A man of antiquity once said: …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
有志者事竟成銓知免於戾
矣玆舉也雅志崇尚維鎭守
太監臣趙誠市舶左少監臣
師章協力賛襄維左叅政臣
徐問右叅政臣侯位左叅議
臣謝顯右叅議臣蕭廷傑副
使臣王俊民僉事臣伍希周
===
臣曾鵬臣屈儒防守巡邏維
署都指揮僉事臣侯汴於試
事與有勞焉謹併書以
獻
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署
員外郎事主事陸銓謹序
punctuated:
「有志者事竟成。」銓知免於戾矣。玆舉也，雅志崇尚，維鎭守太監臣趙誠、市舶左少監臣師章；協力賛襄，維左叅政臣徐問、右叅政臣侯位、左叅議臣謝顯、右叅議臣蕭廷傑、副使臣王俊民、僉事臣伍希周、臣曾鵬、臣屈儒；防守巡邏，維署都指揮僉事臣侯汴，於試事與有勞焉。謹併書以獻。
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署員外郎事主事陸銓謹序。
translation_en:
…“Where there is resolve, endeavors ultimately succeed.” I, Quan, know that I may thus escape blame. In this examination, those whose noble intentions upheld its importance were your servants Zhao Cheng, the Grand Eunuch stationed as Regional Defender, and Shi Zhang, Left Junior Director of Maritime Trade. Those who joined forces to assist were your servants Xu Wen, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Hou Wei, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Xie Xian, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Xiao Tingjie, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; Wang Junmin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and Wu Xizhou, Zeng Peng, and Qu Ru, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners. Responsible for guarding and patrolling was your servant Hou Bian, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. All rendered service in the conduct of the examination. I respectfully record them together here for presentation to the throne.
Preface respectfully composed by Lu Quan, Gentleman for Receiving Virtue and Secretary acting as Vice Director in the Bureau of the Arsenal, Ministry of War.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖七年福建鄉試
監臨官
巡按福建監察御史聶豹〔文蔚江西永豐縣人丁丑進士〕
提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使查約〔原博浙江海寧縣人壬戌進士〕
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使馮馴〔行健四川岳池縣人戊辰進士〕
監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使周用〔行之直隸吳江縣人壬戌進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司副使郭持平〔守衡江西萬安縣人丁丑進士〕
===
考試官
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署員外郎事主事陸銓〔選之浙江鄞縣人癸未進士〕
承直郎刑部福建清吏司主事江以達〔于順江西貴溪縣人丙戌進士〕
同考試官
廣東雷州府儒學教授彭善〔性夫廣東東莞縣人癸酉貢士〕
直隸揚州府高郵州儒學學正王前〔光卿河南鈞州官籍浙江平陽縣人癸酉貢士〕
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭潘鈇〔希義直隸婺源縣人乙酉貢士〕
廣東廣州府增城縣儒學教諭易文彬〔中甫廣西臨桂縣人癸酉貢士〕
浙江金華府東陽縣儒學教諭舒璧〔拱極江西臨川縣人壬午貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖七年福建鄉試

監臨官
巡按福建監察御史聶豹〔文蔚，江西永豐縣人，丁丑進士〕。

提調官
福建等處承宣布政使司左布政使查約〔原博，浙江海寧縣人，壬戌進士〕。
福建等處承宣布政使司右布政使馮馴〔行健，四川岳池縣人，戊辰進士〕。

監試官
福建等處提刑按察司按察使周用〔行之，直隸吳江縣人，壬戌進士〕。
福建等處提刑按察司副使郭持平〔守衡，江西萬安縣人，丁丑進士〕。

考試官
承德郎兵部武庫清吏司署員外郎事主事陸銓〔選之，浙江鄞縣人，癸未進士〕。
承直郎刑部福建清吏司主事江以達〔于順，江西貴溪縣人，丙戌進士〕。

同考試官
廣東雷州府儒學教授彭善〔性夫，廣東東莞縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
直隸揚州府高郵州儒學學正王前〔光卿，河南鈞州官籍，浙江平陽縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
江西饒州府鄱陽縣儒學教諭潘鈇〔希義，直隸婺源縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
廣東廣州府增城縣儒學教諭易文彬〔中甫，廣西臨桂縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
浙江金華府東陽縣儒學教諭舒璧〔拱極，江西臨川縣人，壬午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Fujian Provincial Examination, Seventh Year of Jiajing (1528)

Supervising Official
Nie Bao, Investigating Censor assigned to inspect Fujian. His courtesy name was Wenwei; he was from Yongfeng County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingchou year.

Proctors
Zha Yue, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner in the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Yuanbo; he was from Haining County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.
Feng Xun, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner in the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Xingjian; he was from Yuechi County, Sichuan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Zhou Yong, Surveillance Commissioner in the Fujian Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Xingzhi; he was from Wujiang County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.
Guo Chiping, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in the Fujian Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Shouheng; he was from Wan'an County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Examiners
Lu Quan, Gentleman for Rendering Virtue and Secretary acting as Vice Director in the Bureau of the Arsenal, Ministry of War. His courtesy name was Xuanzhi; he was from Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.
Jiang Yida, Gentleman for Straightforward Service and Secretary in the Fujian Bureau, Ministry of Justice. His courtesy name was Yushun; he was from Guixi County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.

Associate Examiners
Peng Shan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Leizhou Prefecture, Guangdong. His courtesy name was Xingfu; he was from Dongguan County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the guiyou year.
Wang Qian, Instructor in the Confucian School of Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili. His courtesy name was Guangqing; he held official registration in Junzhou, Henan, was originally from Pingyang County, Zhejiang, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.
Pan Fu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Poyang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Xiyi; he was from Wuyuan County, Zhili, and was a tribute student of the yiyou year.
Yi Wenbin, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zengcheng County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. His courtesy name was Zhongfu; he was from Lingui County, Guangxi, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.
Shu Bi, Instructor in the Confucian School of Dongyang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Gongji; he was from Linchuan County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute student of the renwu year.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
直隸滁州全椒縣儒學教諭李秀春〔元甫四川長壽縣人乙酉貢士〕
直隸淮安府儒學訓導李大本〔立甫湖廣公安縣人癸酉貢士〕
浙江杭州府儒學訓導霍文〔子靜貴州前衛官籍山東濟寧州人丙子貢士〕
直隸蘇州府儒學訓導陳鈞〔秉中河南祥符縣人己卯貢士〕
印卷官
福建等處承宣布政使司理問所理問金樸〔文甫浙江鄞縣人丁丑進士〕
福建等處提刑按察司經歷司知事吳材〔大用湖廣監利縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
福建都轉運鹽使司運使李彥〔邦直江西袁州衛籍豐城縣人戊辰進士〕
===
福州府知府朱豹〔子文直隸上海縣人丁丑進士〕
受卷官
興化府知府葉觀〔國光直隸江都縣人丁丑進士〕
泉州府知府顧可久〔與新直隸無錫縣人甲戌進士〕
建寧府同知余禕〔子修江西鄱陽縣人甲子貢士〕
彌封官
邵武府同知鄒武〔靖之直隸常熟縣人甲子貢士〕
福州府推官陳大咸〔宏感廣東海陽縣人丙戌進士〕
建寧府建陽縣知縣薛宗鎧〔子修廣東揭陽縣人癸未進士〕
punctuated:
直隸滁州全椒縣儒學教諭李秀春〔元甫，四川長壽縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
直隸淮安府儒學訓導李大本〔立甫，湖廣公安縣人，癸酉貢士〕。
浙江杭州府儒學訓導霍文〔子靜，貴州前衛官籍，山東濟寧州人，丙子貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府儒學訓導陳鈞〔秉中，河南祥符縣人，己卯貢士〕。

印卷官
福建等處承宣布政使司理問所理問金樸〔文甫，浙江鄞縣人，丁丑進士〕。
福建等處提刑按察司經歷司知事吳材〔大用，湖廣監利縣人，監生〕。

收掌試卷官
福建都轉運鹽使司運使李彥〔邦直，江西袁州衛籍，豐城縣人，戊辰進士〕。
福州府知府朱豹〔子文，直隸上海縣人，丁丑進士〕。

受卷官
興化府知府葉觀〔國光，直隸江都縣人，丁丑進士〕。
泉州府知府顧可久〔與新，直隸無錫縣人，甲戌進士〕。
建寧府同知余禕〔子修，江西鄱陽縣人，甲子貢士〕。

彌封官
邵武府同知鄒武〔靖之，直隸常熟縣人，甲子貢士〕。
福州府推官陳大咸〔宏感，廣東海陽縣人，丙戌進士〕。
建寧府建陽縣知縣薛宗鎧〔子修，廣東揭陽縣人，癸未進士〕。
translation_en:
Li Xiuchun, Instructor in the Confucian School of Quanjiao County, Chuzhou, Zhili, had the courtesy name Yuanfu. He was from Changshou County, Sichuan, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.
Li Daben, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Huai'an Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Lifu. He was from Gong'an County, Huguang, and was a tribute student of the guiyou year.
Huo Wen, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Zijing. He belonged to the official register of Guizhou Front Guard, was a native of Jining Subprefecture, Shandong, and was a tribute student of the bingzi year.
Chen Jun, Assistant Instructor in the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Bingzhong. He was from Xiangfu County, Henan, and was a tribute student of the jimao year.

Officials in Charge of Printing Examination Papers
Jin Pu, Judicial Officer in the Judicial Office of the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Wenfu. He was from Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the dingchou year.
Wu Cai, Clerk in the Registry of the Fujian Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Dayong. He was from Jianli County, Huguang, and was a National University student.

Officials in Charge of Keeping Examination Scripts
Li Yan, Salt Distribution Commissioner of the Fujian Salt Distribution Commission, had the courtesy name Bangzhi. He was registered with Yuanzhou Guard in Jiangxi, was a native of Fengcheng County, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.
Zhu Bao, Prefect of Fuzhou, had the courtesy name Ziwen. He was from Shanghai County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.

Officials in Charge of Receiving Examination Scripts
Ye Guan, Prefect of Xinghua, had the courtesy name Guoguang. He was from Jiangdu County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Gu Kejiu, Prefect of Quanzhou, had the courtesy name Yuxin. He was from Wuxi County, Zhili, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Yu Yi, Vice Prefect of Jianning, had the courtesy name Zixiu. He was from Poyang County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute student of the jiazi year.

Officials in Charge of Sealing Candidates' Identifying Information
Zou Wu, Vice Prefect of Shaowu, had the courtesy name Jingzhi. He was from Changshu County, Zhili, and was a tribute student of the jiazi year.
Chen Daxian, Prefectural Judge of Fuzhou, had the courtesy name Honggan. He was from Haiyang County, Guangdong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
Xue Zongkai, Magistrate of Jianyang County, Jianning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zixiu. He was from Jieyang County, Guangdong, and was a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:

謄錄官

漳州府長泰縣知縣方策〔載道廣西桂林衛人癸未進士〕

===

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
信近於義言可復也恭近於禮逺恥辱也
因不失其親亦可宗也
博厚所以載物也高明所以覆物也悠久
所以成物也
國君進賢如不得已將使卑踰尊疏踰戚
可不慎與
易
===
上六拘係之乃從維之王用亨于西山
王假之尚大也勿憂宜日中宜照天下也
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛
其旨逺其辭文
書
日宣三德夙夜浚明有家日嚴祗敬六德
亮采有邦翕受敷施九德咸事俊乂在
官百僚師師百工惟時撫于五辰庶績
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

信近於義，言可復也；恭近於禮，逺恥辱也；因不失其親，亦可宗也。

博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。

國君進賢如不得已，將使卑踰尊，疏踰戚，可不慎與？

易

上六，拘係之，乃從維之，王用亨于西山。

王假之，尚大也；勿憂，宜日中，宜照天下也。

歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。

其旨逺，其辭文。

書

日宣三德，夙夜浚明有家；日嚴祗敬六德，亮采有邦。翕受敷施，九德咸事，俊乂在官，百僚師師，百工惟時，撫于五辰，庶績
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

When keeping faith accords with righteousness, one's word can be fulfilled. When reverence accords with ritual propriety, disgrace and humiliation are kept at a distance. When those upon whom one relies are worthy of close association, they too may be honored as guides.

Breadth and thickness are the means by which things are borne; height and brightness are the means by which things are sheltered; enduring duration is the means by which things are brought to completion.

When the ruler of a state advances worthy men, he should do so as though compelled by necessity. Since he will be causing the lowly to rise above the exalted and the distantly related to rise above close kin, can he fail to exercise caution?

Book of Changes

Six at the top: He is seized and bound, then further tied fast. The king makes an offering at the Western Mountain.

“The king attains this” means that he esteems greatness. “Do not worry; it is fitting to be like the sun at midday” means that he should illuminate all under Heaven.

Place the remainder between the fingers to symbolize an intercalary month. There are two intercalary months in five years; therefore, place the remainder between the fingers twice before again setting aside a stalk.

Its purport is far-reaching; its language is refined.

Book of Documents

Those who daily manifest three virtues and deepen and illuminate them morning and night may possess a noble house. Those who daily attend with reverence and respect to six virtues and faithfully administer affairs may possess a state. When these virtues are embraced together and widely put into practice, and all nine virtues are employed in service, men of outstanding ability hold office. The many officials instruct one another, and all officers attend to their duties in due season, bringing them into accord with the five celestial seasons, and the many achievements …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
其凝
視遠惟明聽德惟聰
惟王受命無疆惟休亦無疆惟恤
明作有功惇大成裕
詩
是刈是濩爲絺爲綌服之無斁
鶴鳴于九臯聲聞于野魚潜在淵或在于
渚樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維蘀他山
之石可以爲錯
===
穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
天作高山大王荒之彼作矣文王康之彼
岨矣岐有夷之行子孫保之
春秋
翬帥師會齊人鄭人伐宋 宋人蔡人衛
人伐戴鄭伯伐取之 齊人鄭人入郕
〔俱隱公十年〕公及齊侯鄭伯入許〔隱公〕
〔十一年〕鄭忽出奔衛〔桓公十一年〕楚公
子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕公會晋侯宋
punctuated:
其凝。
視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。
惟王受命，無疆惟休，亦無疆惟恤。
明作有功，惇大成裕。

詩
是刈是濩，爲絺爲綌，服之無斁。
鶴鳴于九臯，聲聞于野。魚潜在淵，或在于渚。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維蘀。他山之石，可以爲錯。
穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。
天作高山，大王荒之。彼作矣，文王康之。彼岨矣，岐有夷之行，子孫保之。

春秋
翬帥師會齊人、鄭人伐宋。宋人、蔡人、衛人伐戴，鄭伯伐取之。齊人、鄭人入郕。〔俱隱公十年〕公及齊侯、鄭伯入許。〔隱公〕〔十一年〕鄭忽出奔衛。〔桓公十一年〕楚公子貞帥師伐鄭。〔襄公八年〕公會晋侯、宋
translation_en:
…are brought to completion.
To see far is true clarity of vision; to heed virtue is true acuity of hearing.
The king has received the mandate: boundless is its blessing, and boundless, too, the care it demands.
Act with discernment, and there will be merit; sincerity and magnanimity bring abundant accomplishment.

Book of Odes
They cut it and boil it, making fine and coarse hemp cloth; they wear it without tiring of it.
The crane cries in the deep marshes; its voice is heard in the open country. Fish lie hidden in the depths, or appear by the islets. Pleasant is that garden, where sandalwood trees grow, with fallen leaves beneath them. Stones from other mountains can serve as whetstones.
Reverent and august, fit to be a lord, fit to be a king.
Heaven made the lofty mountain; King Tai opened it up. He undertook the work, and King Wen brought it peace. Though its slopes were rugged, Qi had a level road. May their descendants preserve it.

Spring and Autumn Annals
Hui led an army, joining forces with men of Qi and Zheng to attack Song. Men of Song, Cai, and Wei attacked Dai; the Earl of Zheng attacked and captured them. Men of Qi and Zheng entered Cheng. 〔All in the tenth year of Duke Yin.〕 The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng, entered Xu. 〔Duke Yin,〕〔eleventh year.〕 Hu of Zheng fled to Wei. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan.〕 Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to attack Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕 The duke met with the Marquis of Jin and the Duke of Song…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
小邾子齊世子光伐鄭　楚子伐鄭〔俱襄公九年〕戌鄭虎牢〔襄公十年〕同盟于
亳城北　公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊
世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔俱襄公十一年〕叔孫
豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋向戌
衛齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭罕虎
許人曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕
===
公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男曹
伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕宋公楚子陳侯蔡
侯鄭伯許男曹伯會于盂〔僖公二十一年〕
秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
秋蒐于紅〔昭公八年〕
禮記
是故聖人作爲禮以教人使人以有禮
心中斯須不和不樂而鄙詐之心入之矣
punctuated:
公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。楚子伐鄭。〔俱襄公九年〕戌鄭虎牢。〔襄公十年〕同盟于亳城北。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔俱襄公十一年〕叔孫豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衛齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢。〔昭公元年〕

公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕宋公、楚子、陳侯、蔡侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會于盂。〔僖公二十一年〕秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕晉侯伐秦。〔文公四年〕秋，蒐于紅。〔昭公八年〕

禮記

是故聖人作爲禮以教人，使人以有禮。

心中斯須不和不樂，而鄙詐之心入之矣。
translation_en:
…the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Xiaozhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, attacked Zheng. The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Both entries: ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕 A garrison was stationed at Hulao in Zheng [?]. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕 They jointly swore a covenant north of the walls of Bo. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu in attacking Zheng; they met at Xiaoyu. 〔Both entries: eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕 Shusun Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao. 〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕

The duke met at Kuiqiu with Duke Zhou, the chief minister, the Marquis of Qi, the heir of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Duke of Song, the Viscount of Chu, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao met at Yu. 〔Twenty-first year of Duke Xi.〕 The men of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕 The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. 〔Fourth year of Duke Wen.〕 In autumn, a hunt and military review were held at Hong. 〔Eighth year of Duke Zhao.〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

Therefore the sages established rites to teach the people, so that the people would possess ritual propriety.

If the heart is without harmony and joy for even a moment, thoughts of baseness and deceit enter it.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
外貌斯須不莊不敬而易慢之心入之
矣
饗者鄉也鄉之然後能饗焉
故大臣不可不敬也是民之表也邇臣不
可不慎也是民之道也
第貳塲
論
孔子斟酌先王之禮
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
===
擬漢令禮官勸學興禮詔〔元朔五年〕
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥〔長慶三年〕
擬宋仁宗同輔臣賞花釣魚賦詩謝表〔嘉祐七年〕
判語〔五條〕
照刷文卷
荒蕪田地
朝見留難
飛報軍情
punctuated:
外貌斯須不莊不敬，而易慢之心入之矣。
饗者，鄉也；鄉之，然後能饗焉。
故大臣不可不敬也，是民之表也；邇臣不可不慎也，是民之道也。
第貳塲
論
孔子斟酌先王之禮。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學興禮詔〔元朔五年〕。
擬唐以韓愈為吏部侍郎誥〔長慶三年〕。
擬宋仁宗同輔臣賞花釣魚賦詩謝表〔嘉祐七年〕。
判語〔五條〕
照刷文卷。
荒蕪田地。
朝見留難。
飛報軍情。
translation_en:
…If one's outward bearing lacks dignity and reverence even for a moment, a disposition toward carelessness and arrogance enters in.
To offer a sacrifice (xiang) means to turn toward (xiang); only after turning toward its recipient can one make the offering.
Thus great ministers must be treated with respect, for they are exemplars for the people; attendants close to the ruler must be chosen carefully, for they guide the people.

Second Session

Discourse
Confucius's weighing and adapting the rites of the former kings.

Edicts, Patents, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty ordering the ritual officials to encourage learning and promote rites. 〔Fifth year of Yuanshuo.〕
Compose a patent in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Han Yu as Vice Minister of Personnel. 〔Third year of Changqing.〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty on the occasion of Emperor Renzong's viewing flowers, fishing, and composing poems with his chief ministers. 〔Seventh year of Jiayou.〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Reviewing official documents and files.
Farmland left uncultivated.
Obstructing attendance at a court audience.
Dispatching urgent reports of military affairs.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
聽訟廻避
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問帝王之學與韋布不同盖其富貴之極
逸欲易生宫闈之邃師保罕接故憂勤
惕厲之心往往形於箴銘圖象內外交
養動息不違其道固然湯之盤銘曰苟
日新日日新又日新武王聞太公之言
觴豆几席皆有銘焉豈以湯武之聖必
===
如是而後無過舉歟繼是而後有長夜
屏有無逸圖有連屏五十種有丹扆六
箴有書孟子于座屏有圖敬天於經幄
或以惡戒或以善勉或出於自製或取
於下獻其行業之無愧於箴規與否史
冊可稽然與湯武之心同歟否歟我
太祖高皇帝以天縱之聖繼執中之傳當兵戈
倥偬之餘即納學士宋濂之言而以大
學衍義書諸
punctuated:
聽訟廻避。

第叁場
策〔五道〕

問：帝王之學與韋布不同，盖其富貴之極，逸欲易生；宫闈之邃，師保罕接。故憂勤惕厲之心，往往形於箴銘圖象，內外交養，動息不違，其道固然。湯之盤銘曰：「苟日新，日日新，又日新。」武王聞太公之言，觴豆几席皆有銘焉。豈以湯武之聖，必如是而後無過舉歟？繼是而後，有長夜屏，有無逸圖，有連屏五十種，有丹扆六箴，有書孟子于座屏，有圖敬天於經幄。或以惡戒，或以善勉，或出於自製，或取於下獻。其行業之無愧於箴規與否，史冊可稽；然與湯武之心同歟，否歟？我太祖高皇帝以天縱之聖，繼執中之傳，當兵戈倥偬之餘，即納學士宋濂之言，而以大學衍義書諸
translation_en:
Recusal in hearing lawsuits.

Third Session
Policy Questions 〔Five questions〕

Question: The learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoners. At the height of wealth and honor, indulgence and desire readily arise; secluded within the palace, they seldom meet their preceptors and guardians. Thus their concern for diligent government and their vigilance often find expression in admonitions, inscriptions, and illustrations. These nurture them both inwardly and outwardly, so that in activity and repose they do not depart from the Way. This is indeed the proper course.

The inscription on Tang’s basin reads: “If you can renew yourself for one day, renew yourself daily, and renew yourself yet again.” After King Wu heard the words of Taigong, he had inscriptions placed on his drinking cups, food vessels, tables, and mats. Could it be that even sages such as Tang and Wu had to do this before they could avoid errors in their actions?

In subsequent times there were the Long Night Screen, the Illustration of ‘Against Idleness,’ fifty kinds of linked screens, the Six Admonitions for the Vermilion Throne Screen, passages from the Mencius written on a screen beside the imperial seat, and illustrations of reverence for Heaven in the imperial study. Some used evil as a warning; others used goodness as encouragement. Some were composed by the rulers themselves; others were selected from offerings submitted by their subjects. Whether their conduct and achievements lived up to these admonitions can be examined in the historical records. But were their intentions the same as those of Tang and Wu, or not?

Our Emperor Taizu Gao, endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom, carried on the tradition of holding fast to the Mean. Amid intervals in the press of warfare, he promptly accepted the advice of Academician Song Lian and had the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning written upon …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
殿壁盖功德過於湯武而所以矜持戒謹者
自不能已焉我
皇上繼統中興益懋
聖德然猶不自滿足復
製敬一箴註釋視聽言動心五箴以自警嘗
伏讀而歎曰大哉
王言真所謂聖不自聖無斁而亦保者矣夫千
聖一心萬古一道雖其箴規之言各有
所感而本原之地實無二致請詳陳之
===
以爲我
皇上聖學緝熈之助
問人君欲明而不察仁而不懦察則傷渾
厚之體懦則乏精明之功二者善則相
濟弊則相及也先儒謂漢唐之君有明
而不察者有仁而不懦者有明而察者
有仁而懦者有察而不明者有懦而不
仁者可指而言之與又有兼舉其長者
然與否與宋之仁宗神宗似不爲各無
punctuated:
殿壁，盖功德過於湯武，而所以矜持戒謹者，自不能已焉。我皇上繼統中興，益懋聖德，然猶不自滿足，復製敬一箴，註釋視聽言動心五箴，以自警。嘗伏讀而歎曰：「大哉，王言！真所謂聖不自聖，無斁而亦保者矣。」夫千聖一心，萬古一道，雖其箴規之言各有所感，而本原之地實無二致。請詳陳之，以爲我皇上聖學緝熈之助。

問：人君欲明而不察，仁而不懦。察則傷渾厚之體，懦則乏精明之功。二者善則相濟，弊則相及也。先儒謂漢唐之君，有明而不察者，有仁而不懦者，有明而察者，有仁而懦者，有察而不明者，有懦而不仁者，可指而言之與？又有兼舉其長者，然與否與？宋之仁宗、神宗，似不爲各無
translation_en:
…on the palace walls. His achievements and virtue indeed surpassed those of Tang and Wu, yet he could not cease exercising self-restraint and watchful caution. Our Emperor has succeeded to the imperial line and brought about a restoration, further cultivating his sagely virtue. Yet, still not content with himself, he composed the Admonition on Maintaining Reverent Unity and annotated the five admonitions on seeing, hearing, speaking, acting, and the mind, to admonish himself. Having reverently read them, I exclaimed: “Great indeed are these royal words! Truly this is what is meant by a sage who does not regard himself as a sage, who remains untiring and ever watchful.” The thousand sages share one mind, and throughout all ages there is one Way. Although their words of admonition arose from different circumstances, their underlying foundation is truly the same. Please expound this in detail, to assist our Emperor in continually illuminating his sagely learning.

Question: A ruler should be discerning without being excessively scrutinizing, and benevolent without being weak. Excessive scrutiny impairs the substance of generous magnanimity; weakness leaves one without the efficacy of clear judgment. When well exercised, these two qualities complement each other; when flawed, their defects compound each other. Earlier Confucian scholars said that among the rulers of Han and Tang, some were discerning without excessive scrutiny, some benevolent without weakness, some discerning yet excessively scrutinizing, some benevolent yet weak, some excessively scrutinizing without discernment, and some weak without benevolence. Can you identify and discuss them? Were there also rulers who combined the strengths of both qualities—is this so or not? Renzong and Shenzong of Song would seem each not to have been without…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
所長也將不得進而同之與漢儒治性
之疏以太察無斷爲戒宋儒之論君德
則又以武足之豈仁明猶不可盡與我
皇上聰明仁孝得於天性有非漢唐宋諸君所
及故
即位之初剷除積弊悉與天下更始邇者
春秋漸富勵精有加凡臣工心迹之隱微内
外軍民之利病一毫無有遁其情者可
謂明見萬里之外矣而一念休養元元
===
之意又未嘗不恫瘝乎其身所以衍我
國家億萬載無疆之休者固並行而不悖矣
但不知臣子愛君無已之心亦尚有可
爲
聖德萬一之助者與不然則尚德緩刑之疏求
治太急之言皆見於勵精之朝者顧
今日獨可少與有若人之忠者遂明言之無
諱
問帝王成德致治必資諫臣周官三百六
punctuated:
所長也，將不得進而同之與？漢儒治性之疏，以太察無斷爲戒；宋儒之論君德，則又以武足之。豈仁明猶不可盡與？我皇上聰明仁孝，得於天性，有非漢唐宋諸君所及。故即位之初，剷除積弊，悉與天下更始。邇者春秋漸富，勵精有加，凡臣工心迹之隱微、内外軍民之利病，一毫無有遁其情者，可謂明見萬里之外矣。而一念休養元元之意，又未嘗不恫瘝乎其身。所以衍我國家億萬載無疆之休者，固並行而不悖矣。但不知臣子愛君無已之心，亦尚有可爲聖德萬一之助者與？不然，則尚德緩刑之疏、求治太急之言，皆見於勵精之朝者，顧今日獨可少與？有若人之忠者，遂明言之，無諱。
問：帝王成德致治，必資諫臣。《周官》三百六
translation_en:
…their respective strengths. Could they not, then, be advanced to the same rank? A Han Confucian’s memorial on cultivating one’s nature warned against excessive scrutiny and indecision; a Song Confucian’s discussion of the ruler’s virtues further supplemented them with martial resolve. Could benevolence and discernment still fail to encompass everything?
Our Emperor’s intelligence, benevolence, and filial devotion are innate, surpassing what the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song could attain. Thus, at the beginning of his reign, he eradicated accumulated abuses and made a fresh start together with all under Heaven. Recently, as he has matured, his dedication to government has increased. Whether the hidden subtleties of his officials’ motives and conduct or the benefits and hardships affecting soldiers and civilians within and beyond the capital, not the slightest detail escapes his understanding. Truly, his discernment reaches ten thousand li away. Yet in his constant concern to let the common people rest and recuperate, he has never ceased to feel their suffering as his own. These qualities, through which he extends our dynasty’s boundless blessings for countless ages, assuredly operate together without conflict.
But we wonder whether his servants’ unceasing love for their sovereign might still contribute even the smallest measure to his sagely virtue. Otherwise, memorials urging the elevation of virtue and the mitigation of punishments, and statements warning against excessive haste in seeking good government, have all appeared under rulers diligently applying themselves to government. Can such counsel alone be dispensed with today? Let anyone possessing loyalty like theirs speak plainly, withholding nothing.
Question: For emperors and kings to perfect their virtue and bring about good government, they must rely on remonstrating officials. In the Offices of Zhou, the three hundred and six…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
十屬分職聯事可謂纖悉而諫諍一職
獨缺而不設其故何歟或謂師氏掌以
媺詔王保氏掌諫王惡即其職也周之
聽諫若是其不廣歟後世有諫議大夫
有補闕有拾遺有司諫有正言起於何
時然自漢唐以諫官限天下之言上之
人既選擇柔脆易制者以供任使而憤
時感事思一建明於時者亦且拘攣職
業顧瞻忌諱而不敢輕舉剛正聞於天
===
下者以范仲淹爲相而猶不欲使爲諫
官杜牧憤藩鎮之變以身非諫官而作
罪言使三代之法尚存其弊何至於是
致堂胡氏嘗謂諫官不必設而歐陽脩
司馬光又深言諫官有益於天下豈各
有所見歟夫論聽諫之道莫善於賈山
陸贄論進諫之道莫善於程子蘇洵諸
士懷忠負直以思上助
天子之聖久矣於數子之言必有取焉其折衷
punctuated: 十屬分職聯事，可謂纖悉，而諫諍一職獨缺而不設，其故何歟？或謂師氏掌以媺詔王，保氏掌諫王惡，即其職也。周之聽諫，若是其不廣歟？後世有諫議大夫，有補闕，有拾遺，有司諫，有正言，起於何時？然自漢唐，以諫官限天下之言，上之人既選擇柔脆易制者以供任使，而憤時感事、思一建明於時者，亦且拘攣職業，顧瞻忌諱，而不敢輕舉。剛正聞於天下者，以范仲淹爲相，而猶不欲使爲諫官。杜牧憤藩鎮之變，以身非諫官而作《罪言》。使三代之法尚存，其弊何至於是？致堂胡氏嘗謂諫官不必設，而歐陽脩、司馬光又深言諫官有益於天下，豈各有所見歟？夫論聽諫之道，莫善於賈山、陸贄；論進諫之道，莫善於程子、蘇洵。諸士懷忠負直，以思上助天子之聖久矣，於數子之言必有取焉，其折衷
translation_en:
…offices apportioned duties and coordinated their work: the arrangements may be called meticulous. Yet the office of remonstrance alone was absent and never established. Why was this? Some say that the Preceptor was charged with instructing the king in what was good, and the Protector with remonstrating against the king’s faults, and that these were precisely the duties in question. Was the Zhou’s reception of remonstrance so restricted? In later ages there were Grand Masters of Remonstrance, Rectifiers of Omissions, Reminders, Directors of Remonstrance, and Remonstrators. When did these offices originate?

Yet from the Han and Tang onward, the appointment of remonstrance officials confined the expression of opinion throughout the realm to those offices. Those above selected pliant, weak men, easy to control, to carry out their commands; meanwhile, those indignant at the times and moved by events, who wished to put forward some illuminating proposal, were also constrained by their official duties. Looking anxiously about them and fearing taboos, they dared not act readily. Even Fan Zhongyan, renowned throughout the realm for firmness and integrity, was considered fit to serve as chief councilor, yet was still not wanted as a remonstrance official [?]. Du Mu, indignant at the upheavals caused by the regional military commands, wrote Words of Self-Reproach because he himself was not a remonstrance official. Had the institutions of the Three Dynasties survived, how could these abuses have reached such a point?

Hu of Zhitang once said that remonstrance officials need not be established, whereas Ouyang Xiu and Sima Guang argued emphatically that such officials benefited the realm. Did each perhaps perceive a different aspect of the matter? In discussing the proper way to receive remonstrance, none surpassed Jia Shan and Lu Zhi; in discussing the proper way to offer remonstrance, none surpassed Master Cheng and Su Xun. You candidates have long cherished loyalty and upheld integrity, hoping thereby to assist the sagely virtue of the Son of Heaven. Surely you have found something worth adopting in the words of these thinkers. Weigh and reconcile their views…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之以告我
問知人之難古今通患人君深居九重之
中聚天下之人材而奔走任使之雖嚴
之以選舉精之以考課而人之賢不肖
常眩於名實之間豈勢之所拘法不能
及抑教之無素士無定習變化遷就而
不可辯察歟李克告魏文侯之卜相莊
子之九徵蘇軾之論觀過知仁皆所謂
巧於觀人者人君欲用其術以求天下
===
之才力固有所不能而吾獨以為盡符
其術豪傑之士未必出此而犯之者或
亦未可盡棄也可舉一二以破其術歟
惟朱子本易理以推陽明陰暗之說真
所以窺英俊之心術燭奸邪之肝膽不
知選舉考課之際亦可以兼用其術否
歟先儒有言曰人之才性與時升降又
曰漢武好英風故其時富瓌詭立名之
士漢宣精吏治故其時萃循良核實之
punctuated:
之以告我。

問：知人之難，古今通患。人君深居九重之中，聚天下之人材而奔走任使之。雖嚴之以選舉，精之以考課，而人之賢不肖常眩於名實之間，豈勢之所拘，法不能及？抑教之無素，士無定習，變化遷就而不可辯察歟？李克告魏文侯之卜相、莊子之九徵、蘇軾之論觀過知仁，皆所謂巧於觀人者。人君欲用其術以求天下之才，力固有所不能。而吾獨以為，盡符其術，豪傑之士未必出此，而犯之者或亦未可盡棄也。可舉一二以破其術歟？惟朱子本易理以推陽明陰暗之說，真所以窺英俊之心術，燭奸邪之肝膽。不知選舉考課之際，亦可以兼用其術否歟？先儒有言曰：「人之才性與時升降。」又曰：「漢武好英風，故其時富瓌詭立名之士；漢宣精吏治，故其時萃循良核實之
translation_en:
…weigh these views against one another and tell me your conclusions.

Question: The difficulty of judging people has been a common concern in ancient and modern times. The ruler dwells deep within the ninefold palace precincts, assembling the talented men of the realm and employing them to carry out his commands. Although he makes recruitment rigorous and performance evaluations exacting, judgments of men's worthiness or unworthiness are constantly confused by the discrepancy between reputation and reality. Is this because circumstances impose constraints beyond the reach of regulations? Or is it because instruction has lacked a firm foundation, so that scholars have no settled habits, changing and accommodating themselves in ways that make them impossible to distinguish and assess?

Li Ke's advice to Marquis Wen of Wei on choosing a chief minister, Zhuangzi's nine tests, and Su Shi's discussion of discerning benevolence by observing faults are all instances of what is called skill in judging people. If the ruler wishes to employ their methods to seek out the realm's talent, there are certainly limits to what he can accomplish. Yet I, for my part, believe that outstanding men will not necessarily be found among those who satisfy all their criteria, while those who violate them perhaps cannot all be discarded either. Can you cite one or two examples to refute these methods?

Master Zhu alone, drawing on the principles of the Book of Changes, developed the explanation of yang as bright and yin as dark. This truly provides a means of discerning the intentions of outstanding men and illuminating the innermost thoughts of the treacherous. Might his method also be employed alongside recruitment and performance evaluations?

An earlier Confucian scholar said: “People's abilities and dispositions rise and fall with the times.” He also said: “Emperor Wu of Han prized a heroic spirit, and thus his age abounded in men who established their reputations through extraordinary qualities; Emperor Xuan of Han was exacting in the administration of officials, and thus his age gathered together those of conscientious and benevolent conduct who verified actual results…”

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
能夫士亦係乎上之所以倡率化導而
已耳而亦有不盡然者此人材之所以
難知也夫欲選不失才用不失實是必
有說矣何以釋主司之疑
問周禮一書周公致太平之迹也其羽毛
鱗介壺𧔥貍蠧鼃黽之類不暇悉舉試以其
大者與諸生講之自井牧始於黃而九
夫經野之制備弼服昉於堯而九畿分
國之制詳典刑淑於舜而五刑麗民之
===
制具先儒謂此三者道之所以行也不
知果各自爲用而不相通與抑其中亦
有相待而行者與秦廢井田開阡陌罷
侯置守漢倂肉刑除之願治之君以爲
不復此欲行周公之道不可得也然與
否與議復井田封建者或曰處之有術
或曰可以支變故而蘇洵葉適柳宗元
所論又往往盡利害之實至於肉刑則
陳羣議復之於漢劉頌議復之於晉而
punctuated:
能。夫士亦係乎上之所以倡率化導而已耳，而亦有不盡然者，此人材之所以難知也。夫欲選不失才，用不失實，是必有說矣。何以釋主司之疑？
問：周禮一書，周公致太平之迹也。其羽毛鱗介、壺𧔥、貍蠧、鼃黽之類，不暇悉舉，試以其大者與諸生講之。自井牧始於黃，而九夫經野之制備；弼服昉於堯，而九畿分國之制詳；典刑淑於舜，而五刑麗民之制具。先儒謂此三者，道之所以行也。不知果各自爲用而不相通與？抑其中亦有相待而行者與？秦廢井田，開阡陌，罷侯置守，漢倂肉刑除之。願治之君以爲不復此，欲行周公之道不可得也。然與否與？議復井田、封建者，或曰處之有術，或曰可以支變故，而蘇洵、葉適、柳宗元所論，又往往盡利害之實。至於肉刑，則陳羣議復之於漢，劉頌議復之於晉，而
translation_en:
…men of ability. Scholars, then, depend merely upon how those above lead, transform, and guide them. Yet there are also cases in which this is not entirely so; this is why human talent is difficult to discern. If we wish to select men without overlooking talent and employ them without mistaking their actual abilities, there must surely be an explanation. How would you resolve the doubts of those presiding over the examination?
Question: The Rites of Zhou records how the Duke of Zhou brought about supreme peace. There is no time to enumerate all its provisions concerning feathered, furred, scaled, and shelled creatures, the offices concerned with vessels and harmful creatures [?], burrowing pests, frogs, and the like. Let us instead discuss its major institutions with you candidates. The division of land into fields and pastures began with the Yellow Emperor, and the system for laying out the countryside in units of nine households became complete. The service zones [?] originated with Yao, and the system of dividing the realm into nine zones became fully articulated. The canonical punishments were perfected under Shun [?], and the system of applying the five punishments to the people became complete. Earlier Confucian scholars said that these three were the means by which the Way was put into practice. Did they indeed each serve their own purpose without being interconnected? Or were there also ways in which their operation depended upon one another? Qin abolished the well-field system, opened up field boundaries, abolished the feudal lords, and appointed commandery governors; Han also abolished the mutilating punishments. Rulers aspiring to good government have held that, without restoring these institutions, it would be impossible to put the Duke of Zhou’s Way into practice. Is this so or not? Among those discussing the restoration of the well-field system and feudal enfeoffment, some say there are methods for implementing them, while others say they can help withstand upheavals. Moreover, the discussions of Su Xun, Ye Shi, and Liu Zongyuan frequently give a thorough account of their actual advantages and disadvantages. As for mutilating punishments, Chen Qun proposed restoring them under the Han, and Liu Song proposed restoring them under the Jin, but…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
卒皆不果其是非可否將安所折衷與
後世固有欲限民名田者有均田者有
口分世業者有懲秦孤立大封同姓者
有封建子弟爲王而置三軍者有蠲除
前代之法而更定五刑者其亦聖人之
意與我
朝致治之隆非漢唐所及而三者之制不盡
如古豈周公之法卒不可復於後世將
遂不復其亦足以致治與然今之天下
===
民日益貧吏日益肆獄訟日益煩此其
故何也先王之治固别有其說與尚酌
古準今爲我言之無徒老生之常談云
爾也
punctuated: 卒皆不果，其是非可否，將安所折衷與？後世固有欲限民名田者，有均田者，有口分世業者，有懲秦孤立、大封同姓者，有封建子弟爲王而置三軍者，有蠲除前代之法而更定五刑者，其亦聖人之意與？我朝致治之隆，非漢唐所及，而三者之制不盡如古，豈周公之法卒不可復於後世？將遂不復，其亦足以致治與？然今之天下，民日益貧，吏日益肆，獄訟日益煩，此其故何也？先王之治固别有其說與？尚酌古準今，爲我言之，無徒老生之常談云爾也。
translation_en: …yet in the end none of these proposals was carried out. By what standard, then, should their merits and faults, their feasibility or otherwise, be adjudicated? In later ages, there were indeed those who wished to limit the land registered in private hands; those who instituted equal-field allocation; those who established per-capita allotments and hereditary holdings; those who, taking warning from the isolation of the Qin ruling house, extensively enfeoffed members of the imperial clan; those who enfeoffed sons and younger brothers as princes and established three armies; and those who abolished the preceding dynasty’s laws and revised the Five Punishments. Did these measures also accord with the intentions of the sages? The excellence of the order achieved by our dynasty surpasses anything attained by the Han or Tang, yet its arrangements for these three institutions do not entirely follow antiquity. Could it be that the Duke of Zhou’s institutions ultimately cannot be restored in later ages? Or, even if they remain unrestored, can good order still be achieved? Yet throughout the realm today, the people grow poorer by the day, officials grow increasingly unrestrained, and criminal cases and lawsuits become ever more numerous. What accounts for this? Is there indeed some other explanation of the government of the former kings? Weigh antiquity against present circumstances and explain this to us. Do not merely offer the stale commonplaces of old scholars.

text:
第壹場
四書
信近於義言可復也恭近於禮遠恥辱也
因不失其親亦可宗也
莊用賓
同考試官教諭潘批認理真切造語不凡
非苟作者
同考試官教授彭批止就題目上發揮筆
力自別復古之作也
===
考試官主事江批語意峻潔
考試官署員外郎陸批莊厚可錄
隨事而豫為之所則其悔亡矣蓋動而有悔者
以其弗豫也君子之言行交際可不慎與有子
示人之意如此今夫義者宜也約信而不合其
宜勿利有攸往矣苟慮之於心而宣之於口慨
然以事相許者必協諸義而協也則義之所向
行莫利焉反而求之無所於疑直而從之無所
於窒也行可以顧其言矣有諾責乎哉然則君
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

信近於義，言可復也；恭近於禮，遠恥辱也；因不失其親，亦可宗也。

莊用賓

同考試官教諭潘批：認理真切，造語不凡，非苟作者。

同考試官教授彭批：止就題目上發揮，筆力自別，復古之作也。

考試官主事江批：語意峻潔。

考試官署員外郎陸批：莊厚可錄。

隨事而豫為之所，則其悔亡矣。蓋動而有悔者，以其弗豫也。君子之言行交際，可不慎與？有子示人之意如此。今夫義者，宜也。約信而不合其宜，勿利有攸往矣。苟慮之於心而宣之於口，慨然以事相許者，必協諸義，而協也，則義之所向，行莫利焉。反而求之，無所於疑；直而從之，無所於窒也。行可以顧其言矣，有諾責乎哉？然則君
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When good faith accords with righteousness, one's word can be fulfilled. When reverence accords with ritual propriety, shame and disgrace are kept at a distance. When those on whom one relies are suitable objects of close attachment, they too may be taken as guides.”

Zhuang Yongbin

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: “His grasp of principle is precise and penetrating; his phrasing is exceptional. This is no carelessly composed work.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Professor: “He develops his argument solely from the examination topic itself, yet the strength of his writing is distinctive. This is a work that restores the ancient manner.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: “The language and thought are rigorous and clear.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: “Dignified and substantial; worthy of selection.”

If one makes suitable provision beforehand for each affair, regret will disappear. For those whose actions bring regret suffer this because they have not made provision beforehand. Can a gentleman fail to exercise care in his words, actions, and dealings with others? Such is the intention of Master You's instruction.

Now righteousness means appropriateness. If one pledges one's word without conforming to what is appropriate, no undertaking will be advantageous. If, having considered something in one's heart and expressed it aloud, one generously promises another to do it, one must bring that promise into accord with righteousness. Once it accords, nothing is more advantageous in action than proceeding where righteousness leads. Turning inward to examine it, one finds nothing doubtful; following it directly, one encounters no obstruction. One's actions can thus answer to one's words. How could one be reproached for an unfulfilled promise? Thus the gentleman…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
子寧有巳怨也禮以謹節文也致恭而不中其
節謙而靡光矣苟上交不諂而下交不瀆翼然
以敬相先者盖周旋而中禮也則嘉之所會亨
孰大焉以内焉固不至於失巳以外焉固不至
於失人也允維德之基矣何耻辱乎不然必徇
人以非禮之恭者也非其人也將惟恐迹之不
去巳誰能因之因之不可欲宗之也難矣苟考
衷度物雖邂逅之相依者不失其可親之人焉
則比其人也遂主其家恃爲緩急可也遂尊其
===
德樹之表儀可也因之也固宗之也巳不然則
比之匪人不亦傷乎有子之言辭不迫而意獨
至君子察於此則可與研幾矣抑三者之中莫
不有幾幾者理之先見也吉凶悔吝誰則違之
卒於悔焉凡不明乎理而巳其理明則其幾察
其幾察則樞機之發毫釐不差千里之謬無從
始也羔羊之節冀寔辟之蔡京之薦龜山不得
而與焉往往以豪傑之才而付之知者之一惜
可謂無其故乎
punctuated: 子寧有巳怨也？禮以謹節文也，致恭而不中其節，謙而靡光矣。苟上交不諂而下交不瀆，翼然以敬相先者，盖周旋而中禮也。則嘉之所會，亨孰大焉？以内焉，固不至於失巳；以外焉，固不至於失人也。允維德之基矣，何耻辱乎？不然，必徇人以非禮之恭者也。非其人也，將惟恐迹之不去巳，誰能因之？因之不可，欲宗之也難矣。苟考衷度物，雖邂逅之相依者，不失其可親之人焉，則比其人也，遂主其家，恃爲緩急可也；遂尊其德，樹之表儀可也。因之也，固宗之也巳。不然，則比之匪人，不亦傷乎？有子之言，辭不迫而意獨至。君子察於此，則可與研幾矣。抑三者之中，莫不有幾。幾者，理之先見也。吉凶悔吝，誰則違之？卒於悔焉，凡不明乎理而巳。其理明，則其幾察；其幾察，則樞機之發，毫釐不差，千里之謬無從始也。羔羊之節，冀寔辟之；蔡京之薦，龜山不得而與焉。往往以豪傑之才，而付之知者之一惜，可謂無其故乎？
translation_en: …could the gentleman then have cause to reproach himself? Ritual serves to regulate the proper measures and forms of conduct. If one shows deference without observing its proper measure, one’s humility lacks lustre. If, in dealings with superiors, one does not flatter, and in dealings with inferiors, one is not disrespectful, but stands reverently and takes the lead in showing respect, one’s conduct accords with ritual. When admirable qualities thus come together, what greater flourishing could there be? Inwardly, one certainly does not compromise oneself; outwardly, one certainly does not fail others. This is truly the foundation of virtue. What shame or disgrace could there be? Otherwise, one must be accommodating others with deference contrary to ritual. If the person is unsuitable, one will only fear that the traces of the association cannot be removed from oneself. Who could rely upon such a person? If one cannot rely upon him, it is difficult indeed to wish to honour him as a guiding figure. If one examines one’s inner intentions and weighs external circumstances, ensuring that even those with whom one forms a chance association are people fit to be held close, then, having allied oneself with such a person, one may become a guest of his household and rely upon him in times of need; one may also honour his virtue and establish him as an exemplar. To rely upon him is indeed also to honour him as a guiding figure. Otherwise, to ally oneself with an unworthy person—is this not harmful? Master You’s words are unhurried, yet their meaning reaches exceptionally far. A gentleman who examines this may be engaged in investigating the first subtle indications of things. Indeed, each of these three matters contains such indications. These are the earliest manifestations of principle. Good fortune, ill fortune, regret, and humiliation—who can escape them? To end in regret is simply to have failed to understand principle. When principle is understood, its first indications are discerned; when these are discerned, the release of the pivotal mechanism deviates not even by a hair’s breadth, and an error extending a thousand li has no opportunity to begin. The integrity of ‘The Lamb,’ and Ji’s actually summoning him [?]; Cai Jing’s recommendation of Guishan—these could not meet this standard [?]. So often, people of outstanding talent become an occasion for regret among the discerning. Can this be said to happen without a reason?

text:
博厚所以載物也高明所以覆物也悠久
所以成物也
劉汝楠
同考試官訓導霍批揭書出題不意塲中

式矣
同考試官教諭李批中庸義是形容至誠
功業最難下筆立意純潔措詞莊重無踰此篇
===
考試官主事江批發明博厚高明悠久甚
眞切
考試官署員外郎陸批語意精確
至誠之大業一天地之造化乎物焉夫天地盡
萬物而造化之者乎大業之出於至誠其用夫
豈有異乎哉中庸發明天道之意如此謂夫至
誠之德旣驗於外則其用之所及者何如也蓋
有悠遠以為之端其積自有不能已者故澤之
所被與恩之所漸汪洋透徹而莫測其涯涘所
punctuated:
博厚所以載物也，高明所以覆物也，悠久所以成物也。
劉汝楠
同考試官訓導霍批：揭書出題，不意塲中士子盡為所窘。間有一二畧加發揮，率陳爛可厭。獨此作體認親切，不作尋常捕風捉影語，可以為式矣。
同考試官教諭李批：中庸義是形容至誠功業，最難下筆。立意純潔，措詞莊重，無踰此篇。
考試官主事江批：發明博厚、高明、悠久，甚眞切。
考試官署員外郎陸批：語意精確。
至誠之大業，一天地之造化乎物焉。夫天地，盡萬物而造化之者乎？大業之出於至誠，其用夫豈有異乎哉？中庸發明天道之意如此，謂夫至誠之德旣驗於外，則其用之所及者何如也？蓋有悠遠以為之端，其積自有不能已者。故澤之所被與恩之所漸，汪洋透徹而莫測其涯涘，所
translation_en:
“Breadth and depth are what sustain things; height and brightness are what cover things; enduring constancy is what brings things to completion.”
Liu Runan
Comment by Associate Examiner Huo, Assistant Instructor: Upon opening the book to select the topic, I did not expect all the candidates in the examination compound to be stymied by it. Here and there, one or two developed its meaning a little, but their work was generally stale and tiresome. This composition alone shows an intimate grasp of the subject, without the usual language of chasing the wind and clutching at shadows. It can serve as a model.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The meaning of this passage from the Doctrine of the Mean describes the achievements of utmost sincerity and is exceedingly difficult to write about. For purity of conception and dignity of expression, no essay surpasses this one.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: Its elucidation of breadth and depth, height and brightness, and enduring constancy is most true and apt.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: Its language and meaning are precise.
The great achievement of utmost sincerity is at one with Heaven and Earth’s creative transformation of things [?]. Is it not Heaven and Earth that create and transform all the myriad things? How could the operation of the great achievement proceeding from utmost sincerity be any different? Such is the intent with which the Doctrine of the Mean elucidates the Way of Heaven. It asks: once the virtue of utmost sincerity has manifested itself outwardly, how far does its operation extend? With far-reaching duration as its beginning, its accumulation naturally cannot cease. Thus, wherever its beneficence reaches and its kindness permeates, it is vast and penetrating, its bounds unfathomable, whereby …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
以合天下之物而盡載之蓋博則容之無外厚
則綏之不窮負荷之功極地道之所至而物之
於至誠亦倚之如地以自遂于博厚之中矣有
博厚以為之基其發又有不可遏者故勢之所
就與精之所達峻極昭融而不涉於卑陋所以
合天下之物而盡覆之蓋高則所包者廣明則
所照者遠帲冒之化窮天體之所際而物之於
至誠亦仰之如天以自安于高明之下矣然博
厚高明根之於純一發之為日新有優裕永遠
===
之氣象又所以成乎物焉負荷之不息而無一
物之不遂其願帲冒之不間而無一物之或失
其所蓋地以形成乎所載天以氣成乎所覆至
誠以化成乎所治凡天下之物咸安生全性于
悠久之際矣是則物之覆載與成本於天地亦
本於至誠觀物而至誠之功用大矣嗟乎天地
不誠無以運造化聖人不誠無以成治功其本
同也不然聖人亦天地間之一物覆且載於其
中矣故求天地之誠而全之者所以希聖也其
punctuated: 以合天下之物而盡載之。蓋博則容之無外，厚則綏之不窮，負荷之功極地道之所至，而物之於至誠，亦倚之如地，以自遂于博厚之中矣。有博厚以為之基，其發又有不可遏者，故勢之所就與精之所達，峻極昭融而不涉於卑陋，所以合天下之物而盡覆之。蓋高則所包者廣，明則所照者遠，帲冒之化窮天體之所際，而物之於至誠，亦仰之如天，以自安于高明之下矣。然博厚高明，根之於純一，發之為日新，有優裕永遠之氣象，又所以成乎物焉。負荷之不息，而無一物之不遂其願；帲冒之不間，而無一物之或失其所。蓋地以形成乎所載，天以氣成乎所覆，至誠以化成乎所治，凡天下之物，咸安生全性于悠久之際矣。是則物之覆載與成，本於天地，亦本於至誠。觀物而至誠之功用大矣。嗟乎！天地不誠，無以運造化；聖人不誠，無以成治功，其本同也。不然，聖人亦天地間之一物，覆且載於其中矣。故求天地之誠而全之者，所以希聖也。其
translation_en: …thereby encompassing all things under Heaven and bearing them all. Breadth embraces everything without exception; thickness sustains them without limit. Its work of bearing and supporting reaches the utmost extent of the Way of Earth. Things likewise depend upon utmost sincerity as upon Earth, fulfilling themselves within its breadth and thickness. With breadth and thickness as its foundation, its manifestation is also irresistible. Thus, wherever its force extends and its essential vitality reaches, it is supremely lofty, radiant, and all-pervading, untouched by baseness or narrowness; it thereby encompasses all things under Heaven and shelters them all. Height makes its embrace broad; brightness makes its illumination far-reaching. Its transforming influence shelters all that lies within Heaven’s compass. Things likewise look up to utmost sincerity as to Heaven, finding security beneath its height and brightness. Yet breadth, thickness, height, and brightness are rooted in undivided purity and manifest themselves in daily renewal. They possess an aspect of abundance and everlasting duration, and thereby also bring things to completion. Its bearing and supporting never cease, so that not a single thing fails to attain its desire; its sheltering is uninterrupted, so that not a single thing ever loses its proper place. Earth, through its physical form, brings to completion what it bears; Heaven, through its vital energy, brings to completion what it shelters; utmost sincerity, through transformation, brings to completion what it governs. All things under Heaven thus live securely and fulfill their natures amid its enduring constancy. Thus the sheltering, bearing, and completion of things are rooted in Heaven and Earth, and also in utmost sincerity. When we consider things, how great are the workings of utmost sincerity! Alas! Without sincerity, Heaven and Earth could not set creation and transformation in motion; without sincerity, the sage could not accomplish the work of governance. Their foundation is the same. Otherwise, the sage too would be merely one thing among Heaven and Earth, sheltered and borne within them. Therefore, seeking the sincerity of Heaven and Earth and realizing it fully is the means of aspiring to sagehood. Its…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
功用特餘事焉耳法天地之用以擬聖者妄也
伯之所以小補也知天地則知聖人知聖人則
知伯道之不足爲矣
國君進賢如不得已將使卑踰尊疏踰戚
可不慎與
黃謹容
同考試官訓導陳批踰尊踰戚是說後來
之弊讀齊王孟子問答詞氣其意自見錄此不獨
取其文之工耳
===
同考試官教諭舒批不得已是形容致謹
士子多取下文入講非是作文須理會聖賢口氣
吾以此有取於子
考試官主事江批婉曲有味
考試官署員外郎陸批孟子告齊王意是如此
論人君用人之致謹以其所係者大而不可不
謹焉蓋用人不當其弊必至於易尊親之常矣
所係之大如此而可不逆致其謹乎孟子告齊
宣王之意若曰用人而悔之於後者正以不能
punctuated:
功用特餘事焉耳。法天地之用以擬聖者，妄也，伯之所以小補也。知天地則知聖人，知聖人則知伯道之不足爲矣。
「國君進賢，如不得已，將使卑踰尊，疏踰戚，可不慎與？」
黃謹容
同考試官訓導陳批：踰尊踰戚，是說後來之弊。讀齊王孟子問答詞氣，其意自見。錄此，不獨取其文之工耳。
同考試官教諭舒批：不得已，是形容致謹。士子多取下文入講，非是。作文須理會聖賢口氣，吾以此有取於子。
考試官主事江批：婉曲有味。
考試官署員外郎陸批：孟子告齊王意是如此。
論人君用人之致謹，以其所係者大而不可不謹焉。蓋用人不當，其弊必至於易尊親之常矣。所係之大如此，而可不逆致其謹乎？孟子告齊宣王之意若曰：用人而悔之於後者，正以不能
translation_en:
…Its efficacy is merely a secondary matter. To imitate the operations of Heaven and Earth and thereby aspire to sagehood is misguided; this is why a hegemon can make only a small contribution. To understand Heaven and Earth is to understand the sage; to understand the sage is to understand that the hegemon’s way is unworthy of pursuit.
“When the ruler of a state advances worthy men, he should do so as though compelled by necessity. He will be making the lowly surpass the exalted and the distantly related surpass close kin: can he fail to be cautious?”
Huang Jinrong
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: “‘Surpass the exalted’ and ‘surpass close kin’ refer to the abuses that follow later. Read the wording and tone of the questions and answers between the King of Qi and Mencius, and the meaning becomes apparent. This piece is included not merely for its literary skill.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor: “‘Compelled by necessity’ describes the exercise of utmost caution. Candidates often bring the ensuing passage into their exposition; this is incorrect. In composing an essay, one must grasp the tone of the sages and worthies. It is for this that I commend you.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: “Subtle and nuanced, with a lingering savor.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: “This is indeed what Mencius meant in advising the King of Qi.”
The ruler’s utmost caution in employing men is discussed because so much depends upon it that he cannot fail to be cautious. For if men are employed improperly, the resulting abuses will inevitably overturn the established order of rank and kinship. When the consequences are so great, can he fail to exercise the utmost caution in advance? The intent of Mencius’s advice to King Xuan of Qi was as if to say: Those who employ men and afterward regret it do so precisely because they were unable to…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
慎之於初也吾觀國君懸爵祿以待豪傑必詳
審於明揚之時可以用可以無用若事之迫於
前而勉爲之者焉虛名位以擢賢俊必遲疑於
遴選之際可以任可以無任若勢之迫於身而
強圖之者焉是何也用之者所以尊之也而尊
非其人於理不得不復選卑賤而有才者以踰
之非故踰也才不足以稱其尊君亦不得而庇
之也任之者所以戚之也而戚非其人其勢不
得不更求疏遠而有德者以踰之非故踰也德
===
不足以當其戚君亦不得而昵之也夫尊卑有
常國之體統存焉一舉措而輒易其尊卑雖人
之才與不才皆足以當之於體統亦甚褻矣此
其所係豈特一人之舉措而可不逆爲之慮哉
親疏有等國之名分在焉一用舍而卽更其親
疏雖人之德與不德各有以致之於名分亦甚
瀆矣此其所關豈特一時之用舍而可不預爲
之圖哉夫王於臣之不才者固不暇惜而倂其
尊戚之禮輕之可乎禮重而用才無不當矣嘗
punctuated: 慎之於初也。吾觀國君懸爵祿以待豪傑，必詳審於明揚之時，可以用，可以無用，若事之迫於前而勉爲之者焉。虛名位以擢賢俊，必遲疑於遴選之際，可以任，可以無任，若勢之迫於身而強圖之者焉。是何也？用之者，所以尊之也；而尊非其人，於理不得不復選卑賤而有才者以踰之。非故踰也，才不足以稱其尊，君亦不得而庇之也。任之者，所以戚之也；而戚非其人，其勢不得不更求疏遠而有德者以踰之。非故踰也，德不足以當其戚，君亦不得而昵之也。夫尊卑有常，國之體統存焉。一舉措而輒易其尊卑，雖人之才與不才皆足以當之，於體統亦甚褻矣。此其所係，豈特一人之舉措，而可不逆爲之慮哉？親疏有等，國之名分在焉。一用舍而卽更其親疏，雖人之德與不德各有以致之，於名分亦甚瀆矣。此其所關，豈特一時之用舍，而可不預爲之圖哉？夫王於臣之不才者，固不暇惜，而倂其尊戚之禮輕之，可乎？禮重而用才無不當矣。嘗
translation_en:
…exercise care at the outset. I observe that when a ruler holds out ranks and emoluments to attract outstanding men, he must scrutinize them carefully when bringing their merits to light and promoting them. Where a man might either be employed or left unemployed, the ruler should act as though circumstances pressing upon him had compelled him to do so reluctantly. When he leaves titles and positions vacant in order to advance worthy and talented men, he must pause and deliberate at the moment of selection. Where a man might either be appointed or left unappointed, the ruler should proceed as though circumstances bearing upon him had forced him to undertake it. Why is this? To employ a man is to accord him honor. If the man honored is unsuitable, reason dictates that the ruler must select someone of lowly standing who possesses talent and raise him above the former appointee. This is not a deliberate wish to supersede him: his talent is insufficient to match his honored position, and the ruler cannot shield him. To entrust a man with office is to bring him close. If the man brought close is unsuitable, circumstances dictate that the ruler must seek someone distant from him who possesses virtue and raise him above the former appointee. This is not a deliberate wish to supersede him: his virtue is insufficient to warrant such closeness, and the ruler cannot continue to favor him.
High and low standing have their established order, in which the dignity and hierarchy of the state reside. If every appointment or dismissal changes these standings, then even though the talent or lack of talent of the men concerned fully warrants the change, the dignity of that hierarchy is gravely diminished. Can the implications concern merely the appointment or dismissal of a single man, such that one need not consider them beforehand? Closeness and distance have their gradations, in which the state's distinctions of status and duty reside. If every decision to employ or dismiss someone immediately changes these relations, then even though the virtue or lack of virtue of the men concerned has brought about the respective results, those distinctions are gravely profaned. Can the implications concern merely a single occasion of employment or dismissal, such that one need not plan for them in advance? Certainly, a king has no leisure to spare concern for untalented ministers; but may he also treat lightly the rites governing the honor and closeness accorded to them? When ritual propriety is taken seriously, talent will always be employed fittingly. I have formerly…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
觀高宗之用傅說文王之用呂望其始也盡舉
平日所尊且戚者而踰之至於用之旣久舉天
下之卑且疎者又莫能踰焉人皆曰信之篤也
任之專也不知傅說呂望之賢實致之而高宗
文王之愼又先之矣不然以商周之時而何夢
卜之晩乎然則進賢而不法二聖吾未見其爲
不得已也
易
王假之尚大也勿憂宜日中宜照天下也
===
陳鍾
同考試官教諭潘批發揮聖人戒盛之意
明白透徹予可謂憂治世而危明主者
同考試官教授彭批理到之言憂深思遠
讀之令人有警省處
考試官主事江批鳴盛識幾非苟作者
考試官署員外郎陸批講尚大宜照處他卷不及
彖傳釋豐之辭本其有恃治之心著其得守治
之道夫治不可恃恃則可憂矣得中而不過其
punctuated:
觀高宗之用傅說、文王之用呂望，其始也，盡舉平日所尊且戚者而踰之；至於用之旣久，舉天下之卑且疎者，又莫能踰焉。人皆曰：「信之篤也，任之專也。」不知傅說、呂望之賢實致之，而高宗、文王之愼又先之矣。不然，以商周之時，而何夢卜之晩乎？然則進賢而不法二聖，吾未見其爲不得已也。

易
王假之，尚大也；勿憂，宜日中，宜照天下也。

陳鍾

同考試官教諭潘批：發揮聖人戒盛之意，明白透徹，予可謂憂治世而危明主者。
同考試官教授彭批：理到之言，憂深思遠，讀之令人有警省處。
考試官主事江批：鳴盛識幾，非苟作者。
考試官署員外郎陸批：講尚大、宜照處，他卷不及。

彖傳釋豐之辭，本其有恃治之心，著其得守治之道。夫治不可恃，恃則可憂矣。得中而不過，其
translation_en:
…have observed how Gaozong employed Fu Yue and King Wen employed Lü Wang. At first, they raised these men above all those whom they had ordinarily honored and treated as kinsmen. Once they had employed them for a long time, none of the lowly or distantly connected men throughout the realm could surpass them either. People all say: “Their trust was profound, and the responsibility they entrusted to them was undivided.” They do not realize that the worthiness of Fu Yue and Lü Wang truly brought this about, while the circumspection of Gaozong and King Wen preceded it. Otherwise, in the days of Shang and Zhou, why did the dream and the divination come so late? Thus, when someone advances worthy men without following these two sages, I cannot see that he acts out of unavoidable necessity.

Book of Changes
“The king attains this”: he esteems greatness. “Do not worry; it is fitting to be like the sun at midday”: it is fitting to illuminate all under Heaven.

Chen Zhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: The exposition of the sage’s intention to warn against the dangers of flourishing prosperity is lucid and thorough. “I” [?] may be called one who worries over an orderly age and fears for an enlightened ruler.

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Professor: These words reach the underlying principle, expressing deep concern and far-reaching thought. Reading them gives one cause for vigilance and reflection.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: He celebrates flourishing prosperity while recognizing the first signs of change; this is no careless composition.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: Other scripts cannot match its explanation of “esteems greatness” and “it is fitting to illuminate.”

In explaining the wording of the hexagram Abundance, the Commentary on the Judgments takes as its starting point the inclination to rely complacently on good order and makes clear the way to preserve that order. Good order must not be relied upon complacently: such reliance gives cause for concern. Attaining the mean without exceeding it—is this…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
守治之道乎昔文王係豐之辭彖傳申之以為
天下方以為無事而實深有可慮者豐之時也
今夫化廣而地不改闢治成而民不改聚王者
値此固可樂也然坐享乎盈成之景運習處乎
熈皞之餘休其心豈肯遽足哉吾知勢足以逞
志則氣象不屑於舊章之狹小時足以侈心則
規摸必嫌於成憲之朴陋長馭而遠駕上嘉而
下樂凡制度之更張征伐之振布雖天下之所
深忌而實王者之所以勵精興事焉者矣謂之
曰王假之得非假則尚大乎然斯時也運隆而
無往不復勢盛而無平不陂王者徒憂亦無益
也必專守乎舊章而不過允執乎成憲而不違
其意果何所謂哉盖釁孽生於安寧明或有所
不察禍患隱於幾微聰或有所不聞廣詢而博
問昭德而塞違凡四海之休戚萬民之利病此
固王者之所易忘而實時勢之所宜旁燭洞察
焉者矣謂之曰宜日中得非以中則能照乎是
則處豐之道必當忘其所可恃而備其所當慮
punctuated: 守治之道乎？昔文王係豐之辭，彖傳申之，以為天下方以為無事，而實深有可慮者，豐之時也。今夫化廣而地不改闢，治成而民不改聚，王者値此，固可樂也。然坐享乎盈成之景運，習處乎熈皞之餘休，其心豈肯遽足哉？吾知勢足以逞志，則氣象不屑於舊章之狹小；時足以侈心，則規摸必嫌於成憲之朴陋。長馭而遠駕，上嘉而下樂，凡制度之更張、征伐之振布，雖天下之所深忌，而實王者之所以勵精興事焉者矣。謂之曰：「王假之。」得非「假則尚大」乎？然斯時也，運隆而無往不復，勢盛而無平不陂，王者徒憂亦無益也。必專守乎舊章而不過，允執乎成憲而不違，其意果何所謂哉？盖釁孽生於安寧，明或有所不察；禍患隱於幾微，聰或有所不聞。廣詢而博問，昭德而塞違，凡四海之休戚、萬民之利病，此固王者之所易忘，而實時勢之所宜旁燭洞察焉者矣。謂之曰：「宜日中。」得非「以中則能照」乎？是則處豐之道，必當忘其所可恃，而備其所當慮。
translation_en:
…the way to preserve good government? Long ago, King Wen appended the judgment to the hexagram Abundance (Feng), and the Commentary on the Judgments elaborated upon it: when all under Heaven believe that nothing is amiss, yet there is in fact much that warrants profound concern, this is the time of Abundance.

Now, when the transforming influence of government extends widely without the land being opened anew [?], and good government is established without the people being gathered anew [?], a king encountering such circumstances certainly has cause for joy. Yet, comfortably enjoying the splendid fortune of fullness and accomplishment, and accustomed to the lingering blessings of radiant harmony, would he readily allow his heart to be content? I know that when his power suffices to indulge his ambitions, his aspirations will disdain the narrow limits of old institutions; when the times encourage extravagance in his heart, his plans will inevitably find established statutes crude and inadequate. He extends his reins and drives afar; those above approve, and those below rejoice. Changes to institutions and the vigorous deployment of punitive campaigns, though deeply dreaded by all under Heaven, are precisely the means by which the king rouses his energies and launches undertakings. The judgment says of this, “The king attains it.” Is this not what is meant by “Attaining it, he prizes greatness”?

Yet at such a time, though fortune flourishes, nothing goes forth without returning; though power is at its height, no level ground remains without a slope. Mere anxiety on the king’s part is of no benefit either. Must he simply adhere to old institutions without exceeding them, and faithfully uphold established statutes without departing from them? What, indeed, is the intended meaning? The seeds of calamity arise amid peace, and even keen sight may fail to discern them; disaster lies concealed in the slightest beginnings, and even acute hearing may fail to detect it. He must consult widely and inquire broadly, make virtue manifest and block wrongdoing. The joys and sorrows of all within the Four Seas, the benefits and harms affecting the myriad people—these are certainly things a king may easily forget, yet they are precisely what the circumstances of the time require him to illuminate on every side and examine thoroughly. The judgment says of this, “It is fitting to be as the sun at midday.” Is this not what is meant by “Through centrality, he can illuminate”?

Thus, the way to conduct oneself amid Abundance requires that one put aside what one might rely upon and prepare for what ought to cause concern…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
彖傳之意切矣大抵治亂天也而亦或能違之
者人之勝天也勝天之道易書備矣城隍戒于
泰貞疾警于豫棟撓防于大過衣袽備于旣濟
而日中之守數義兼焉夫聖人豈不知無喪之
感人所深諱哉愚者蔽於已萌智者察於未著
彖辭亦惟智者觀之而已矣
歸竒於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛
鄭守道
===
同考試官敎諭潘批此題本注自明作者
多爲舊說所拘此篇體認親切鋪叙簡當錄之
同考試官敎授彭批蓍法曆法士子見理
不明輒爲牽制纏繞知子邃於理數乆矣
考試官主事江批得潔凈精微之旨
考試官署員外郎陸批發明蓍曆法同處甚
精潔
大傳論揲蓍之歸餘更端於曆法無不合焉夫
揲蓍有餘則歸再歸則掛其理微矣大傳卽治
punctuated:
彖傳之意切矣！大抵治亂，天也，而亦或能違之者，人之勝天也。勝天之道，《易》書備矣：城隍戒于泰，貞疾警于豫，棟撓防于大過，衣袽備于旣濟，而日中之守，數義兼焉。夫聖人豈不知無喪之感，人所深諱哉？愚者蔽於已萌，智者察於未著。彖辭亦惟智者觀之而已矣。
「歸竒於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。」
鄭守道
同考試官敎諭潘批：「此題本注自明，作者多爲舊說所拘。此篇體認親切，鋪叙簡當，錄之。」
同考試官敎授彭批：「蓍法、曆法，士子見理不明，輒爲牽制纏繞。知子邃於理數乆矣。」
考試官主事江批：「得潔凈精微之旨。」
考試官署員外郎陸批：「發明蓍曆法同處，甚精潔。」
大傳論揲蓍之歸餘，更端於曆法，無不合焉。夫揲蓍有餘則歸，再歸則掛，其理微矣。大傳卽治
translation_en:
…How urgent is the intent of the Commentary on the Judgments! Generally speaking, order and disorder are determined by Heaven; yet when people can sometimes counteract this, it is humanity overcoming Heaven. The way to overcome Heaven is fully set out in the Book of Changes: the city wall and moat offer an admonition in Tai (Peace); persistent illness gives a warning in Yu (Enthusiasm); the sagging ridgepole calls for precautions in Daguo (Great Exceeding); and clothes and rags provide preparedness in Jiji (Already Across). Maintaining the sun at midday encompasses all these meanings. Surely the sage knew that the admonition concerning “no loss” [?] touches upon what people deeply dread mentioning? Fools remain blind to what has already begun to emerge; the wise discern what has not yet become apparent. Only the wise can truly comprehend the judgments on the hexagrams.
“Place the remainder between the fingers to symbolize an intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalary months; therefore, place the remainder between the fingers twice, and then suspend a stalk.”
Zheng Shoudao
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: “The original commentary itself makes this topic clear, but writers are often constrained by older explanations. This essay shows an intimate and accurate understanding, and its exposition is concise and apt. I select it for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Professor: “When examination candidates fail to perceive clearly the principles of the yarrow-stalk procedure and calendrical calculation, they readily become entangled and constrained by them. I have long known your profound understanding of principle and number.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: “It captures the purport of purity, refinement, and subtlety.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: “Its elucidation of what the yarrow-stalk procedure and calendrical calculation share is exceptionally precise and lucid.”
In discussing the setting aside of remainders when counting yarrow stalks, the Great Commentary shifts its exposition to calendrical calculation: the two correspond in every respect. When counting yarrow stalks, one sets aside any remainder; after setting aside the remainder twice, one suspends a stalk. The principle involved is subtle. The Great Commentary draws upon calendrical …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
曆之同者以明之非以見蓍法之妙乎且其論
大衍之數而及此若曰揲蓍之法固有象兩儀
三才四時者矣而歸奇何所象哉蓋策揲而奇
生必置扐然後可以成畫歲運而日餘必置閏
然後可以定時故方四揲乎左策也取奇而不
足於揲者扐於左手三四指之間是凡三節而
一扐曆法有積盈虛三十六日去後六日而爲
三歲一閏者矣質之不相類乎及四揲乎右策
也取餘而不盡於數者扐於左手二三指之間
===
是凡五節而再扐曆法有積氣朔二十四日總
前六日而爲五歲一閏者矣合之不相同乎然
閏再則日窮窮則自有循環之理扐再則策盡
盡則不可無通變之法故曆至於五歲再閏氣
盈之數已周朔虛之數已終天道有無窮之運
也而曆法可止於再閏乎於是別起積分以爲
後閏之端焉揲蓍至於五節而再扐左之奇者
已歸右之奇者已扐易卦必十八變而成也而
蓍法可止於再扐乎於是別起一掛以爲後扐
punctuated: 曆之同者以明之，非以見蓍法之妙乎？且其論大衍之數而及此，若曰：揲蓍之法固有象兩儀、三才、四時者矣，而歸奇何所象哉？蓋策揲而奇生，必置扐，然後可以成畫；歲運而日餘，必置閏，然後可以定時。故方四揲乎左策也，取奇而不足於揲者，扐於左手三四指之間，是凡三節而一扐。曆法有積盈虛三十六日，去後六日，而爲三歲一閏者矣，質之不相類乎？及四揲乎右策也，取餘而不盡於數者，扐於左手二三指之間，是凡五節而再扐。曆法有積氣朔二十四日，總前六日，而爲五歲一閏者矣，合之不相同乎？然閏再則日窮，窮則自有循環之理；扐再則策盡，盡則不可無通變之法。故曆至於五歲再閏，氣盈之數已周，朔虛之數已終，天道有無窮之運也，而曆法可止於再閏乎？於是別起積分，以爲後閏之端焉。揲蓍至於五節而再扐，左之奇者已歸，右之奇者已扐，易卦必十八變而成也，而蓍法可止於再扐乎？於是別起一掛，以爲後扐
translation_en:
…the analogous features of calendrical regulation to elucidate it—is this not to reveal the subtlety of the yarrow-stalk method? Moreover, when its discussion of the number of the Great Expansion reaches this point, it is as though it says: the method of counting yarrow stalks certainly includes operations symbolizing the Two Modes, the Three Powers, and the Four Seasons; but what does setting aside the remainder symbolize? When stalks are counted out, a remainder arises, which must be lodged between the fingers before a hexagram line can be formed. As the years revolve, surplus days arise, and an intercalary month must be inserted before the seasons can be correctly determined.

Thus, when counting the left-hand stalks in groups of four, one takes the remainder, insufficient to form another group, and lodges it between the third and fourth fingers of the left hand. This makes three operations in all, with one lodging of the remainder. In calendrical calculation, the accumulated excess and deficiency amount to thirty-six days; setting aside the last six days yields one intercalary month in three years. If we examine the two, are they not analogous? When one proceeds to count the right-hand stalks in groups of four, one takes those left over from the count and lodges them between the second and third fingers of the left hand. This makes five operations in all, with a second lodging of the remainder. In calendrical calculation, the accumulated discrepancy between the solar terms and the new moons amounts to twenty-four days; combining these with the preceding six days yields an intercalary month at the fifth year. If we compare the two, are they not alike?

Yet after two intercalations, the accumulated days are exhausted; once exhausted, they naturally follow the principle of cyclical renewal. After two lodgings of the remainders, the stalks have all been dealt with; once they have been dealt with, there must be a method for continuing through change. Thus, when the calendar reaches two intercalations in five years, the numerical cycle of solar excess has been completed, and that of lunar deficiency has reached its end. The movement of the Way of Heaven is inexhaustible: can calendrical calculation stop after two intercalations? Accordingly, a fresh accumulation of fractional days is begun, providing the starting point for the next intercalation. When the counting of yarrow stalks reaches five operations and two lodgings of the remainders, the remainder on the left has been set aside, and that on the right has been lodged between the fingers. A hexagram of the Book of Changes requires eighteen transformations to be completed: can the yarrow-stalk method stop after two lodgings? Accordingly, one stalk is again set apart, to serve for the subsequent lodging…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
之始焉夫以曆法筮法之同如此蓋皆出於自
然而非強合者矣大抵天下之物皆出於天其
理無不同者况蓍策之生本於聖人之幽贊而
揲扐之法又起於圖象乎其推之造化而皆合
也固聖人之功實蓍策天然自有之理聖人能
因而成之耳若物無是理而聖人有意為之則
易書亦一太玄而已矣
書
視遠惟明聽德惟聰
===
謝炯
同考試官訓導李批聰明二字作者多說
向外去獨此就德上發明深合經㫖宜錄以式
同考試官教諭易批懋德之目耳目尤為
切要子獨能發揮聰明二字親切可取
考試官主事江批密緻
考試官署員外郎陸批文有思致
大臣告君之視聽當盡其用而思其則焉甚矣
人君視聽之不可苟也亦本諸聰明之則而已
punctuated:
之始焉。夫以曆法、筮法之同如此，蓋皆出於自然而非強合者矣。大抵天下之物皆出於天，其理無不同者，况蓍策之生本於聖人之幽贊，而揲扐之法又起於圖象乎？其推之造化而皆合也，固聖人之功，實蓍策天然自有之理，聖人能因而成之耳。若物無是理，而聖人有意為之，則易書亦一太玄而已矣。
書
視遠惟明，聽德惟聰。
謝炯
同考試官訓導李批：「聰明二字，作者多說向外去，獨此就德上發明，深合經㫖，宜錄以式。」
同考試官教諭易批：「懋德之目，耳目尤為切要。子獨能發揮聰明二字，親切可取。」
考試官主事江批：「密緻。」
考試官署員外郎陸批：「文有思致。」
大臣告君之視聽，當盡其用而思其則焉。甚矣，人君視聽之不可苟也！亦本諸聰明之則而已
translation_en:
…to serve as the beginning of the subsequent setting aside of stalks. Such correspondences between calendrical methods and divination methods all arise naturally; they are not forced agreements. Generally speaking, all things under Heaven originate in Heaven, and their principles invariably accord. How much more so with yarrow stalks, whose emergence is rooted in the sages’ mysterious assistance to the divine, and whose methods of counting and setting aside derive from diagrams and images! That these methods, when extended to the workings of creation, accord with them throughout is certainly an achievement of the sages. Yet these are really principles naturally inherent in the yarrow stalks themselves; the sages could simply follow them and bring them to completion. If things lacked these principles and the sages deliberately contrived them, then the Book of Changes would be merely another Supreme Mystery (Taixuan).
Book of Documents
“To see far is clarity of sight; to listen to virtue is acuity of hearing.”
Xie Jiong
Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Most writers explain the two words ‘acuity’ and ‘clarity’ in terms of outward things. This author alone elucidates them in terms of virtue, closely according with the meaning of the Classic. It should be recorded as a model.”
Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor, comments: “Among the particulars of cultivating virtue, the ears and eyes are especially crucial. You alone have been able to expound the two words ‘acuity’ and ‘clarity’ in a pertinent manner worthy of acceptance.”
Examiner Jiang, Secretary, comments: “Closely reasoned and finely wrought.”
Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director, comments: “The writing shows thoughtful conception.”
A great minister instructs his ruler that, in seeing and hearing, he should fully exercise these faculties and reflect upon their proper standards. How essential it is that a ruler not be careless in his seeing and hearing! These must simply be grounded in the standards of acuity and clarity…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而可徒求諸用哉伊尹告太甲之意蓋謂思孝
思恭所以懋德也而耳目之用尤為切身當何
如哉彼物交於前目則視之然必欲其遠焉坐
九重而明徹乎萬里之休戚秉離照而旁燭乎
宇宙之幾微於人所不及見者而吾獨見之亦
曰思乎明焉耳蓋明者目之則而視之所由以
遠者也精白其念慮復虛靈於固有澡雪其心
志發光輝於感通是惟無視視必思明自然蔽
錮開而萬物莫遁其情障翳徹而眾理悉呈其
===
蘊視不患乎不遠矣發言盈庭耳實聽之然必
欲其德焉聲之所入皆足以責難陳善辭之所
達悉關乎論道經邦惟義理之當聽者然後聽
之亦曰思乎聰焉耳蓋聰者耳之則而聽之所
由德者也卽其虛通之體存之而使其可以受
自其穎慧之性充之而不使至于塞是惟無聽
聽則思聰自然至理不惑于耳順之際妙道旁
通於睿聽之下聽不患其不德矣是則視可以
遠惟明及之聽可以德惟聰致之懋德之功莫
punctuated: 而可徒求諸用哉？伊尹告太甲之意，蓋謂思孝思恭，所以懋德也，而耳目之用尤為切身，當何如哉？彼物交於前，目則視之，然必欲其遠焉。坐九重而明徹乎萬里之休戚，秉離照而旁燭乎宇宙之幾微，於人所不及見者而吾獨見之，亦曰思乎明焉耳。蓋明者目之則，而視之所由以遠者也。精白其念慮，復虛靈於固有；澡雪其心志，發光輝於感通。是惟無視，視必思明，自然蔽錮開而萬物莫遁其情，障翳徹而眾理悉呈其蘊，視不患乎不遠矣。發言盈庭，耳實聽之，然必欲其德焉。聲之所入，皆足以責難陳善；辭之所達，悉關乎論道經邦。惟義理之當聽者，然後聽之，亦曰思乎聰焉耳。蓋聰者耳之則，而聽之所由德者也。卽其虛通之體，存之而使其可以受；自其穎慧之性，充之而不使至于塞。是惟無聽，聽則思聰，自然至理不惑于耳順之際，妙道旁通於睿聽之下，聽不患其不德矣。是則視可以遠，惟明及之；聽可以德，惟聰致之。懋德之功莫
translation_en:
…and can one seek it merely in their use? Yi Yin’s intention in admonishing Tai Jia was, presumably, that attentiveness to filial devotion and reverence serves to cultivate virtue. Yet the use of the ears and eyes concerns one’s own person especially closely: how, then, should they be used? When things present themselves before us, the eyes see them, but their vision must reach far. Seated deep within the palace, the ruler must clearly perceive the joys and sorrows of people ten thousand li away; wielding the radiance of Li, the trigram of fire, he must illuminate on every side the subtlest stirrings throughout the universe. Where others cannot see, he alone sees. This means simply being mindful of clarity of vision. For clarity is the standard governing the eyes, and it is what enables sight to reach far. Purify one’s thoughts, restoring the mind’s inherent openness and spiritual awareness; cleanse one’s heart and intentions, bringing forth their radiance in responsive communion with things. Thus, whenever one looks, one must be mindful of clarity. Obstructions will naturally fall away, and nothing will be able to conceal its true circumstances; impediments will be cleared, and all principles will fully disclose their depths. There will then be no fear that one’s vision does not reach far.

When utterances fill the court, the ears indeed hear them, but such hearing must accord with virtue. Everything that enters the ears should serve to demand difficult achievements of the ruler and lay good counsel before him; everything conveyed in words should concern discussing the Way and governing the realm.
