Listen only to what moral principle requires one to hear. This means simply being mindful of acuity of hearing. For acuity is the standard governing the ears, and it is what enables hearing to accord with virtue. Preserve their essential openness and receptivity so that they can receive; develop their innate perceptiveness and intelligence so that they do not become obstructed. Thus, whenever one listens, one must be mindful of acuity. When the ear is attuned, the highest principles will naturally be apprehended without confusion, and the subtle Way will be comprehended in every direction through sagacious listening. There will then be no fear that one’s hearing fails to accord with virtue. Thus sight can reach far, but only clarity enables it to do so; hearing can accord with virtue, but only acuity brings this about. In the work of cultivating virtue, nothing…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
要於此矣抑君德之成敗未有不自耳目始者
一不能制而非禮之聲色得以乘之其不至于
盲聵者幾希矣舜之明達湯之不邇武之不役
皆汲汲於此而況不及數聖者乎雖然舊章之
壞也亦聰明爲之然則耳目之德豈以庸愚而
不足顧專溺於彼則於遠於德有不能及矣
明作有功惇大成裕
黃康
同考試官訓導李批此題多主若彝撫事
===
立說似失之拘此只平平說去而意無滲漏可謂
有識矣
同考試官教諭易批詞理俱到深得周公
告成王之意者錄之
考試官主事江批疏暢
考試官署員外郎陸批能說得明作惇大相濟
意出
有所以成乎治功者有所以存乎治體者人臣
之得於所感也甚矣治之不可偏也周工有明
punctuated:
要於此矣。抑君德之成敗，未有不自耳目始者。一不能制，而非禮之聲色得以乘之，其不至于盲聵者幾希矣。舜之明達，湯之不邇，武之不役，皆汲汲於此，而況不及數聖者乎？雖然，舊章之壞也，亦聰明爲之。然則耳目之德，豈以庸愚而不足？顧專溺於彼，則於遠於德有不能及矣。
明作有功，惇大成裕。
黃康
同考試官訓導李批：此題多主若彝撫事立說，似失之拘。此只平平說去，而意無滲漏，可謂有識矣。
同考試官教諭易批：詞理俱到，深得周公告成王之意者，錄之。
考試官主事江批：疏暢。
考試官署員外郎陸批：能說得明作惇大相濟意出。
有所以成乎治功者，有所以存乎治體者，人臣之得於所感也。甚矣，治之不可偏也！周工有明
translation_en:
…nothing is more essential than this. Moreover, the success or failure of a ruler’s virtue invariably begins with his ears and eyes. Once he fails to restrain them and allows sounds and sights contrary to ritual propriety to gain entry, he can scarcely avoid becoming blind and deaf. Shun’s clear discernment, Tang’s refusal to draw near to sensual pleasures, and King Wu’s refusal to be enslaved by them all show their earnest concern with this. How much more must those who fall short of these sages be concerned! Yet established ordinances, too, can be ruined by cleverness and acuity. Is deficiency in the virtue of the ears and eyes, then, necessarily due to dullness and ignorance? If one becomes wholly absorbed in such cleverness, one will fail to attain far-reaching vision and virtue through hearing.
“Act with discernment and achieve merit; be generous and magnanimous and attain ample ease.”
Huang Kang.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Most treatments of this topic base their argument on “following constant norms and attending to affairs,” which seems unduly restrictive. This essay simply proceeds in a straightforward manner, yet leaves no gaps in its meaning. Its author may indeed be said to possess discernment.
Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: Both expression and reasoning are fully realized. This essay profoundly grasps the intent of the Duke of Zhou’s admonition to King Cheng. Include it.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: Lucid and fluent.
Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: It successfully brings out how discerning action and generous magnanimity complement one another.
There is that by which achievements in government are accomplished, and that by which the fundamental order of government is preserved: these are what ministers gain through the influence they receive. How vital it is that government should not be one-sided! The officials of Zhou [?] possess discerning…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
作惇大之德而用惟其宜焉其觀感於王者深
矣周公教成王以內治之道如此蓋謂王於洛
邑能任我所用之舊人以圖我所行之舊政百
工有不欽承於德意耶蓋天下雖治政之失於
因循事之流于廢弛者尚多也不有賴於明作
乎百工必能滌慮洗志以效能竭力殫忠以趨
事精白一心苟可以輝煌乎事業盡吾之智識
以圖之而不辭奮發尚往凡可以裨益於國家
犯世之利害以為之而不避聰明共協於廟堂
===
百廢煥然而脩飭精神會合於有僚庶政秩然
其振舉功莫有尚焉者矣然治平既久法之不
能以盡善人之或難以責備者不少也不有望
於惇大乎百工又能崇古道而寬裕以宅心識
大體而休易以養望包容荒穢於凡勢之不可
以取必者姑少狥乎俗以和衆慎乃憲度於凡
弊之不至大甚者不輕變其常以多事恂恂以
立政而忠厚之風自成皞皞以化俗而和平之
福已致裕莫有尚焉者矣凡此皆百工之觀感
punctuated: 作、惇大之德，而用惟其宜焉，其觀感於王者深矣。周公教成王以內治之道如此。蓋謂王於洛邑能任我所用之舊人，以圖我所行之舊政，百工有不欽承於德意耶？蓋天下雖治，政之失於因循、事之流于廢弛者尚多也，不有賴於明作乎？百工必能滌慮洗志以效能，竭力殫忠以趨事，精白一心，苟可以輝煌乎事業，盡吾之智識以圖之而不辭；奮發尚往，凡可以裨益於國家，犯世之利害以為之而不避。聰明共協於廟堂，百廢煥然而脩飭；精神會合於有僚，庶政秩然其振舉，功莫有尚焉者矣。然治平既久，法之不能以盡善、人之或難以責備者不少也，不有望於惇大乎？百工又能崇古道而寬裕以宅心，識大體而休易以養望，包容荒穢，於凡勢之不可以取必者，姑少狥乎俗以和衆；慎乃憲度，於凡弊之不至大甚者，不輕變其常以多事。恂恂以立政，而忠厚之風自成；皞皞以化俗，而和平之福已致，裕莫有尚焉者矣。凡此皆百工之觀感
translation_en:
…the virtues of energetic action and generous magnanimity, employing each as circumstances require: profound indeed is the influence that observing the king has upon them. Such was the Duke of Zhou’s instruction to King Cheng concerning the way to govern within the realm. His meaning was this: if the king at Luoyi can employ the experienced men whom I employed, to pursue the established policies that I carried out, would any of the officials fail reverently to uphold his virtuous intentions? For although the realm is well governed, there remain many policies impaired by following routine and many affairs that have fallen into neglect. Must these not depend upon enlightened action? The officials will surely cleanse their thoughts and purify their intentions to demonstrate their abilities, exhausting their strength and devotion in attending to their duties. With wholly pure and single-minded purpose, whenever something can bring brilliance to their achievements, they will devote all their knowledge and understanding to pursuing it, without declining the task. Rousing themselves and pressing forward, whenever something can benefit the state, they will undertake it without shrinking from the worldly prospects of gain or harm [?]. Their intelligence will work in concert at court, and all neglected undertakings will be splendidly restored and put in order. Their energies will unite among their fellow officials, and the various affairs of government will be revived in orderly fashion. No accomplishment could surpass this.

Yet when orderly peace has long prevailed, there are many laws that cannot attain complete excellence, and people of whom perfection may be difficult to demand. Must one not look to generous magnanimity? The officials will also be able to honor the ancient Way, grounding their hearts in tolerance and generosity, and to recognize the larger principles, cultivating their standing through calmness and ease. They will embrace even what is uncultivated and impure: wherever circumstances make it impossible to insist upon a certain outcome, they will provisionally accommodate customary practice a little, so as to bring harmony to the people. They will exercise care with their statutes and standards: wherever abuses have not become very grave, they will not lightly alter established practices and thereby multiply complications. Through sincere and courteous conduct they will establish government, and a spirit of loyalty and generosity will arise of itself. Through broad and open-hearted conduct they will transform customs, and the blessings of harmony and peace will have been attained. No liberality could surpass this. All this results from the officials’ observing and being moved by…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
於王而王之意嚮有以致之者也王亦自省而
已矣抑此二道其用相須不可偏勝焉者有周
盛時明作而不矯激敦大而不弛縱上下倡和
協力相濟治亦古今莫及焉後世偏才用事崇
新進則更張太煩尚老成則優容太過往往矯
枉過甚而同歸於弊焉夫水火交濟百物攸利
不然適足以害物而已矣
詩
穆穆皇皇宜君宜王
===
李愷
同考試官訓導陳批詩人忠愛其君之意
宛然在目
同考試官教諭舒批禮曰天子穆穆諸侯
皇皇斷案明甚場中士子一槩混說非是此作得之
考試官主事江批得旨
考試官署員外郎陸批以穆穆皇皇分屬良是
詩人願王者之嗣皆無忝於重焉甚矣王之貽
其嗣者甚重也而皆足以宜之福莫大矣宜公
punctuated:
於王，而王之意嚮有以致之者也。王亦自省而已矣。抑此二道，其用相須，不可偏勝焉者。有周盛時，明作而不矯激，敦大而不弛縱，上下倡和，協力相濟，治亦古今莫及焉。後世偏才用事，崇新進則更張太煩，尚老成則優容太過，往往矯枉過甚，而同歸於弊焉。夫水火交濟，百物攸利；不然，適足以害物而已矣。

詩
穆穆皇皇，宜君宜王。

李愷

同考試官訓導陳批：「詩人忠愛其君之意，宛然在目。」
同考試官教諭舒批：「禮曰：『天子穆穆，諸侯皇皇。』斷案明甚。場中士子一槩混說，非是。此作得之。」
考試官主事江批：「得旨。」
考試官署員外郎陸批：「以穆穆皇皇分屬，良是。」

詩人願王者之嗣皆無忝於重焉。甚矣，王之貽其嗣者甚重也！而皆足以宜之，福莫大矣。宜公
translation_en:
…from the king; it is the king’s intentions and inclinations that bring this about. The king need only examine himself. Yet these two ways depend upon one another in practice; neither may predominate. At the height of the Zhou, enlightened action did not become excessive zeal, and generous forbearance did not become lax indulgence. Those above and below responded to one another and joined forces in mutual support. Their government was unequalled in antiquity or later times. In subsequent ages, men of one-sided abilities directed affairs: when newcomers were favored, changes became too numerous; when seasoned men were esteemed, indulgence went too far. Again and again, attempts to correct errors overshot the mark, ending alike in abuses. When water and fire complement one another, all things benefit; otherwise, they serve only to harm things.

The Classic of Poetry
“Reverent and august, fit to be a lord, fit to be a king.”

Li Kai

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The poet’s loyal love for his ruler appears vividly before our eyes.”
Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor, comments: “The Record of Rites says: ‘The Son of Heaven is reverent; the feudal lords are august.’ The authoritative judgment is perfectly clear. The candidates in the examination hall all discuss these indiscriminately, which is wrong. This composition gets it right.”
Examiner Jiang, Secretary, comments: “Grasps the purport.”
Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director, comments: “Assigning ‘reverent’ and ‘august’ to their respective referents is quite correct.”

The poet wishes that the king’s heirs may all prove worthy of their weighty inheritance. How weighty indeed is what the king bequeaths to his heirs! If all are equal to it, no blessing could be greater. It is fitting that the ducal …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
尸以之答鳧鷖也意謂吾王之干祿則百福矣
子孫則千億矣使多而不賢抑何所於利哉吾
願其至德淵微純一緝維天之命玄機密勿日
新崇聖敬之躋惟聲惟色殆不可得而聞亦不
可得而見也固如彼其穆穆焉精白無瑕渾然
金玉完其質文章外見燦然追琢之既成赫兮
咺兮殆抑之而愈揚也遏之而愈光也又如彼
其皇皇焉吾知王者之子孫庶固未有不為諸
侯者君而宜焉無幾也夫以其皇皇也則分茅
===
胙土而允矣一國之君入于王朝足以覲文王
之耿光振于屏翰足以揚武王之大烈四國于
蕃也四方于宣也豈有侯度不修而上奸王命
者哉所謂諸侯皇皇是已嫡固未有不為天子
者王而宜焉無幾也夫以其穆穆也則嗣大歷
服而展也天下之主端拱無為百辟之儀刑具
在建其有極萬幾之恭默無遺天命以凝也人
心以輯也豈有縱慾敗度而弗克負荷者哉所
謂天子穆穆是已凡若此者皆人所深願而不
punctuated: 尸以之答《鳧鷖》也。意謂吾王之干祿，則百福矣；子孫，則千億矣。使多而不賢，抑何所於利哉？吾願其至德淵微，純一緝維天之命；玄機密勿，日新崇聖敬之躋。惟聲惟色，殆不可得而聞，亦不可得而見也。固如彼其穆穆焉。精白無瑕，渾然金玉完其質；文章外見，燦然追琢之既成。赫兮咺兮，殆抑之而愈揚也，遏之而愈光也。又如彼其皇皇焉。吾知王者之子孫，庶固未有不為諸侯者，君而宜焉，無幾也。夫以其皇皇也，則分茅胙土而允矣。一國之君，入于王朝，足以覲文王之耿光；振于屏翰，足以揚武王之大烈。四國于蕃也，四方于宣也。豈有侯度不修而上奸王命者哉？所謂諸侯皇皇是已。嫡固未有不為天子者，王而宜焉，無幾也。夫以其穆穆也，則嗣大歷服而展也。天下之主，端拱無為，百辟之儀刑具在；建其有極，萬幾之恭默無遺。天命以凝也，人心以輯也。豈有縱慾敗度而弗克負荷者哉？所謂天子穆穆是已。凡若此者，皆人所深願而不
translation_en:
…the ritual impersonator of the ancestor uses this to respond to “Wild Ducks and Gulls” (Fu yi). The meaning is this: our king seeks blessings and receives them by the hundred; his descendants number a thousand hundred million. Yet if they are numerous but lack worthiness, what benefit is there in that? I wish that their consummate virtue should be profound and subtle, and that in purity and singleness they should perpetuate Heaven’s mandate; that the mysterious workings within them should be diligent and unremitting, and that, renewing themselves daily, they should rise ever higher in sagely reverence. As for any sound or outward appearance, scarcely anything can be heard or seen. Such indeed is their solemn dignity. Utterly pure and without blemish, their substance is as whole and perfect as gold and jade; their cultivated excellence appears outwardly, resplendent as a finished carving. Radiant and majestic, the more one tries to suppress them, the more they rise; the more one tries to restrain them, the more brightly they shine. Such, too, is their splendid bearing.

I know that among a king’s descendants, those of the secondary lines invariably become feudal lords; yet few are fit to be rulers. With such splendid bearing, however, they are indeed worthy to receive the enfeoffment of land symbolized by the division of thatch. As rulers of individual states, when they enter the royal court, they are worthy to appear before King Wen’s brilliant glory; when they exert themselves as the realm’s protective screens and supports, they are worthy to exalt King Wu’s great achievements. They serve as bulwarks for the states and extend royal influence throughout the four quarters. How could any fail to uphold the standards of a feudal lord and thereby transgress the king’s commands? This is what is meant by “the feudal lords are splendid in bearing.”

Those in the direct line of succession invariably become Sons of Heaven; yet few are fit to be kings. With such solemn dignity, however, they are truly worthy to inherit the great succession and its charge. As lords of all under Heaven, they sit with hands folded and govern without contrived action, fully embodying the model for all the princes. They establish the supreme standard, leaving nothing unattended in their reverent stillness amid the myriad affairs of government. Thus Heaven’s mandate is secured, and human hearts are brought into concord. How could any indulge their desires, ruin the established standards, and prove unable to bear their charge? This is what is meant by “the Son of Heaven is solemnly dignified.” All such things are what people deeply desire, yet cannot…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
可必得也詩人願之於君忠愛之情溢於言表
矣抑是猶未足以盡其意也而曰不愆不忘率
由舊章夫舊章之决裂類非庸下者能之愆忘
之病賢君有不免也故大甲之不順以其顛覆
湯之典刑啓之能賢也亦曰敬承繼禹之道耳
君王之宜與否夫亦慎其所率而已矣詩人之
意固不以頌而以規與
天作高山大王荒之彼作矣文王康之彼
岨矣岐有夷之行子孫保之
===
傅鎭
同考試官訓導陳批温柔敦厚之趣見於
言外
同考試官教諭舒批創業守成之意是作
足以發之
考試官主事江批頌義似此者絶少
考試官署員外郎陸批詞意莊重
詩人述王業所由成而深有望於其後焉夫莫
爲之後前者替矣此詩人所以深致其意與周
punctuated:
可必得也。詩人願之於君，忠愛之情溢於言表矣。抑是猶未足以盡其意也，而曰：「不愆不忘，率由舊章。」夫舊章之决裂，類非庸下者能之；愆忘之病，賢君有不免也。故大甲之不順，以其顛覆湯之典刑；啓之能賢也，亦曰敬承繼禹之道耳。君王之宜與否，夫亦慎其所率而已矣。詩人之意，固不以頌而以規與？

天作高山，大王荒之。彼作矣，文王康之。彼岨矣，岐有夷之行，子孫保之。

傅鎭

同考試官訓導陳批：「温柔敦厚之趣，見於言外。」
同考試官教諭舒批：「創業守成之意，是作足以發之。」
考試官主事江批：「頌義似此者絶少。」
考試官署員外郎陸批：「詞意莊重。」

詩人述王業所由成，而深有望於其後焉。夫莫爲之後，前者替矣。此詩人所以深致其意與？周
translation_en:
…cannot necessarily be attained. The poet wishes these things for his ruler, and his loyal affection overflows beyond his words. Yet even this does not fully express his meaning, so he says: “Neither erring nor forgetting, follow the old statutes.” The breaking apart of old statutes is generally beyond the ability of mediocre and inferior men; even worthy rulers cannot always escape the faults of error and forgetfulness. Thus Tai Jia’s disobedience lay in his overturning Tang’s established norms; and Qi’s worthiness likewise amounted simply to reverently carrying on the Way of Yu. Whether a ruler proves worthy of his position depends upon taking care over what he follows. Surely the poet’s intent is to admonish through these words of praise?

“Heaven made the lofty mountain; King Tai brought it under cultivation. He accomplished the work; King Wen brought it peace. Rugged though it was, Qi had a level road. May their descendants preserve it.”

Fu Zhen 傅鎭

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “A spirit of gentleness, kindness, sincerity, and generosity appears beyond the words.”
Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor, comments: “This composition adequately brings out the meaning of founding an enterprise and preserving its achievements.”
Examiner Jiang, Secretary, comments: “Expositions of the meaning of the hymns such as this are exceedingly rare.”
Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director, comments: “The language and ideas are dignified and weighty.”

The poet recounts how the royal enterprise was accomplished and places profound hopes in those who come after. For if no one carries it on, the achievements of those who came before will decline. Is this not why the poet expresses his meaning so earnestly? The Zhou…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
人祭大王之詩其意蓋謂知創業之惟艱則知
守成之不可易我周之興其一日乎自上天之
載泄於鴻濛而岐山之高作於西土逮天旣厭
亂眷西顧而增式廓也則有我大王者始去邠
而遷之其作屏修平與夫啓辟而攘剔之實嘗
荒度土功矣作則作矣天造草昧猶建侯而未
寧也則有我文王者又奕世而君之其懷保惠
鮮所以修和而輯寧之無所不用其極矣於是
彼岨之岐向爲無人之境固荆榛而麋鹿也今
===
則歸之者衆遂成都會之區有平平而蕩蕩焉
我周王業其爲成亦甚不易矣獨無所賴於其
後乎凡我文子文孫相與共承是業者盍仰而
思俯而念曰父作之子述之作而不述非孝也
我將爲孝子焉恪勤守物以光昭先君之令德
可不務乎祖有功宗有德忝而弗肖非順也我
將爲順孫焉繩其祖武以啓佑後人之丕緒誰
其尸乎使岐山之業永爲不拔之基我周之祀
將與天而罔極子孫之責塞而大王之靈亦庶
punctuated: 人祭大王之詩，其意蓋謂：知創業之惟艱，則知守成之不可易。我周之興，其一日乎？自上天之載泄於鴻濛，而岐山之高作於西土，逮天旣厭亂，眷西顧而增式廓也，則有我大王者始去邠而遷之。其作屏修平，與夫啓辟而攘剔之，實嘗荒度土功矣。作則作矣，天造草昧，猶建侯而未寧也。則有我文王者又奕世而君之，其懷保惠鮮，所以修和而輯寧之，無所不用其極矣。於是彼岨之岐，向爲無人之境，固荆榛而麋鹿也；今則歸之者衆，遂成都會之區，有平平而蕩蕩焉。我周王業，其爲成亦甚不易矣，獨無所賴於其後乎？凡我文子文孫，相與共承是業者，盍仰而思、俯而念，曰：父作之，子述之，作而不述，非孝也。我將爲孝子焉，恪勤守物，以光昭先君之令德，可不務乎？祖有功，宗有德，忝而弗肖，非順也。我將爲順孫焉，繩其祖武，以啓佑後人之丕緒，誰其尸乎？使岐山之業永爲不拔之基，我周之祀將與天而罔極，子孫之責塞，而大王之靈亦庶
translation_en:
…the poem in which the people of Zhou sacrifice to King Tai. Its meaning is presumably this: knowing how difficult it was to establish the enterprise, one knows that preserving its achievements cannot be easy. Was the rise of our Zhou accomplished in a single day? From the time when Heaven’s workings emerged from primordial chaos and lofty Mount Qi arose in the western lands, until Heaven grew weary of disorder, turned its favor westward, and enlarged the domain [?], our King Tai departed from Bin and settled there. In erecting defenses and leveling the land, opening up the territory and clearing away its obstructions, he indeed planned the earthworks on a grand scale. The foundations had been laid, yet Heaven’s creation was still in its early, unsettled state: a lord had been established, but peace had not yet been secured. Then our King Wen, generations later, became its ruler. In cherishing and protecting the people and showing kindness to the bereft, he spared no effort to bring them harmony and peace. Thus rugged Qi, formerly an uninhabited wilderness of thorns, brushwood, and deer, now attracted multitudes who gave it their allegiance. It became a populous center, well ordered and spacious. The accomplishment of our Zhou’s royal enterprise was indeed far from easy. Could it alone have no need to rely upon those who came after?

All you cultivated sons and grandsons of ours, who together inherit this enterprise, should you not look up in reflection and bow your heads in thought, saying: “The father establishes it; the son carries it forward. If it is established but not carried forward, that is unfilial. I would be a filial son: must I not devote myself to reverently and diligently preserving what has been entrusted to me, thereby making the former ruler’s excellent virtue shine forth? The founding ancestor has meritorious achievements; the ancestral successor has virtue. To disgrace them and fail to resemble them is to be undutiful. I would be a dutiful grandson: who, then, shall take responsibility for following the ancestors’ footsteps and opening up and safeguarding the great enterprise for later generations?” If the enterprise at Mount Qi is made an enduring, unshakable foundation, the sacrifices of our Zhou will last as endlessly as Heaven. The descendants’ responsibility will have been fulfilled, and King Tai’s spirit, too, may perhaps…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎其可慰矣抑遷岐非得已而周以岐興者天
實為之文王以後於豐於鎬於洛而遷者屢焉
豈大王之志與繼志述事固於其德不於其地
也王用享于岐山則神豈嘗舍諸矣使世守其
德以勿失墜雖至今猶存可也國家之作也天
也保也人也人怠而天去矣
春秋
翬帥師會齊人鄭人伐宋　宋人蔡人衛
人伐戴鄭伯伐取之　齊人鄭人入郕
===
〔俱隱公十年〕公及齊侯鄭伯入許〔隱公〕
〔十一年〕鄭忽出奔衛〔桓公十一年〕楚公
子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕公會晉侯宋
公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
小邾子齊世子光伐鄭　楚子伐鄭〔俱〕
〔襄公九年〕戍鄭虎牢〔襄公十年〕同盟于
亳城北　公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊
世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔俱襄公十一年胡傳〕
punctuated:
乎其可慰矣！抑遷岐非得已，而周以岐興者，天實為之。文王以後，於豐、於鎬、於洛，而遷者屢焉，豈大王之志與？繼志述事，固於其德，不於其地也。王用享于岐山，則神豈嘗舍諸矣？使世守其德，以勿失墜，雖至今猶存可也。國家之作也，天也；保也，人也。人怠而天去矣。

春秋

翬帥師會齊人、鄭人伐宋。宋人、蔡人、衛人伐戴，鄭伯伐取之。齊人、鄭人入郕。〔俱隱公十年〕公及齊侯、鄭伯入許。〔隱公〕〔十一年〕鄭忽出奔衛。〔桓公十一年〕楚公子貞帥師伐鄭。〔襄公八年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。楚子伐鄭。〔俱〕〔襄公九年〕戍鄭虎牢。〔襄公十年〕同盟于亳城北。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚。〔俱襄公十一年胡傳〕
translation_en:
…might thus be comforted! Yet the migration to Qi was undertaken only because there was no alternative, and it was Heaven itself that brought about Zhou’s rise at Qi. From King Wen onward, the capital was moved repeatedly—to Feng, to Hao, and to Luo. Could this have been King Tai’s intention? Carrying on his intentions and completing his undertakings surely depends on his virtue, not on his location. “The king makes offerings at Mount Qi”: have the spirits ever abandoned it? Had successive generations preserved that virtue without letting it lapse, the dynasty could have survived even to the present. The founding of a state is Heaven’s doing; its preservation is the work of men. When men grow negligent, Heaven departs.

Spring and Autumn Annals

Hui led an army to join forces with men of Qi and Zheng in attacking Song. Men of Song, Cai, and Wei attacked Dai; the Earl of Zheng attacked and captured them. Men of Qi and Zheng entered Cheng. 〔All in the tenth year of Duke Yin.〕

The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng, entered Xu. 〔Duke Yin,〕〔eleventh year.〕

Hu of Zheng fled to Wei. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Huan.〕

Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to attack Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang.〕

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guang, heir apparent of Qi, in attacking Zheng. The Viscount of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Both in〕〔the ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕

A garrison was stationed at Hulao in Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang.〕

They jointly swore a covenant north of Bocheng. The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Guang, heir apparent of Qi, the Viscounts of Ju, Zhu, and Teng, the Earls of Xue and Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng; they met at Xiaoyu. 〔Both in the eleventh year of Duke Xiang; Hu’s Commentary.〕

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
豹會晉趙武楚公子圍齊國弱宋向戌
衞齊惡陳公子招蔡公孫歸生鄭罕虎
許人曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕
劉汝楠
同考試官訓導霍批忽不君僑能臣士子
類能言之詞理精當者無踰此篇
同考試官教諭李批敘事簡古斷制謹嚴
自與俗作迥異録此以式經生
考試官主事江批敘事有法度
===
考試官署員外郎陸批約而盡
春秋責國君無故而失守予賢臣多難以圖存
衞之奔虢之會鄭之君臣實為之而勢之盛衰
不與也自周鄭交質而莊益用張假命稱兵肆
伐上公之宋隂謀設險巧取三國之師齊鄭合
而郕危蝥弧登而許入駸駸乎日有聲於天下
矣孰不曰以遺腹植之猶將十世振乎忽也辭
婚則明其非耦多福實昧於自求方其敗戎救
齊也一人焉繼而君國也又一人焉隨物而盈
punctuated:
豹會晉趙武、楚公子圍、齊國弱、宋向戌、衞齊惡、陳公子招、蔡公孫歸生、鄭罕虎、許人、曹人于虢〔昭公元年〕。
劉汝楠。
同考試官訓導霍批：忽不君，僑能臣，士子類能言之，詞理精當者無踰此篇。
同考試官教諭李批：敘事簡古，斷制謹嚴，自與俗作迥異，録此以式經生。
考試官主事江批：敘事有法度。
考試官署員外郎陸批：約而盡。
春秋責國君無故而失守，予賢臣多難以圖存。衞之奔，虢之會，鄭之君臣實為之，而勢之盛衰不與也。自周鄭交質，而莊益用張，假命稱兵，肆伐上公之宋；隂謀設險，巧取三國之師。齊鄭合而郕危，蝥弧登而許入，駸駸乎日有聲於天下矣。孰不曰以遺腹植之，猶將十世振乎？忽也辭婚，則明其非耦，多福實昧於自求。方其敗戎救齊也，一人焉；繼而君國也，又一人焉。隨物而盈
translation_en:
…Bao met at Guo with Zhao Wu of Jin, Prince Wei of Chu, Guo Ruo of Qi, Xiang Xu of Song, Qi E of Wei, Prince Zhao of Chen, Gongsun Guisheng of Cai, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Xu and Cao.〔First year of Duke Zhao.〕
Liu Runan 劉汝楠.
Comment by Associate Examiner Huo, Assistant Instructor: That Hu failed to act as a ruler and Qiao could act as a minister are points most candidates can express. But none surpasses this essay in the precision and aptness of its language and reasoning.
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: The narration is concise and antique in style; its judgments are circumspect and rigorous. It stands far apart from commonplace compositions. I have selected it to serve as a model for students of the Classics.
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: The narration follows sound principles of composition.
Comment by Examiner Lu, acting Vice Director: Concise yet comprehensive.
The Spring and Autumn Annals censures rulers who lose their charge without sufficient cause, and gives credit to worthy ministers who strive to preserve their states amid many troubles. The flight to Wei and the meeting at Guo were indeed brought about by Zheng’s ruler and minister respectively; the waxing or waning of the state’s power had no part in them. After Zhou and Zheng exchanged hostages, Duke Zhuang became increasingly assertive. Invoking royal commands, he raised troops and brazenly attacked Song, whose ruler held the rank of senior duke; through secret schemes and stratagems, he cleverly secured the armies of three states. When Qi and Zheng joined forces, Cheng was imperiled; when the Maohu banner was raised upon the walls, Xu was entered. With rapid strides, his renown grew daily throughout the realm. Who would not have said that even if a posthumous son were set up as his successor, the state would still flourish for ten generations?
When Hu declined the marriage, he understood that the match was unsuitable; yet he truly failed to understand how to seek abundant blessings through his own conduct. When he defeated the Rong and rescued Qi, he was one man; when he subsequently ruled his state, he was quite another. Filling up in response to external circumstances…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
隨物而涸國人所爲賦狡童也卒之命卿見執
大國挾盟遑遑焉去鄭之恐後矣後雖反國而
渠彌之難不免謂由人乎哉欲爲君盡君道春
秋書之責忽之不能君也自國耳有功而簡益
不兢今年蒙楚之伐明年行晉之成晉兵甫掣
二廣之茅復前楚難未紓三駕之轅相擊岌岌
乎兩大有必爭之勢矣孰不曰卽知者圖之其
能一朝居乎僑也始從鄉校之譏竟反輿人之
誦四國之爲大叔知之數世之福北宮預之舉
===
實沉破臺駘晉平所爲稱博物也卒之壞諸侯
之館垣卻逆女之公子晏然于虢之會成矣三
十年間金革之聲遂寢伊誰之力與不有君子
其何能國春秋書之子子產之能國也噫祭仲
專而鄭忽奔季氏强而昭公出庸君之制於其
臣也其終類至於失國然魯定之不振視鄭簡
有𢘆矣墮三都誅正卯三月之內孔丘之功實
博焉子產一惠人耳猶能以區區之鄭當晉楚
之衝女樂拒而相事終三年其有成矣孔子之
punctuated:
隨物而涸，國人所爲賦《狡童》也。卒之命卿見執，大國挾盟，遑遑焉去鄭之恐後矣。後雖反國，而渠彌之難不免，謂由人乎哉？欲爲君，盡君道。《春秋》書之，責忽之不能君也。自國耳有功，而簡益不兢。今年蒙楚之伐，明年行晉之成；晉兵甫掣，二廣之茅復前；楚難未紓，三駕之轅相擊。岌岌乎，兩大有必爭之勢矣。孰不曰：「卽知者圖之，其能一朝居乎？」僑也始從鄉校之譏，竟反輿人之誦。四國之爲，大叔知之；數世之福，北宮預之。舉實沉，破臺駘，晉平所爲稱博物也。卒之壞諸侯之館垣，卻逆女之公子，晏然于虢之會成矣。三十年間，金革之聲遂寢，伊誰之力與？不有君子，其何能國？《春秋》書之，子子產之能國也。
噫！祭仲專而鄭忽奔，季氏强而昭公出，庸君之制於其臣也，其終類至於失國。然魯定之不振，視鄭簡有𢘆矣。墮三都，誅正卯，三月之內，孔丘之功實博焉。子產一惠人耳，猶能以區區之鄭當晉楚之衝。女樂拒而相事終，三年其有成矣。孔子之
translation_en:
…and ran dry as circumstances changed: this was why the people of his state composed “The Cunning Boy.” In the end, his appointed minister was seized, and a great state used a covenant to exert pressure; in his alarm, he feared only that he would not leave Zheng soon enough. Although he later returned to his state, he could not escape the disaster brought upon him by Qu Mi. Could this be attributed to others? If one wishes to be a ruler, one must fulfill the ruler’s Way. The Spring and Autumn Annals records these events to reproach Hu for his inability to act as a ruler.
After Guo Er [?] rendered meritorious service, Duke Jian grew still less vigilant. This year Zheng suffered an attack by Chu; the next, it implemented a peace agreement with Jin. Jin’s troops had barely withdrawn before the spears [?] of Chu’s two chariot divisions advanced again; before the danger from Chu had eased, the chariot shafts of Jin’s three successive expeditions were clashing together. How precarious! The two great powers were bound to contend for it. Who would not have said, “Even if a wise man devised a plan, could he remain there for a single morning?” Yet Qiao, initially subjected to criticism in the village schools, ultimately won songs of praise from the common people. Taishu understood his service to the four states [?]; Beigong foresaw blessings lasting several generations. He explained Shichen and clarified the mystery of Tai Tai: this was why Duke Ping of Jin praised his extensive knowledge. In the end, he demolished the walls of the lodging for the feudal lords and turned back the ducal son who had come to fetch a bride; at the meeting at Guo, he calmly secured an agreement. For thirty years the sounds of arms and armor consequently fell silent. Whose achievement was this? Without a gentleman, how could a state be governed? The Spring and Autumn Annals records these events to honor [?] Zichan’s ability to govern a state.
Alas! When Ji Zhong monopolized power, Hu of Zheng fled; when the Ji lineage grew strong, Duke Zhao went into exile. When mediocre rulers are controlled by their ministers, the outcome generally is the loss of their states. Yet Duke Ding of Lu, despite his weakness, possessed greater constancy [?] than Duke Jian of Zheng. Demolishing the fortifications of the three cities and executing Zhengmao—within three months, Kong Qiu’s achievements were indeed extensive. Zichan was merely a benevolent man, yet even he could enable tiny Zheng to withstand the pressure of Jin and Chu. Had the female musicians been refused and Confucius’s service as minister continued to its conclusion, in three years there would have been results. Confucius’s…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
賢優於子產季桓之知不及子皮此春秋所以
作乎
秦人伐晉文公三年晉侯伐秦文公四年
蘇瀾
同考試官訓導霍批會傳明經闡盡聖人
待秦晉奧旨且格高辭健錄之
同考試官教諭李批經之蘊子殆發之無
餘尚薦攸宜
考試官主事江批深得傳意
===
考試官署員外郎陸批有斷制
春秋紀二國之兵有責之備者有待之畧者責
之備故秦不嫌於貶待之畧故晉不與於貶焉
此所謂志而晦也且秦繆何為而伐晉也晉嘗
三敗其師也夫秦之怨晉實深之以直報者人
之情耳遽得貶者何君子貴懲忿大室慾殽函
之敗秦誓作焉不遠而復將慾之窒矣彭衙之
師弗利而焚舟之舉繼之謂之懲忿不可也吾
聞古有三戰而三北者君子不以為怯也柰何
punctuated:
賢優於子產，季桓之知不及子皮，此春秋所以作乎？

「秦人伐晉」，文公三年；「晉侯伐秦」，文公四年。
蘇瀾

同考試官訓導霍批：會傳明經，闡盡聖人待秦晉奧旨，且格高辭健，錄之。
同考試官教諭李批：經之蘊，子殆發之無餘，尚薦攸宜。
考試官主事江批：深得傳意。
考試官署員外郎陸批：有斷制。

春秋紀二國之兵，有責之備者，有待之畧者。責之備，故秦不嫌於貶；待之畧，故晉不與於貶焉。此所謂志而晦也。且秦繆何為而伐晉也？晉嘗三敗其師也。夫秦之怨晉，實深之，以直報者，人之情耳。遽得貶者何？君子貴懲忿，大室慾。殽函之敗，秦誓作焉，不遠而復，將慾之窒矣。彭衙之師弗利，而焚舟之舉繼之，謂之懲忿，不可也。吾聞古有三戰而三北者，君子不以為怯也。柰何
translation_en:
…surpassed Zichan in worthiness, while Ji Huan’s understanding fell short of Zipi’s. Was this why the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed?

“The men of Qin attacked Jin”—the third year of Duke Wen; “The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin”—the fourth year of Duke Wen.
By Su Lan.

Associate Examiner Huo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He brings together the commentaries to illuminate the Classic, fully revealing the Sage’s profound intent in his treatment of Qin and Jin. Moreover, the style is elevated and the language vigorous. Accept it.”
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “You have brought out virtually all the Classic’s hidden meaning, leaving nothing unexplained. It is fitting to recommend you highly.”
Examiner Jiang, Secretary, comments: “He has thoroughly grasped the meaning of the commentary.”
Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director, comments: “He shows decisive judgment.”

In recording the warfare between these two states, the Spring and Autumn Annals holds one to exacting standards and treats the other less strictly. Because it holds Qin to exacting standards, it does not hesitate to censure Qin; because it treats Jin less strictly, it does not subject Jin to censure. This is what is meant by recording matters while leaving the meaning implicit.

Now why did Duke Mu of Qin attack Jin? Jin had defeated his army three times. Qin’s resentment toward Jin was indeed deep; to repay injury with uprightness is simply human feeling. Why, then, was he immediately censured? The gentleman values restraining anger and curbing desire [?]. After the defeat at Yao and Han, the Oath of Qin was composed. By returning to the proper path before straying far, he seemed about to curb his desires. Yet the unsuccessful campaign at Pengya was followed by the expedition in which he burned his boats. This cannot be called restraining anger. I have heard that in antiquity there were men who fought three times and fled three times, yet the gentleman did not consider them cowardly. Why must …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
必若所為然後為武與春秋人之若曰改過不
吝王者之事也夫人無望焉耳矣賢如秦繆猶
或貳之成人之美者不求之而輒盡乎傳謂以
王事責之者是也晉襄何為又伐秦也讎其取
王官與郊也夫秦之報乃其所耳晉又報之則
滋甚矣得無貶者何君子無始禍無怙亂忘親
背惠襲人之師先事加人非省德而動矣許魯
之侵不已而復求釋憾於西焉不謂之敢行稱
亂不可也吾聞一夫猶不可狃況匹敵之國也
===
必百戰百勝然後快於心與春秋仍爵之若曰
睚眦之怨必報常人之情也有志者不屑焉晉
襄至此無多賴矣顧欲於一字重輕之不亦遠
乎傳謂以常情待之者是也望之深故責之備
待之畧亦教之道也聖人之心無不欲其入於
善與抑秦繆過而悔之而復貳之惜也然至是
見伐而不報誓言其終踐乎不然則秦誓一篇
罔人之語耳削之後也夫豈不義而序書終之
重改過嘉釋怨風乎後之君子云爾也三良之
punctuated:
必若所為，然後為武與？《春秋》人之，若曰：「改過不吝，王者之事也，夫人無望焉耳矣。賢如秦繆，猶或貳之，成人之美者不求之而輒盡乎？」傳謂以王事責之者，是也。
晉襄何為又伐秦也？讎其取王官與郊也。夫秦之報，乃其所耳。晉又報之，則滋甚矣。得無貶者何？君子無始禍，無怙亂。忘親背惠，襲人之師，先事加人，非省德而動矣。許魯之侵不已，而復求釋憾於西焉，不謂之敢行稱亂不可也。吾聞一夫猶不可狃，況匹敵之國也？必百戰百勝，然後快於心與？《春秋》仍爵之，若曰：「睚眦之怨必報，常人之情也，有志者不屑焉。晉襄至此，無多賴矣。顧欲於一字重輕之，不亦遠乎？」傳謂以常情待之者，是也。
望之深，故責之備；待之畧，亦教之道也。聖人之心，無不欲其入於善與？抑秦繆過而悔之，而復貳之，惜也！然至是見伐而不報，誓言其終踐乎？不然，則《秦誓》一篇，罔人之語耳，削之後也夫？豈不義而序《書》終之？重改過，嘉釋怨，風乎後之君子云爾也。三良之
translation_en:
…Must he act in this way before he can be considered martial? The Spring and Autumn Annals designates him merely as a “man,” as if to say: “To correct one’s faults without hesitation is the business of a true king; this is not expected of ordinary men. Yet even someone as worthy as Duke Mu of Qin sometimes repeats his faults. Would one who seeks to bring another’s virtues to fulfillment abandon him outright without demanding more of him?” This is what the commentary means by holding him to the standards of a true king.
Why did Duke Xiang of Jin again attack Qin? To avenge its capture of Wangguan and Jiao. Qin’s retaliation had been warranted; for Jin to retaliate in turn only aggravated matters. Why, then, did he escape censure? A gentleman neither initiates calamity nor relies upon disorder. Forgetting kinship and betraying past kindness, ambushing another’s army and taking the initiative in attacking others—these were not actions taken after examining his own virtue. Not content with the incursions against Xu and Lu [?], he again sought to vent his resentment in the west. One cannot but call this boldly perpetrating and fomenting disorder [?]. I have heard that even a single man must not be treated with contempt, much less a state of equal strength. Must he fight a hundred battles and win them all before his heart is satisfied? The Spring and Autumn Annals nevertheless retains his noble title, as if to say: “To avenge even a hostile glance is the impulse of an ordinary person; a man of aspiration disdains it. By this point, little could be hoped for from Duke Xiang of Jin. Would it not be far-fetched to seek to influence him through the weight of a single word?” This is what the commentary means by treating him according to ordinary human feelings.
Because expectations are high, the demands are exacting; treating someone less strictly is also a way of teaching. Does not the sage’s heart desire that everyone enter into goodness? Yet Duke Mu of Qin committed a fault, repented, and then repeated it: how regrettable! Nevertheless, when he was attacked on this occasion, he did not retaliate. Had he finally fulfilled the words of his oath? Otherwise, the “Oath of Qin” would be nothing but deceptive words, fit to be excised by later generations [?]. Surely there was a righteous purpose in placing it last in the arrangement of the Book of Documents? It was simply to honor the correction of faults, commend the relinquishment of resentment, and admonish the gentlemen of later ages. As for the three worthy men’s…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
殉黃鳥賦焉其不得正而斃矣君子曰秦繆之
不為盟主也宜哉
禮記
心中斯須不和不樂而鄙詐之心入之矣
外貌斯須不莊不敬而易慢之心入之
矣
張槩
同考試官學正王批此題專就禮上說作
者以樂入之殊失本旨理明詞整如此篇者可以
===
式矣
考試官主事江批有體認
考試官署員外郎陸批講二入字不類衆作
即外物之易乗以見自治之當密焉夫外物之
入必乗其可而幾則甚易也致禮以治躬者其
可少有間斷乎記樂記者之意謂夫著誠去偽
禮之經也危微之分間不容髮彼禮雖修外而
達內以之心中而常和且樂焉可也苟斯須之
間涵養或缺而意緒乖張積習未真而天機拂
punctuated:
殉，《黃鳥》賦焉，其不得正而斃矣。君子曰：「秦繆之不為盟主也，宜哉！」

禮記

心中斯須不和不樂，而鄙詐之心入之矣；外貌斯須不莊不敬，而易慢之心入之矣。

張槩

同考試官學正王批：「此題專就禮上說，作者以樂入之，殊失本旨。理明詞整如此篇者，可以式矣。」

考試官主事江批：「有體認。」

考試官署員外郎陸批：「講二入字，不類衆作。」

即外物之易乗，以見自治之當密焉。夫外物之入，必乗其可，而幾則甚易也。致禮以治躬者，其可少有間斷乎？記《樂記》者之意，謂夫著誠去偽，禮之經也。危微之分，間不容髮。彼禮雖修外而達內，以之心中而常和且樂焉，可也。苟斯須之間，涵養或缺而意緒乖張，積習未真而天機拂
translation_en:
…being sacrificed to accompany him in death, the poem “Yellow Birds” was composed on their account. He thus died without attaining what was right. The gentleman says: “How fitting that Duke Mu of Qin did not become leader of the covenant!”

Book of Rites

“If the heart is without harmony and joy even for a moment, baseness and deceit enter it; if the outward demeanor lacks dignity and reverence even for a moment, frivolity and arrogance enter it.”

Zhang Gai

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “This topic concerns ritual propriety exclusively. By introducing music, the author departs markedly from its original purport. Yet an essay with reasoning as clear and language as orderly as this can serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: “Shows personal understanding.”

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: “Its explanation of the two occurrences of ‘enter’ differs from the other essays.”

The ease with which external things exploit an opening shows how closely one must govern oneself. External things enter only by taking advantage of an opportunity, and the incipient turning point is very easily crossed. Can those who fully apply ritual propriety to governing themselves allow even the slightest interruption? The intention of the compiler of the Record of Music is that manifesting sincerity and eliminating falsity constitute the constant principle of ritual propriety. The distinction between the precarious and the subtle admits not even a hair’s breadth of separation. Although ritual propriety cultivates the outward person, it reaches within; through it, the heart may remain constantly harmonious and joyful. But if, even for a moment, inward cultivation is deficient and one’s thoughts become unruly, or accumulated practice has not become genuine and the spontaneous workings of one’s nature are thwarted…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
鬱則內亂其神矣內之亂者外之所以得閒也
故鄙詐之心不旋踵而遂入焉謂之入者以凡
陋詭譎元非已有出乎彼而後入乎此也猶之
元氣傷而客邪有不中乎夫以不和不樂者纔
斯須而鄙詐之心即入之可見心中不可斯須
而非禮矣禮自外作而飾貌以之外貌而常莊
且敬焉可也苟斯須之間防檢疎而矜持之念
薄繩約縱而嚴肅之意微則外弛其備矣外之
弛者內之所以不固也故易慢之心不旋踵而
===
遂入焉謂之入者以忽畧偷惰本自外至滅於
東而後生於西也猶之藩籬徹而冠盜有不速
乎夫以不莊不敬者纔斯須而易慢之心即入
之可見外貌不可斯須而非禮矣大抵心欲虛
不可以無主也心欲實不可以有物也莊敬和
樂心之主也鄙詐易慢心之物也曰斯須曰入
者正見夫相代之勢甚易雖其外物得而入之
則遂為主於內矣正善惡之幾而吉凶之判也
不察乎此而曰若之何為君子為小人也不亦
punctuated: 鬱，則內亂其神矣。內之亂者，外之所以得閒也。故鄙詐之心不旋踵而遂入焉。謂之入者，以凡陋詭譎元非已有，出乎彼而後入乎此也。猶之元氣傷，而客邪有不中乎？夫以不和不樂者纔斯須，而鄙詐之心即入之，可見心中不可斯須而非禮矣。禮自外作而飾貌，以之外貌而常莊且敬焉，可也。苟斯須之間防檢疎而矜持之念薄，繩約縱而嚴肅之意微，則外弛其備矣。外之弛者，內之所以不固也。故易慢之心不旋踵而遂入焉。謂之入者，以忽畧偷惰本自外至，滅於東而後生於西也。猶之藩籬徹，而冠盜有不速乎？夫以不莊不敬者纔斯須，而易慢之心即入之，可見外貌不可斯須而非禮矣。大抵心欲虛，不可以無主也；心欲實，不可以有物也。莊敬和樂，心之主也；鄙詐易慢，心之物也。曰斯須，曰入者，正見夫相代之勢甚易，雖其外物得而入之，則遂為主於內矣。正善惡之幾而吉凶之判也。不察乎此，而曰若之何為君子、為小人也，不亦
translation_en:
…becomes stifled, then one's spirit is disordered within. This internal disorder gives external influences an opening. Thus a mean and deceitful disposition enters before one can turn on one's heel. It is called “entering” because vulgarity and guile were originally not one's own [?]: they issue from there and only then enter here. It is like injury to one's vital energy: how could invading pathogenic influences fail to strike? If even a moment's lack of harmony and joy allows a mean and deceitful disposition to enter immediately, we can see that the heart must never depart from ritual propriety, even for a moment. Ritual propriety arises externally and adorns one's bearing. It is fitting to apply it to one's outward appearance, remaining constantly dignified and reverent. If, even for a moment, vigilance and restraint grow lax and the resolve to maintain self-command weakens, if discipline slackens and the intention to remain solemn diminishes, then one's outward defenses are relaxed. This outward laxity leaves the interior insecure. Thus a careless and disrespectful disposition enters before one can turn on one's heel. It is called “entering” because negligence and indolence originally arrive from outside: extinguished in the east, they then arise in the west. It is like removing a protective fence: how could this fail to invite robbers [?]? If even a moment's lack of dignity and reverence allows a careless and disrespectful disposition to enter immediately, we can see that one's outward bearing must never depart from ritual propriety, even for a moment.

In general, the heart should be empty, yet cannot lack a master; the heart should be full, yet cannot contain extraneous things. Dignity, reverence, harmony, and joy are the heart's masters; meanness, deceit, carelessness, and disrespect are extraneous things within it. The expressions “a moment” and “entering” precisely reveal how readily one state displaces another: once those external things gain entry, they become masters within. This is precisely the incipient point of good and evil, where good fortune and misfortune divide. To fail to examine this, yet ask how one becomes a gentleman or a petty person—is this not …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
謬乎
故大臣不可不敬也是民之表也邇臣不
可不慎也是民之道也
陳席珍
同考試官學正王批民之表類能言之此
篇於民之道發揮更覺親切
考試官主事江批平實中有頓挫處
考試官署員外郎陸批奇氣逸發
君之待臣當畢盡其道者皆以其有關於天下
===
也夫以其為民之表與其道也則大臣邇臣所
關誠不小矣人君敬而慎之也而豈徒哉且立
乎朝廷之上詔天子以出政令者大臣也大臣
可以不敬乎必信之篤無或疑也任之專無或
貳也所以然者非徒遠廉地以高其堂也夫既
舉而加諸大臣之位則使之羽儀天下矣固天
下所望而震焉者也苟人君之敬少有不至則
民將曰是嘗不獲乎上者也皆易焉而莫之重
出乎身加乎民千里之外違之矣是自裂冠毀
punctuated:
謬乎？

故大臣不可不敬也，是民之表也；邇臣不可不慎也，是民之道也。

陳席珍

同考試官學正王批：「民之表，類能言之；此篇於民之道，發揮更覺親切。」
考試官主事江批：「平實中有頓挫處。」
考試官署員外郎陸批：「奇氣逸發。」

君之待臣當畢盡其道者，皆以其有關於天下也。夫以其為民之表與其道也，則大臣、邇臣所關誠不小矣。人君敬而慎之也，而豈徒哉？且立乎朝廷之上，詔天子以出政令者，大臣也。大臣可以不敬乎？必信之篤，無或疑也；任之專，無或貳也。所以然者，非徒遠廉地以高其堂也。夫既舉而加諸大臣之位，則使之羽儀天下矣，固天下所望而震焉者也。苟人君之敬少有不至，則民將曰：「是嘗不獲乎上者也。」皆易焉而莫之重。出乎身，加乎民，千里之外違之矣。是自裂冠毀
translation_en:
… mistaken?

“Thus great ministers must be treated with respect, for they are the people's examples; ministers close to the ruler must be treated with care, for they are the people's guides.”

Chen Xizhen

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “Most can discuss ‘the people's examples’; this essay's exposition of ‘the people's guides’ is especially apt.”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: “Within its plain and substantial writing are passages of rhythmic variation.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: “An extraordinary spirit flows forth freely.”

That a ruler must fully observe the proper way of treating his ministers is entirely because they have a bearing on all under Heaven. Since they serve as the people's examples and guides, the importance of great ministers and ministers close to the ruler is indeed considerable. How could the ruler's respect and care in treating them be without purpose? Those who stand at court and advise the Son of Heaven in issuing governmental commands are the great ministers. Can great ministers be treated without respect? The ruler must trust them deeply, without any doubt, and entrust them with undivided responsibility, without divided allegiance. The reason for this is not merely to elevate the hall by setting its edges farther from the ground [?]. Once he has raised men to the rank of great minister, he has made them models for all under Heaven: they are those to whom all under Heaven look with awe. If the ruler's respect falls short even slightly, the people will say, “These are men who have failed to obtain their superior's approval.” All will slight them, and none will esteem them. When commands issue from their persons and are imposed upon the people, those a thousand li away will disobey. This is to tear one's own cap and destroy …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
冕而日就天下於解弛也尚欲其維四國而毗
天子乎故曰是民之表也則雖欲不敬之不可
也布於迺左若右以旦夕承弼厥辟者邇臣也
邇臣可以不慎乎必一顰一笑愛之至也一咄
一咤審乃發也所以然者非徒嚴近習而使不
得招權市寵也夫既使之密邇於君則好惡其
所先得矣必甚焉而投其所向也苟感應之間
不出於正則民將曰吾君之情在此也皆靡然
而莫之敢後發乎邇見乎遠日捷而求其反也
===
難矣是不防微杜漸以率天下而路也尚何以
振紀綱而勵風俗乎故曰是民之道也則雖欲
不慎之不可也敬大臣則民心畏而朝廷尊慎
邇臣則民鄉方而教化立聖人之言何其要哉
抑敬而慎之待之道也擇而用之為之地焉苟
非其人重其權適足以資其奸周其防終無以
勝其弊矣此周之常伯常任乃克宅克俊者為
之而綴衣虎賁亦必皆庶常吉士也豈苟焉而
已哉
punctuated: 冕，而日就天下於解弛也，尚欲其維四國而毗天子乎？故曰：「是民之表也。」則雖欲不敬之，不可也。布於迺左若右，以旦夕承弼厥辟者，邇臣也。邇臣可以不慎乎？必一顰一笑，愛之至也；一咄一咤，審乃發也。所以然者，非徒嚴近習而使不得招權市寵也。夫既使之密邇於君，則好惡其所先得矣，必甚焉而投其所向也。苟感應之間不出於正，則民將曰：「吾君之情在此也。」皆靡然而莫之敢後。發乎邇，見乎遠，日捷而求其反也難矣。是不防微杜漸，以率天下而路也，尚何以振紀綱而勵風俗乎？故曰：「是民之道也。」則雖欲不慎之，不可也。敬大臣，則民心畏而朝廷尊；慎邇臣，則民鄉方而教化立。聖人之言，何其要哉！抑敬而慎之，待之道也；擇而用之，為之地焉。苟非其人，重其權，適足以資其奸；周其防，終無以勝其弊矣。此周之常伯、常任，乃克宅克俊者為之，而綴衣、虎賁，亦必皆庶常吉士也。豈苟焉而已哉！
translation_en:
…his ceremonial headdress, daily bringing the realm into laxity and disorder. Could he still expect them to uphold the four quarters and assist the Son of Heaven? Hence the saying, “They are the models for the people.” Thus, even if he wished to withhold respect from them, he could not.

Those stationed at your left and right, attending and assisting their sovereign morning and evening, are the intimate ministers. Can one fail to exercise caution toward them? Even a single frown or smile must be most carefully sparingly bestowed; even a single exclamation or rebuke must be considered before it is uttered. The reason is not merely to keep close attendants under strict control and prevent them from appropriating power and trading in favor. Once they have been brought into intimate proximity to the ruler, they are the first to perceive his likes and dislikes; they will surely carry these further, catering to his inclinations. If this interplay of stimulus and response does not proceed from what is right, the people will say, “Here lie our ruler’s true feelings.” All will yield to the prevailing tendency, none daring to lag behind. What originates close at hand manifests itself far away, spreading more swiftly each day, until reversing it becomes difficult. This is to fail to check the slightest beginnings and forestall their growth, thereby leading the realm down that road [?]. How, then, could one strengthen the governing order and improve customs? Hence the saying, “They are the guides of the people.” Thus, even if he wished to dispense with caution toward them, he could not.

Respect great ministers, and the people will feel awe and the court will be honored; exercise caution toward intimate ministers, and the people will turn toward rectitude and moral instruction will take firm root. How essential are the sage’s words! Yet respect and caution concern the way these men are treated; selecting and employing them provides the foundation for this. If they are not the right men, increasing their authority merely supplies resources for their treachery; however comprehensive the precautions against them, these will ultimately fail to overcome the harm they cause. Thus, under the Zhou, the offices of chief minister and regular minister were filled by men capable of holding office and distinguished in ability [?], while even the keepers of the robes and the Tiger Guards had to be men of consistently good character. How could such appointments have been made casually?

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
第貳塲
論
孔子斟酌先王之禮
劉汝楠
同考試官訓導霍批孔子具明聖兼述作
其詳見於春秋大畧實具於此吾子以宏深衍奧
之才而發之於舂容英偉之度纔數百言而意義
周匝筆力高古曷圖經生中有是作也
同考試官敎諭李批從孔子心志上發出
===
述作的意思抑揚開闔如有制之師森不可犯且
字面句法的有根據異日以文名天下者非子與
秋闈不足冠也
考試官主事江批平實古雅
考試官署員外郎陸批意深而不晦詞約而有
章慕秦漢之文而有得者
聖人之宅心也宏而其爲志也遠苟可以述不
必作焉苟有所作不遑恤焉故其述之也爲益
詳而其作之也非踰越法無常理有當也述先
punctuated:
第貳塲
論
孔子斟酌先王之禮
劉汝楠

同考試官訓導霍批：孔子具明聖，兼述作，其詳見於春秋，大畧實具於此。吾子以宏深衍奧之才，而發之於舂容英偉之度，纔數百言，而意義周匝，筆力高古，曷圖經生中有是作也！

同考試官敎諭李批：從孔子心志上發出述作的意思，抑揚開闔，如有制之師，森不可犯。且字面句法的有根據，異日以文名天下者，非子與？秋闈不足冠也。

考試官主事江批：平實古雅。

考試官署員外郎陸批：意深而不晦，詞約而有章，慕秦漢之文而有得者。

聖人之宅心也宏，而其爲志也遠。苟可以述，不必作焉；苟有所作，不遑恤焉。故其述之也爲益詳，而其作之也非踰越。法無常，理有當也。述先
translation_en:
Second Session
Discourse
Confucius Weighed and Adapted the Rites of the Former Kings
Liu Runan

Comment by Associate Examiner Huo, Assistant Instructor: Confucius possessed illumination and sagacity [?], and combined transmission with creation. The details appear in the Spring and Autumn Annals; their broad outlines are fully embodied here. You have brought your capacious, profound, and penetrating talent to expression with an unhurried and imposing bearing. In just a few hundred words, the meaning is comprehensively developed, and the writing is lofty and antique. Who could have imagined such a composition among students of the Classics!

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: You draw out the meaning of transmission and creation from Confucius’s own mind and aspirations. The rises and falls, the opening out and drawing together, resemble a disciplined army, imposing and unassailable. Moreover, your wording and sentence patterns have firm foundations. Will it not be you who one day wins renown throughout the realm for literary accomplishment? First place in the autumn Provincial Examination would be an insufficient distinction for you.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: Plain and substantial, antique and elegant.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: The meaning is profound without being obscure; the language is concise yet well ordered. Here is someone who admires the prose of the Qin and Han and has grasped something of its excellence.

The sage is broad in his disposition and far-reaching in his aspirations. Where transmission suffices, he need not create; where creation is called for, he has no leisure for misgivings. Thus, in transmitting, he makes things still more detailed; in creating, he does not transgress due bounds. Institutions have no fixed form, but principle determines what is fitting. In transmitting the former…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
王而不屑必巳之爲出聖人之心不若是狹矣
襲長去短就中而宜之亦不專事於述焉是則
聖人存天理遏人欲定先王之法以待來世之
志也豈作之能嫌四代之禮法之詳也爲邦一
問孔子斟酌之而述作具斟酌云者議之擬之
而不苟於所從也或因或革而其則在我也不
所斟酌者先王之禮則固未嘗作矣取先王之
禮而斟酌之而萬世常行之道立謂之述可乎
作者之謂聖豈孔子而不足以出其巳作非聖
===
人意也無所述而後有所作也易曰包羲氏始
作神農氏作黃帝堯舜氏作是也孔子嘗學夏
殷周之禮而聞韶也則先王之禮與其樂之不
可誣章章明矣顏淵也而創語之是主於逞私
見而不必其宜於天下後世也非孔子之心也
夫以其心則然也而三代之制皆因時損益久
而入於弊也誰能禦之六月而嘗八佾而舞春
秋之時可不扼腕而嘆者無幾也有其德無其
位孔子固不曰我將舉而措之天下也無亦曰
punctuated: 王，而不屑必巳之爲出，聖人之心不若是狹矣。襲長去短，就中而宜之，亦不專事於述焉。是則聖人存天理、遏人欲，定先王之法以待來世之志也，豈作之能嫌？四代之禮法之詳也，爲邦一問，孔子斟酌之而述作具。斟酌云者，議之擬之，而不苟於所從也；或因或革，而其則在我也。不所斟酌者先王之禮，則固未嘗作矣。取先王之禮而斟酌之，而萬世常行之道立，謂之述可乎？作者之謂聖，豈孔子而不足以出其巳作？非聖人意也。無所述而後有所作也，《易》曰：「包羲氏始作，神農氏作，黃帝堯舜氏作。」是也。孔子嘗學夏殷周之禮，而聞韶也，則先王之禮與其樂之不可誣，章章明矣。顏淵也而創語之，是主於逞私見，而不必其宜於天下後世也，非孔子之心也。夫以其心則然也，而三代之制皆因時損益，久而入於弊也，誰能禦之？六月而嘗，八佾而舞，春秋之時，可不扼腕而嘆者無幾也。有其德無其位，孔子固不曰：「我將舉而措之天下也。」無亦曰：
translation_en:
…the former kings, without deigning to insist that everything originate with himself: the sage’s mind was not so narrow. He inherited their strengths, discarded their shortcomings, and settled upon an appropriate mean; neither did he devote himself exclusively to transmitting the past. Such was the sage’s aspiration: to preserve Heaven’s principle, restrain human desires, and establish the laws of the former kings for generations to come. How could creating new institutions be objectionable? The ritual institutions of the four dynasties were comprehensive. In answering a single question about governing a state, Confucius weighed them judiciously, encompassing both transmission and creation. To weigh them meant to deliberate and assess, never choosing carelessly what to follow. Whether retaining or reforming, he held the standard of judgment within himself. What he weighed was the ritual practice of the former kings, so in that sense he had indeed created nothing [?]. Yet when he selected and weighed their rites, establishing a Way that could be practiced perpetually for ten thousand generations, could this be called merely transmission? One who creates is called a sage: could Confucius have been incapable of producing creations of his own [?]? That was not the sage’s intention. Only where there was nothing to transmit did creation become necessary. The Book of Changes says, “Bao Xi first arose; Shen Nong arose; Huang Di, Yao, and Shun arose.” This illustrates the point.

Confucius had studied the rites of Xia, Yin, and Zhou and had heard the Shao music. Thus it was abundantly clear that the rites and music of the former kings could not be misrepresented. Had he devised entirely new teachings to convey to Yan Yuan, this would have meant giving priority to airing his private opinions, without ensuring their suitability for the world and later generations. Such was not Confucius’s intention. His intention was indeed thus; yet the institutions of the Three Dynasties had all undergone additions and reductions according to their times. Who could prevent abuses from developing over the years? Performing the autumn offering in the sixth month, dancing with eight rows of dancers—in the Spring and Autumn period, scarcely anything failed to provoke dismay and lamentation. Possessing the virtue but lacking the position, Confucius certainly did not say, “I shall put these into practice throughout the world.” Rather, he would simply have said: …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
擇乎中庸議其因革而制爲一定者於此聖人
復起不易吾言焉則先王之禮猶不自我而遂
無聞於後世也是則孔子之志也是故禮時爲
大斟酌之行乎夏行禮必及樂斟酌之舞乎韶
禮辨於物斟酌之乘且服乎殷之輅周之冕書
曰惟元祀十有二月是殷有其時矣春秋曰天
王使家父來求車是周有其車矣書曰伊尹以
冕服奉嗣王歸於亳是殷有其冕矣周禮大司
樂以樂舞敎國子是周有樂矣而改歲必以寅
===
順也質於輅文於冕中也盡善盡美備也順則
不惑中則不愆備則不慙以俟百世如一日然
其出乎彼入乎此一斟一酌皆斷自聖心所以
存天理遏人欲非有一毫牽合附會於其間作
者之事大賢不得而與也志也故其作春秋也
於正月必繫春則旣行夏之時矣而其自謂也
直曰吾志在春秋春秋爲後世作者也而志在
焉明有作凡以爲後世也若曰有吾之志則可
也不然則非天子不議禮孔子雖聖匹夫也而
punctuated:
擇乎中庸，議其因革，而制爲一定者於此。聖人復起，不易吾言焉，則先王之禮猶不自我而遂無聞於後世也。是則孔子之志也。是故禮時爲大，斟酌之，行乎夏；行禮必及樂，斟酌之，舞乎韶；禮辨於物，斟酌之，乘且服乎殷之輅、周之冕。《書》曰：「惟元祀十有二月。」是殷有其時矣。《春秋》曰：「天王使家父來求車。」是周有其車矣。《書》曰：「伊尹以冕服奉嗣王歸於亳。」是殷有其冕矣。《周禮》大司樂以樂舞敎國子，是周有樂矣。而改歲必以寅，順也；質於輅，文於冕，中也；盡善盡美，備也。順則不惑，中則不愆，備則不慙，以俟百世如一日然。其出乎彼、入乎此，一斟一酌，皆斷自聖心，所以存天理、遏人欲，非有一毫牽合附會於其間。作者之事，大賢不得而與也，志也。
故其作《春秋》也，於正月必繫春，則旣行夏之時矣。而其自謂也，直曰：「吾志在《春秋》。」《春秋》爲後世作者也，而志在焉，明有作凡以爲後世也。若曰有吾之志，則可也；不然，則非天子不議禮，孔子雖聖，匹夫也，而
translation_en:
…choose what accords with the Mean, deliberate on what to retain and what to change, and thereby establish a fixed standard. Were a sage to arise again, he would not alter my words; thus the rites of the former kings would not, through any failure of mine, pass into oblivion among later generations. Such was Confucius’s intent. Hence, in ritual, timing is paramount: after weighing the alternatives, he chose to follow the Xia calendar. The performance of ritual necessarily involves music: after weighing the alternatives, he chose the Shao dance. Ritual distinctions find expression in material objects: after weighing the alternatives, he chose to ride in the Yin carriage and wear the Zhou ceremonial cap. The Book of Documents says, “In the twelfth month of the first year.” Thus the Yin had their own calendar. The Spring and Autumn Annals says, “The Heavenly King sent Jiafu to request a carriage.” Thus the Zhou had their own carriages. The Book of Documents says, “Yi Yin, wearing ceremonial cap and robes, escorted the succeeding king back to Bo.” Thus the Yin had their own ceremonial caps. In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Director of Music teaches the sons of the state through music and dance. Thus the Zhou had their own music. Yet beginning the year with the month designated yin accords with the proper order; simplicity in the carriage and ornament in the ceremonial cap attain the proper balance; and the utmost goodness joined with the utmost beauty constitutes completeness. Accord with the proper order prevents confusion; balance prevents error; completeness leaves no cause for shame. These standards can await a hundred generations as though they were a single day. In rejecting something from one tradition and adopting something from another, every weighing and every choice proceeded from the sage’s own judgment. Their purpose was to preserve Heaven’s principle and restrain human desires, without the slightest forced reconciliation or contrived association. The work of an originator is something in which even a great worthy cannot participate: it is a matter of intent [?].
Thus, when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he invariably attached “spring” to “the first month,” thereby already putting the Xia calendar into practice. Speaking of himself, he said simply, “My intent resides in the Spring and Autumn Annals.” The Spring and Autumn Annals was composed for later generations, and his intent resides in it: this makes clear that whatever he composed was for later generations. To say that it embodies his intent is acceptable. Otherwise, since no one other than the Son of Heaven may deliberate on ritual institutions, Confucius, though a sage, was a commoner, and…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
其志荒矣孔子之述述而作也孔子之作作於
述也斟酌云者程子察其心與其志乎而先王
之禮非盡於是也發其兆耳顏子亞聖也進之
矣農山之對其志可知也博文約禮所得者邃
矣鄭聲佞人之戒孔子不徐徐焉三月不違者
而猶懼其不免與罔游於逸罔淫於樂禹之聖
固不待益之言而後知也凡所以為訓耳此法
外之意而聖人之蘊也非獨以顏子告也發聖
人之蘊者顏子也
===
表
擬宋仁宗同輔臣賞花釣魚賦詩謝表〔嘉祐七年〕
許福
同考試官訓導陳批宋表如此精鍊者自
是一體塲屋中有此作是必有奇抱者矣
同考試官教諭舒批得駢儷體且寫出一
時同樂意
考試官主事江批含英咀華表之佳者
punctuated:
其志荒矣。孔子之述，述而作也；孔子之作，作於述也。斟酌云者，程子察其心與其志乎？而先王之禮非盡於是也，發其兆耳。顏子亞聖也，進之矣。農山之對，其志可知也；博文約禮，所得者邃矣。鄭聲佞人之戒，孔子不徐徐焉。三月不違者，而猶懼其不免與？罔游於逸，罔淫於樂，禹之聖固不待益之言而後知也。凡所以為訓耳。此法外之意，而聖人之蘊也，非獨以顏子告也。發聖人之蘊者，顏子也。

表
擬宋仁宗同輔臣賞花釣魚賦詩謝表〔嘉祐七年〕
許福

同考試官訓導陳批：「宋表如此精鍊者，自是一體。塲屋中有此作，是必有奇抱者矣。」
同考試官教諭舒批：「得駢儷體，且寫出一時同樂意。」
考試官主事江批：「含英咀華，表之佳者。」
translation_en:
…his purpose would then be misguided. Confucius’s transmission of tradition was transmission that also created; his creation took place through transmission. In speaking of “weighing and choosing,” was Master Cheng discerning his heart and his purpose? Yet the rites of the former kings are not exhausted by these prescriptions: they merely disclose their beginnings. Master Yan was second only to the Sage, and Confucius advanced him further. His aspirations can be known from his reply at Nongshan [?]; through broad learning in letters and restraint through ritual, his attainments were profound. In warning against the music of Zheng and glib speakers, Confucius did not proceed leisurely. Even for one whose heart did not depart from benevolence for three months, did he still fear that such dangers might prove inescapable? “Do not wander in idleness; do not indulge excessively in pleasure.” With his sagely wisdom, Yu certainly did not need to wait for Yi’s words before understanding this. All such words serve as instruction. This is the meaning beyond the prescribed rules, the Sage’s innermost understanding; it was not conveyed to Master Yan alone. It was Master Yan who brought the Sage’s innermost understanding to light.

Memorial
A memorial of thanks, composed as if by the chief ministers of Emperor Renzong of the Song after joining him in viewing flowers, fishing, and composing poems. 〔Seventh year of Jiayou〕
By Xu Fu.

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “A Song-style memorial refined to this degree constitutes a distinctive form in its own right. Someone who produces such a work in the examination hall must possess extraordinary aspirations.”

Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor, comments: “It captures the form of parallel prose and also conveys the feeling of shared enjoyment on that occasion.”

Examiner Jiang, Secretary, comments: “It savors the blossoms and chews their essence—a fine example of a memorial.”

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官署員外郎陸批表麗而則
嘉祐七年某月某日恭遇
駕幸後苑臣等得同賞花釣魚賦詩者萬象
光昭
盛世啓雍熈之運
六龍順動靈辰協樂育之休仰承
睿藻之寵頒益侈儒林之勝事光榮罕儷踴躍
奚勝臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊以
皇州春早花期獨盛於上林太液恩深魚牣
===
久誇乎靈沼必賢者而後樂此惟明王善
與人同麓人先時以戒途虞官卜磯而望
幸霄騰浮景仰窺蒼帝之呈靈風不揚波俯察
馮夷之效順細草偏承乎
玉輦神鮫獻技于金鉤百穀惟蕃露湛青門
之錦群生成若日華素滻之文採不折萌
王道奚心於玩物釣維取順
聖情適意於忘筌隋園剪綵雖工終愧體元出
震唐室放生誠惠何如舍靜懲貪矜榮擬
punctuated:
考試官署員外郎陸批：表麗而則。
嘉祐七年某月某日，恭遇駕幸後苑，臣等得同賞花釣魚賦詩者。萬象光昭，盛世啓雍熈之運；六龍順動，靈辰協樂育之休。仰承睿藻之寵頒，益侈儒林之勝事。光榮罕儷，踴躍奚勝！臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊以皇州春早，花期獨盛於上林；太液恩深，魚牣久誇乎靈沼。必賢者而後樂此，惟明王善與人同。麓人先時以戒途，虞官卜磯而望幸。霄騰浮景，仰窺蒼帝之呈靈；風不揚波，俯察馮夷之效順。細草偏承乎玉輦，神鮫獻技于金鉤。百穀惟蕃，露湛青門之錦；群生成若，日華素滻之文。採不折萌，王道奚心於玩物；釣維取順，聖情適意於忘筌。隋園剪綵雖工，終愧體元出震；唐室放生誠惠，何如舍靜懲貪。矜榮擬
translation_en:
Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director, comments: “The memorial is elegant yet conforms to proper standards.”
On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of Jiayou [1062], we respectfully had the good fortune to accompany Your Majesty on your visit to the rear gardens, enjoying the flowers, angling, and composing poems together.
The myriad forms of creation shine resplendently: this flourishing age ushers in an era of harmony and peace. The six imperial dragons move in accord with Heaven: this auspicious day brings the blessings of joyful nurture. Looking upward, we receive the gracious bestowal of Your Majesty’s refined verses, adding further splendor to this magnificent occasion for the community of scholars. Such glory is seldom equaled; how can we contain our exultation! We, your servants, in utmost awe and trepidation, bow our heads and knock our foreheads upon the ground.
We humbly reflect that spring comes early to the imperial capital, and flowers bloom with exceptional luxuriance in Shanglin Park. Your bounty runs deep as Taiye Lake; the abundance of fish has long been celebrated at the Numinous Pond. Only the worthy can truly delight in these things; only an enlightened king excels at sharing his enjoyment with others. The keepers of the wooded foothills prepare the route in advance; the wardens of the natural preserves select an angling rock and await the imperial visit. Shimmering radiance rises into the heavens, and, looking upward, we glimpse the numinous manifestation of the Azure Emperor. No wind raises waves, and, looking downward, we observe Feng Yi, the water god, displaying his submission. The tender grasses are especially favored by the passage of the jade imperial carriage; marvelous fish display their skill at the golden hook.
The many grains flourish luxuriantly, and dew lies thick upon the brocade of Qingmen. All living things come to maturity in harmony, and sunlight illuminates the patterned surface of the clear Chan River [?]. In picking flowers, you do not break the budding shoots: how could the Kingly Way be intent upon toying with things? In angling, you take only what yields willingly; your sagely heart finds contentment in forgetting the fish trap once its purpose is fulfilled. Though the cut-silk flowers of the Sui gardens were skillfully made, they must ultimately pale before your embodiment of the primal creative power and emergence in the sign of Zhen. The Tang court’s release of living creatures was indeed benevolent, yet how could it compare with sparing the tranquil and chastening the greedy? Glorying in this honor, we propose to …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
奏乎甘泉
灑翰忽傳乎大雅百篇刪後驚聞解阜之章七
步才高寡和陽春之曲光騰奎璧林間花
鳥深愁響協宫商水底魚龍欲奮
朝廷特典章掖奇逢茲蓋伏遇
○○○○至仁天育盛德海涵迎筴以撫五辰
斷鼇而立四極養人法種樹之術臨淵興
結網之思任老成而萋菲之謗不行開言
路而骨鯁之臣必用
===
大業重光於三葉豐年屢兆於多魚吾王不休
百辟方均情千夏諺君子樂胥
曠恩遂媲美于周詩吹萬同欣如臨比懼獨
樂恥嚴刑於入囿遠遊陋不軌於觀棠采
菽采芹想見成周忠厚魚罶魚藻追踪洛
鎬交孚玉律回造化之春何假鄒生之技
客槎犯斗牛之渚應來太史之占竊念臣
等樗櫟散材江湖蠢質弁髦獻芹負志偶
隨桂苑攀枝
punctuated:
奏乎甘泉，灑翰忽傳乎大雅。百篇刪後，驚聞解阜之章；七步才高，寡和陽春之曲。光騰奎璧，林間花鳥深愁；響協宫商，水底魚龍欲奮。朝廷特典，章掖奇逢。茲蓋伏遇○○○○至仁天育，盛德海涵；迎筴以撫五辰，斷鼇而立四極。養人法種樹之術，臨淵興結網之思。任老成而萋菲之謗不行，開言路而骨鯁之臣必用。
大業重光於三葉，豐年屢兆於多魚。吾王不休，百辟方均情千夏諺；君子樂胥，曠恩遂媲美于周詩。吹萬同欣，如臨比懼。獨樂恥嚴刑於入囿，遠遊陋不軌於觀棠。采菽采芹，想見成周忠厚；魚罶魚藻，追踪洛鎬交孚。玉律回造化之春，何假鄒生之技？客槎犯斗牛之渚，應來太史之占。竊念臣等樗櫟散材，江湖蠢質；弁髦獻芹負志，偶隨桂苑攀枝。
translation_en:
…presented at Ganquan, while writings from the imperial brush suddenly circulate as works of great elegance. After the ancient poems were edited, we hear with wonder a new song of relieving the people’s distress and enriching their wealth. Talent so lofty that verses are composed within seven paces produces a “Spring Sunshine” melody that few can match. Its brilliance rises to the Kui and Bi constellations; flowers and birds in the woods are deeply saddened [?]. Its sounds accord with the gong and shang notes; fish and dragons beneath the waters are ready to rise. This is an exceptional ceremony of the court, a rare encounter within the imperial precincts [?]. This has come about because we have humbly encountered Your Majesty [four circle marks in the text], whose consummate benevolence nurtures like Heaven and whose abundant virtue embraces like the sea. Receiving the calendrical tallies, you regulate the five celestial bodies; cutting off the giant turtle’s legs, you establish the four cosmic pillars. In nurturing the people, you follow the art of tending trees; standing beside the deep pool, you conceive the thought of making a net. You entrust affairs to mature and experienced men, so that slanders woven from petty insinuations gain no ground; you open the channels of remonstrance, so that upright and outspoken ministers are invariably employed.
The great enterprise shines anew in the third generation; plentiful fish repeatedly portend abundant harvests. “If our king takes no rest,” the assembled lords share the sentiment of the Xia proverb [?]; “the noble man rejoices,” and your extraordinary grace thus rivals the beauty celebrated in the poems of Zhou. All beings stirred by the wind rejoice together, while we feel apprehension as though approaching danger [?]. You would be ashamed to enjoy pleasure alone and impose harsh penalties upon those entering your park; you disdain the improper distant excursion to watch the fishing at Tang. “Gathering Beans” and gathering water celery call to mind the loyalty and generosity of the perfected Zhou; fish in wicker traps and “Fish among the Waterweeds” follow the example of mutual trust at Luo and Hao. The jade pitch pipes bring back the spring of creation: what need is there for Master Zou’s skill? A traveler’s raft reaches the celestial shores of the Dipper and Ox constellations; surely this will occasion a prognostication by the Grand Astrologer.
We humbly reflect that we, your servants, are useless timber like the tree of heaven and the oak, uncultivated men from the rivers and lakes. Like discarded caps and hairpieces, we nevertheless cherish the humble wish to offer water celery [?]; by chance, we have joined those who pluck branches in the cassia grove…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
朝端佩紫何功深愧龍門點額幸際采葑之
世遂叨縱壑之歡眷此趨陪賚蕏混栽于
蕙圃何以殫竭涓流少助乎鯨波忠罄葵
心赤膽以報
國勞甘魴尾畢力以匡
時當盤錯而不辭效王臣之蹇蹇飲江河而
知足思良士之瞿瞿伏願
益廣賁敷弘周滲漉
恩不專于向陽之花木
===
澤必及于涸轍之鮒魚申重巽之風化行必偃
懋中孚之德信格無知臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第參場
策
punctuated:
朝端佩紫何功？深愧龍門點額。幸際采葑之世，遂叨縱壑之歡。眷此趨陪，賚蕏混栽于蕙圃，何以殫竭涓流，少助乎鯨波？忠罄葵心，赤膽以報國；勞甘魴尾，畢力以匡時。當盤錯而不辭，效王臣之蹇蹇；飲江河而知足，思良士之瞿瞿。伏願益廣賁敷，弘周滲漉，恩不專于向陽之花木，澤必及于涸轍之鮒魚。申重巽之風，化行必偃；懋中孚之德，信格無知。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第參場

策
translation_en:
…What merit have we to wear purple insignia at court? We are deeply ashamed to have struck our foreheads against the Dragon Gate. Fortunately, we have encountered an age that gathers even humble turnips, and thus undeservedly enjoy the freedom of fish released into deep waters. As we attend upon you, like undeserving plants mingled in a garden of fragrant orchids [?], how can we exhaust our tiny streams to contribute even a little to the mighty waves? We shall pour out the loyalty of our sunflower hearts and repay the state with utter devotion; gladly accepting toil like the laboring tail of a bream, we shall exert all our strength to sustain the age. Confronted with tangled roots and stubborn knots, we shall not shrink back, emulating the steadfastness of the king’s servants in adversity. Drinking from the rivers, we shall know contentment, mindful of the circumspection of worthy men.

We humbly wish that you may spread your bounty still more widely and make its permeating influence universal. May your favor extend beyond the flowers and trees that face the sun; may your beneficence surely reach the carp stranded in a dried-up cart rut. Extend the wind of moral influence represented by the doubled Wind hexagram: wherever your transforming influence passes, the grass must bend. Cultivate the virtue of the Inner Truth hexagram: sincerity reaches even creatures without understanding. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, we, your servants, are overwhelmed with fervent emotion, reverence, and trembling. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude and bring it to your hearing.

Third Session

Policy Questions

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
第一問
李愷
同考試官訓導陳批聖學淵源最難測識
此策敷張惕厲實而不諛忠而能規得士如此可
以貢之
明天子矣
同考試官敎諭舒批我
聖祖
皇上心學遠繼湯武較之漢唐宋諸君奚啻碔砆美玉但塲中士子
===
率多以虛言抑揚獨此策探究本原析別異同確
有真見于其涵泳
聖化獨深者歟
考試官主事江批識明而氣昌志愛而言
忠積學之有待者
考試官署員外郎陸批言備忠愛之誠蓋知事
君之道者
德已盛而守之者其心虛道未至而慕之
者其志歉惟虛也一聞乎善即感其心之
punctuated:
第一問
李愷

同考試官訓導陳批：聖學淵源，最難測識。此策敷張惕厲，實而不諛，忠而能規。得士如此，可以貢之明天子矣。

同考試官敎諭舒批：我聖祖、皇上心學，遠繼湯武，較之漢唐宋諸君，奚啻碔砆美玉！但塲中士子率多以虛言抑揚，獨此策探究本原，析別異同，確有真見，于其涵泳聖化獨深者歟？

考試官主事江批：識明而氣昌，志愛而言忠，積學之有待者。

考試官署員外郎陸批：言備忠愛之誠，蓋知事君之道者。

德已盛而守之者，其心虛；道未至而慕之者，其志歉。惟虛也，一聞乎善，即感其心之
translation_en:
First Question
Li Kai

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: The sources of sagely learning are exceedingly difficult to fathom. This policy essay expounds the need for vigilance: it is substantial without flattery, loyal yet capable of admonition. A scholar such as this may be presented to the enlightened Son of Heaven.

Comment by Associate Examiner Shu, Instructor: The learning of the mind of our sagely founder and His Majesty continues the distant tradition of Tang and Wu. Compared with the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, the difference is surely no less than that between jade-like stone and fine jade! Yet candidates in the examination hall mostly offer empty words of disparagement and praise. This policy essay alone investigates the foundations and distinguishes similarities and differences, displaying genuine insight. Might its author be one who has immersed himself exceptionally deeply in the influence of sagely rule [?]?

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: His discernment is clear and his spirit abundant; his intentions express love for his sovereign, and his words are loyal. He has accumulated learning and awaits his opportunity.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: His words fully express sincere loyalty and love. He evidently understands the way to serve a ruler.

One whose virtue is already abundant and who preserves it keeps his mind receptive; one who has not yet attained the Way but yearns for it feels his aspirations unfulfilled. Precisely because he is receptive, as soon as he hears of goodness, he is moved by what his heart …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
固有而矜畏生惟歉也偶觸乎善亦愧其
心之未能而戒懼至以虛而矜畏者本之
以心得而資之以力制則益固矣以歉而
戒懼者勉強于須臾而因循于永久則復
逸矣故箴規之設其事同而心實頓殊其
迹似而效實懸絶嗚呼知此則我
太祖高皇帝暨我
皇上之所以比休湯武而陋漢唐宋諸君於下
風者不辨而自明矣請敬陳之夫人君身
===
雖處乎九重之尊而心則當乎衆欲之攻
聲色貨利乗間而竊發便嬖使令伺便而
投術暗長於幾微則英明或失於辨察憑
陵於昏惰則剛武或失於決斷雖以賢聖
之君處之而一或不檢未有不溺於宴安
狥於外誘者是故位無崇高自恃則患生
德無賢聖自足則慾至朽索之御惓惓垂
訓于夏典漆器之造懇懇交諍于虞庭蓋
自堯舜以來箴銘雖未立而矜持戒畏之
punctuated: 固有，而矜畏生。惟歉也，偶觸乎善，亦愧其心之未能，而戒懼至。以虛而矜畏者，本之以心得，而資之以力制，則益固矣；以歉而戒懼者，勉強于須臾，而因循于永久，則復逸矣。故箴規之設，其事同而心實頓殊，其迹似而效實懸絶。嗚呼！知此，則我太祖高皇帝暨我皇上之所以比休湯武，而陋漢唐宋諸君於下風者，不辨而自明矣。請敬陳之。夫人君身雖處乎九重之尊，而心則當乎衆欲之攻。聲色貨利乗間而竊發，便嬖使令伺便而投術。暗長於幾微，則英明或失於辨察；憑陵於昏惰，則剛武或失於決斷。雖以賢聖之君處之，而一或不檢，未有不溺於宴安、狥於外誘者。是故位無崇高，自恃則患生；德無賢聖，自足則慾至。朽索之御，惓惓垂訓于《夏典》；漆器之造，懇懇交諍于虞庭。蓋自堯舜以來，箴銘雖未立，而矜持戒畏之
translation_en:
…what is inherent in his heart, and circumspection and awe arise. Only because he feels himself deficient, even a chance encounter with goodness makes him ashamed of what his heart has not yet achieved, and caution and apprehension follow. When humility brings circumspection and awe, grounding these in inward understanding and sustaining them through vigorous self-restraint makes them ever firmer. When a sense of deficiency brings caution and apprehension, exerting oneself briefly but drifting along indefinitely leads back to laxity. Thus, although the institution of admonitions is the same in practice, the underlying dispositions differ utterly; although the outward forms resemble one another, their effects are worlds apart. Ah! Once this is understood, it becomes clear without argument why our Taizu Gao Huangdi and our present emperor equal Tang and Wu in glory, relegating the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song to an inferior position. Allow me respectfully to explain.

Although a ruler occupies the exalted position within the ninefold palace, his heart faces the assault of manifold desires. Music, sensual beauty, wealth, and profit seize openings to arise stealthily; favorites and attendants watch for opportunities to ply their devices. When these influences grow imperceptibly from minute beginnings, even an intelligent ruler may fail to discern them; when they gain ascendancy amid mental torpor and indolence, even a resolute and martial ruler may fail to act decisively. Even a worthy or sage ruler confronting them, if he lets his vigilance slip at all, cannot avoid becoming immersed in ease and yielding to external temptations. Thus, however exalted his position, self-reliance breeds calamity; however worthy or sage his virtue, self-satisfaction admits desire. The image of driving with rotten reins earnestly conveys a lasting admonition in the Documents of Xia; the manufacture of lacquerware elicited earnest remonstrances at the court of Yu. For, since the time of Yao and Shun, although admonitory inscriptions had not yet been instituted, the disposition toward circumspection, self-restraint, caution, and awe…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
心未有不存者成湯以聲色則不邇以貨
利則不殖矣然盤之銘曰苟日新日日新
又日新苟者若有所望而未能日者若有
所期而未至武王以耳目則不役以百度
則惟貞矣然觴之銘曰樂極則悲沉湎致
非悲以禁樂心於未熾非以防私慾於將
萌夫位如湯武無可畏之勢德如湯武無
可防之慾而猶若此下此者當何如也嘗
以是而求之漢唐宋諸君則有可慨者焉
===
若成帝之長夜屏玄宗之無逸圖憲宗之
連屏五十種敬宗之丹扆六箴高宗之孟
子屏孝宗之敬天圖不可謂非聞湯武之
風而興起焉者然飛燕入宮而長樂之荒
淫日甚國忠秉政而漁陽之鼙鼓遂振長
夜無逸特虛文耳功怠於淮西而故老以
漸疏斥志溺於鷹犬而貂宦竊弄威福連
屏丹扆亦空言耳若高宗之屈志於虜庭
孝宗之重禁乎道學愚又未敢謂其于屏
punctuated:
心未有不存者。成湯以聲色則不邇，以貨利則不殖矣。然盤之銘曰：「苟日新，日日新，又日新。」苟者，若有所望而未能；日者，若有所期而未至。武王以耳目則不役，以百度則惟貞矣。然觴之銘曰：「樂極則悲，沉湎致非。」悲以禁樂心於未熾，非以防私慾於將萌。夫位如湯武，無可畏之勢；德如湯武，無可防之慾，而猶若此，下此者當何如也？嘗以是而求之漢唐宋諸君，則有可慨者焉。
若成帝之長夜屏、玄宗之無逸圖、憲宗之連屏五十種、敬宗之丹扆六箴、高宗之孟子屏、孝宗之敬天圖，不可謂非聞湯武之風而興起焉者。然飛燕入宮，而長樂之荒淫日甚；國忠秉政，而漁陽之鼙鼓遂振。長夜、無逸，特虛文耳。功怠於淮西，而故老以漸疏斥；志溺於鷹犬，而貂宦竊弄威福。連屏、丹扆，亦空言耳。若高宗之屈志於虜庭、孝宗之重禁乎道學，愚又未敢謂其于屏
translation_en:
…this disposition of restraint, vigilance, and apprehension was invariably present. Cheng Tang kept his distance from music and sensual pleasures and did not accumulate wealth or pursue profit. Yet the inscription on his washing basin read: “If you can renew yourself for one day, renew yourself daily, and renew yourself yet again.” The word “if” suggests something hoped for but not yet achieved; “daily” suggests something anticipated but not yet attained. King Wu did not allow himself to be enslaved by his ears and eyes, and maintained correctness in all established rules. Yet the inscription on his drinking cup read: “Pleasure taken to its extreme brings sorrow; drunken indulgence leads to wrongdoing.” “Sorrow” restrains the desire for pleasure before it burns fiercely; “wrongdoing” guards against selfish desires just as they begin to sprout. With a position like that of Tang or Wu, there was no power to fear; with virtue like theirs, there were no desires to guard against. Yet they still acted thus. How, then, should those inferior to them conduct themselves? When I examine the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song by this standard, I find much to lament.
Consider Emperor Cheng’s Long Night Screen, Emperor Xuanzong’s Illustration of Against Idleness, Emperor Xianzong’s fifty kinds of linked screens, Emperor Jingzong’s Six Admonitions for the Vermilion Screen, Emperor Gaozong’s Mencius Screen, and Emperor Xiaozong’s Illustration of Reverence for Heaven. One cannot deny that these rulers were stirred to emulation upon hearing of Tang and Wu’s exemplary conduct. Yet when Feiyan entered the palace, debauchery at Changle grew worse by the day; when Guozhong held the reins of government, the war drums of Yuyang began to thunder. The Long Night and Against Idleness were merely empty ornament. Complacency followed the achievement at Huaixi, and veteran statesmen were gradually estranged and dismissed; the ruler’s heart became engrossed in hawks and hounds, while eunuchs in sable caps usurped the power to punish and reward. The linked screens and the Vermilion Screen were likewise empty words. As for Gaozong’s submission to the barbarian court and Xiaozong’s stringent prohibition of the Learning of the Way [?], I, in my ignorance, would not yet venture to say that, with regard to their screens …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
于圖真能躬行而無愧也此無他蓋其平
居暇日原無操持涵養之力特以一念之
良心生於夜氣一時之善言觸乎天機遂
不覺仰慚俯愧而欲假之以為進脩之具
豈可得哉卒之無根之善不可以襲取有
種之欲又難以頓拔隄防乍設而橫流暫
止習狎既久而故態悉見亦無怪其然耳
洪惟我
太祖高皇帝文武聖神度越百王然於兵戈之
===
餘即書真德秀大學衍義于
廡壁以自警我
皇上聰明睿知超越千古然於燕閒之暇
親製敬一箴及註釋宋儒視聽言動心五箴以
自助道已至而猶若未至德已盛而猶若
未盛是即成湯武王之心也聖學之淵源
豈韋布之淺薄者所能窺測哉蓋嘗論之
性之所主常切於理而難於存養是即所
謂道心情之所向多溺於欲而易於縱逸
punctuated:
于圖，真能躬行而無愧也。此無他，蓋其平居暇日，原無操持涵養之力，特以一念之良心生於夜氣，一時之善言觸乎天機，遂不覺仰慚俯愧，而欲假之以為進脩之具，豈可得哉？卒之，無根之善不可以襲取，有種之欲又難以頓拔。隄防乍設，而橫流暫止；習狎既久，而故態悉見，亦無怪其然耳。
洪惟我太祖高皇帝，文武聖神，度越百王，然於兵戈之餘，即書真德秀《大學衍義》于廡壁以自警。我皇上聰明睿知，超越千古，然於燕閒之暇，親製《敬一箴》及註釋宋儒視聽言動心五箴以自助。道已至，而猶若未至；德已盛，而猶若未盛，是即成湯、武王之心也。聖學之淵源，豈韋布之淺薄者所能窺測哉？
蓋嘗論之，性之所主，常切於理而難於存養，是即所謂道心；情之所向，多溺於欲而易於縱逸
translation_en:
…and with regard to the diagram, truly put its teachings into practice and had nothing to be ashamed of. There was no other reason for this: in their ordinary hours of leisure, they had never exerted themselves to maintain moral discipline and nurture their character. It was merely that a single good thought arose in the restorative vital energy of the night, or a timely word of goodness stirred their innate moral impulse. They then unwittingly felt shame before Heaven and earth and wished to borrow these admonitions as aids to self-cultivation. How could this succeed? In the end, goodness without roots cannot be acquired through outward imitation, while desires with seeds already planted are difficult to uproot at once. When embankments are first erected, the flood briefly stops; once familiarity has bred complacency, all the old ways reappear. There is nothing surprising in this.
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, sage-like and wondrous in both civil and military accomplishments, surpassed the hundred kings. Yet even amid the intervals of warfare, he had Zhen Dexiu’s Extended Meaning of the Great Learning inscribed on the walls of a side hall to admonish himself. Our present Emperor, perceptive and sagacious beyond all rulers of antiquity, nevertheless personally composed the Admonition on Reverent Unity in his hours of leisure and annotated five admonitions by Song Confucian scholars concerning seeing, hearing, speaking, acting, and the mind, to assist his own cultivation. Though he has attained the Way, he acts as though he has not; though his virtue is already abundant, he acts as though it is not. This is precisely the mind of Cheng Tang and King Wu. How could a shallow scholar in commoner’s clothing fathom the profound sources of such sagely learning?
I have considered the matter thus: what our nature governs is always closely aligned with principle, yet difficult to preserve and nurture—this is what is called the moral mind. The inclinations of our feelings are often submerged in desire and readily lapse into unrestrained indulgence…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
是卽所謂人心然非於道心之所在而時
培植之則無以察其惟微之幾於人心之
所發而常克制之則無以識其惟危之漸
故聖賢之德所造愈高而戒謹之心益切
於毫釐所得愈深而幾微之警益嚴於動
靜蓋有不能自已者譬之治生之家彼親
竭力于畒畝遠服乎車牛而致倉廩之富
則所以謹其藩衞以防乎盜賊者肯少怠
哉朱子曰敬者聖學之所以成始成終蓋
===
其始也盡心思慮皇皇焉常恐求而弗得
其終也防微杜漸慄慄焉惟恐守而或失
日新之銘成湯之聖敬日躋也觴豆之銘
武王之敬勝則吉也我
皇祖書衍義於
廡壁而謂學士宋濂曰朕之爲君上畏天地
下畏兆民兢兢業業不敢自逸其大要亦
敬而已矣然則我
皇上之以敬一自箴豈非上接湯武不傳之道
punctuated: 是卽所謂人心。然非於道心之所在而時培植之，則無以察其惟微之幾；於人心之所發而常克制之，則無以識其惟危之漸。故聖賢之德，所造愈高，而戒謹之心益切於毫釐；所得愈深，而幾微之警益嚴於動靜，蓋有不能自已者。譬之治生之家，彼親竭力于畒畝，遠服乎車牛，而致倉廩之富，則所以謹其藩衞以防乎盜賊者，肯少怠哉？朱子曰：「敬者，聖學之所以成始成終。」蓋其始也，盡心思慮，皇皇焉常恐求而弗得；其終也，防微杜漸，慄慄焉惟恐守而或失。日新之銘，成湯之聖敬日躋也；觴豆之銘，武王之敬勝則吉也。我皇祖書《衍義》於廡壁，而謂學士宋濂曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」其大要亦敬而已矣。然則我皇上之以敬一自箴，豈非上接湯武不傳之道
translation_en:
…this is precisely what is called the human mind. Yet unless one continually nurtures the moral mind wherever it resides, one cannot discern its exceedingly subtle incipient stirrings; unless one constantly restrains the human mind wherever it manifests itself, one cannot recognize the gradual development of its perilous tendencies [?]. Thus, the higher the virtue attained by sages and worthies, the more closely their vigilance attends to the slightest detail; the deeper their attainment, the stricter their watch over subtle stirrings, whether in activity or stillness. Indeed, they cannot help being so. Consider a household securing its livelihood: its members personally exhaust their strength in the fields and travel far with carts and oxen, thereby filling their granaries. Would they then consent to the slightest slackening in guarding their fences and defenses against thieves?

Master Zhu said: “Reverent attentiveness is that by which sagely learning achieves both its beginning and its completion.” At the beginning, one devotes oneself fully to thought and reflection, anxiously fearing that one may seek without attaining; at the end, one guards against the slightest beginnings and checks their gradual development, trembling lest one lose what one seeks to preserve. The inscription concerning daily renewal expresses Cheng Tang’s daily ascent in sagely reverence; the inscriptions on drinking cups and food vessels express King Wu’s principle that when reverence prevails, good fortune follows. Our imperial ancestor inscribed the Amplified Meaning on the walls of a covered gallery and told Academician Song Lian: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth; below I stand in awe of the myriad people. Cautious and vigilant, I dare not indulge in ease.” Its essential import, too, was simply reverent attentiveness. Thus, when our reigning emperor admonishes himself through ‘reverence and unity,’ is he not reaching back to carry on the Way of Tang and Wu, whose transmission had lapsed…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
統而默契我
皇祖獨得之心法哉抑愚又有感焉真德秀曰
惟學可以養此心惟敬可以存此心惟親
近君子可以維持此心我
皇上經筵日講不間于寒暑
朝御章疏不倦于朝夕惟學惟親近君子又
兼舉而無憾矣然啓沃有講章而事關亂
亡則禁忌而不敢上聞書史有疏解而道
涉時政則避諱而不敢旁及得無猶有所
===
擇而未廣乎
殿閣大臣非
宣召不得以請對臺諫章牘雖機密不得以面
陳得無猶有所拘而未盡乎以
皇上之聖明而顧問之禮
午朝之儀卒未復
祖宗之舊此誠愚之所未解也狂瞽之言因執
事之問而敷對至此不識可轉而聞之於
上否謹對
punctuated:
統，而默契我皇祖獨得之心法哉？抑愚又有感焉。真德秀曰：「惟學可以養此心，惟敬可以存此心，惟親近君子可以維持此心。」我皇上經筵日講，不間于寒暑；朝御章疏，不倦于朝夕。惟學、惟親近君子，又兼舉而無憾矣。

然啓沃有講章，而事關亂亡，則禁忌而不敢上聞；書史有疏解，而道涉時政，則避諱而不敢旁及。得無猶有所擇而未廣乎？殿閣大臣非宣召不得以請對，臺諫章牘雖機密不得以面陳。得無猶有所拘而未盡乎？以皇上之聖明，而顧問之禮、午朝之儀，卒未復祖宗之舊，此誠愚之所未解也。狂瞽之言，因執事之問而敷對至此，不識可轉而聞之於上否？謹對。
translation_en:
…the succession of the Way, and inwardly accord with the method of cultivating the mind uniquely apprehended by our imperial ancestor? Yet I, in my ignorance, have a further reflection. Zhen Dexiu said: “Only learning can nourish this mind; only reverence can preserve this mind; only drawing close to men of virtue can sustain this mind.” Our Emperor’s Classics Colloquia and daily lectures proceed without interruption through cold and heat; he attends to memorials at court, untiring from morning to evening. Learning and drawing close to men of virtue are thus both pursued, leaving nothing to regret.

Yet although lecture texts are prepared to enlighten the sovereign’s mind, when their subject concerns disorder and the fall of states, it is treated as forbidden, and no one dares bring it to his hearing.
