Although the classics and histories receive explanatory commentary, when their teachings touch upon current government, the subject is avoided as taboo, and no one dares even allude to it. Might there still be selectivity here, rather than sufficient breadth? The Grand Secretaries may not request an audience unless summoned by imperial command; the Censors and Supervising Secretaries, even when their memorials concern confidential matters, may not present them in person. Might there still be constraints here that prevent full expression? Despite our Emperor’s sagacity, the observances for consulting his ministers and the ceremonies of the midday audience have still not been restored to the precedents of his imperial ancestors. This is truly something that I, in my ignorance, cannot understand. These rash and blind words have been set forth at such length in response to your question. I do not know whether they might be conveyed onward to His Majesty’s hearing. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
第二問
劉汝楠
同考試官訓導霍批此策本無微詞隱義
作者往往撫拾漢唐之君事實補綴成篇令人厭
觀獨子就我
皇上勵精之治上發揮且能攄其忠悃可以覘異日矣
同考試官敎諭李批是必年少而負賈生
之志者錄之不獨以其文也
考試官主事江批忠愛如此可與事
===
君矣
考試官署員外郎陸批深達治體
國家有元氣有神氣纏綿固護其端不可
見而其中盎然禍難卒作賴以不遽動是
爲元氣丰采所加懦者起怠者奮如太阿
出匣不可嚮邇是爲神氣元氣欲實仁以
養之也而懦焉則神氣弛神氣欲張勵精
以作之也而察焉則元氣索二者之弛索
爲亟焉故夫中興之治率勵精者致之而
punctuated:
第二問
劉汝楠
同考試官訓導霍批：此策本無微詞隱義，作者往往撫拾漢唐之君事實，補綴成篇，令人厭觀。獨子就我皇上勵精之治上發揮，且能攄其忠悃，可以覘異日矣。
同考試官敎諭李批：是必年少而負賈生之志者，錄之不獨以其文也。
考試官主事江批：忠愛如此，可與事君矣。
考試官署員外郎陸批：深達治體。
國家有元氣，有神氣。纏綿固護，其端不可見，而其中盎然，禍難卒作，賴以不遽動，是爲元氣。丰采所加，懦者起，怠者奮，如太阿出匣，不可嚮邇，是爲神氣。元氣欲實，仁以養之也，而懦焉則神氣弛；神氣欲張，勵精以作之也，而察焉則元氣索。二者之弛索爲亟焉。故夫中興之治，率勵精者致之，而
translation_en:
Second Question
Liu Runan

Comment by Associate Examiner Huo, Assistant Instructor: This policy question contains no subtle wording or hidden meaning. Writers commonly gather up facts about the rulers of the Han and Tang and patch them together into essays that weary the reader. You alone develop your argument around our emperor’s vigorous efforts in government, and you also give expression to your heartfelt loyalty. This affords a glimpse of what you may become in years to come.

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: This must be a young man who cherishes the aspirations of Master Jia [Jia Yi]. His selection rests on more than his writing alone.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: With such loyalty and devotion, he is someone with whom one could serve the sovereign.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: He has a profound grasp of the essentials of government.

A state possesses vital energy and animating spirit. That which envelops and firmly protects it, whose workings cannot be seen yet abound within, and on which it relies to avoid being immediately shaken when calamity suddenly strikes—this is vital energy. That whose imposing presence rouses the timid and stirs the indolent, like the sword Tai’a drawn from its scabbard, which none dare approach—this is animating spirit. Vital energy needs to be substantial: benevolence nourishes it. Yet if benevolence becomes weakness, the animating spirit slackens. The animating spirit needs to be vigorous: energetic exertion arouses it. Yet if such exertion becomes excessive scrutiny, vital energy is exhausted. The slackening of the one and exhaustion of the other are grave dangers. Thus, the achievements of a dynastic restoration are generally brought about by those who exert themselves vigorously, but…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
繼世者少不相似焉輒遂不可救豈非張
之者太過而未嘗措天下於優柔平中之
域哉愚讀史至路溫舒尚德緩刑之疏蘇
軾求治太急之言未嘗不嘆二臣之忠不
售於當時而使漢宋升沉消長之幾遂决
於此也三代而下有勵精如漢之宣帝宋
之神宗者乎其願治也未嘗一日不三代
天下亦未嘗一日不三代望之一時精華
果銳之氣作之不遺餘力聰明果斷要有
===
大過人者使其察標本之理舍一切之法
而從容以須之和靜以鎮之乂安長治也
孰禦焉一則德教不純刑名繩下最不厭
衆心者趙蓋韓楊之死也一則挾小宋制
紛更變亂釀成靖康之釁者熙寧元豐之
政也培養封植之意微振揚飭勵之功過
漢宋之元氣索然矣宣帝之身猶不失中
興之稱神宗末年已永為基禍之主國之
不兢不待元成徽欽而後見俾後之君子
punctuated: 繼世者少不相似焉，輒遂不可救。豈非張之者太過，而未嘗措天下於優柔平中之域哉？愚讀史，至路溫舒尚德緩刑之疏、蘇軾求治太急之言，未嘗不嘆二臣之忠不售於當時，而使漢宋升沉消長之幾遂决於此也。三代而下，有勵精如漢之宣帝、宋之神宗者乎？其願治也，未嘗一日不三代；天下亦未嘗一日不三代望之。一時精華果銳之氣，作之不遺餘力，聰明果斷，要有大過人者。使其察標本之理，舍一切之法，而從容以須之，和靜以鎮之，乂安長治也，孰禦焉？一則德教不純，刑名繩下，最不厭衆心者，趙蓋韓楊之死也；一則挾小宋制，紛更變亂，釀成靖康之釁者，熙寧元豐之政也。培養封植之意微，振揚飭勵之功過，漢宋之元氣索然矣。宣帝之身，猶不失中興之稱；神宗末年，已永為基禍之主。國之不兢，不待元成徽欽而後見。俾後之君子
translation_en:
…when their successors fall even slightly short of resembling them, the situation at once becomes irretrievable. Is this not because they have strained the state’s animating force too far, without ever settling the realm into a condition of ease, gentleness, balance, and moderation? Whenever, in reading history, I reach Lu Wenshu’s memorial advocating esteem for virtue and the mitigation of punishments, or Su Shi’s remarks on pursuing good government too hastily, I cannot help lamenting that the loyalty of these two ministers found no acceptance in their day, so that the turning points determining the rise and fall, decline and growth of Han and Song were settled thereby. Since the Three Dynasties, has anyone applied himself to government as vigorously as Emperor Xuandi of Han or Emperor Shenzong of Song? In their aspirations for good government, not a day passed when they did not seek to emulate the Three Dynasties; nor did a day pass when the realm did not expect this of them. They spared no effort in stirring the brilliant, resolute, and vigorous energies of their age. In intelligence and decisiveness, they certainly far surpassed ordinary men. Had they discerned the relationship between branches and roots, abandoned expedient measures, awaited results with composure, and steadied the realm through harmony and tranquillity, who could have prevented lasting peace and good government?

In the one case, moral instruction was impure, and penal and administrative techniques were used to constrain subordinates. Nothing more deeply dissatisfied the people than the deaths of Zhao, Gai, Han, and Yang. In the other, regarding the institutions of Song as inadequate [?], the ruler repeatedly altered them and threw them into disorder: it was the policies of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras that brewed the calamity of Jingkang. Too little attention was given to nourishing and cultivating the state, and too much effort to rousing, disciplining, and spurring it on; the vital energy of Han and Song was exhausted. Xuandi himself still retained the reputation of a ruler who had restored his dynasty; by Shenzong’s final years, he had already become forever the ruler who laid the foundations of disaster. The state’s inability to sustain itself [?] was apparent without waiting for the reigns of Yuandi and Chengdi, or Huizong and Qinzong. This caused gentlemen of later ages…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
欲成人之美者恨起之九原而不可得也
故漢昭十四而識上官桀之詐明而不察
有足驗者至於章帝雖稱長厚事功所就
不及孝宣遠甚羅從彥竟以彼善於此者
其意顧不可想與則孝元以下或仁而懦
或懦而不仁或察而不明者固不足厪執
事之問也無亦憂治世而危明主乎
聖天子在上賢公卿在下愚無有於國武子之
慮也請得而盡言之夫我
===
祖宗以仁厚立國重煕累洽
聖聖相承元氣之厚如歲之春至於
先朝承平既久人心怠緩法度廢弛我
皇上以不世出之資起而承之豈能一日逸於
民上哉搜煩剔蠹振揚而飭勵之君子猶
以為晚也邇猶宴視逖聽以致大小臣工
亦罔不滌除厥志以承休德中興之盛軼
殷宗而陋漢宋矣但自古神氣固弛於積
弊之後而元氣反索於勵精之餘矯枉之
punctuated:
欲成人之美者，恨起之九原而不可得也。故漢昭十四而識上官桀之詐，明而不察，有足驗者。至於章帝，雖稱長厚，事功所就不及孝宣遠甚，羅從彥竟以彼善於此者，其意顧不可想與？則孝元以下，或仁而懦，或懦而不仁，或察而不明者，固不足厪執事之問也。無亦憂治世而危明主乎？聖天子在上，賢公卿在下，愚無有於國武子之慮也，請得而盡言之。
夫我祖宗以仁厚立國，重煕累洽，聖聖相承，元氣之厚如歲之春。至於先朝，承平既久，人心怠緩，法度廢弛。我皇上以不世出之資，起而承之，豈能一日逸於民上哉？搜煩剔蠹，振揚而飭勵之，君子猶以為晚也。邇猶宴視逖聽，以致大小臣工亦罔不滌除厥志，以承休德，中興之盛軼殷宗而陋漢宋矣。但自古神氣固弛於積弊之後，而元氣反索於勵精之餘，矯枉之
translation_en:
…those who wish to bring another’s virtues to perfection regret that they cannot raise him from the grave. Thus Emperor Zhao of Han, at fourteen, recognized Shangguan Jie’s deception: here is sufficient evidence of discernment without intrusive scrutiny. As for Emperor Zhang, although praised for generosity and kindness, his accomplishments fell far short of Emperor Xiaoxuan’s. Yet Luo Congyan ultimately judged the former better than the latter. Can we not discern his intention? As for Emperor Xiaoyuan and those after him, some were benevolent but weak, some weak without being benevolent, and some scrutinizing without being discerning. They surely do not merit troubling you with an inquiry. Might you nevertheless be anxious over a well-governed age and apprehensive for an enlightened ruler? With the sage Son of Heaven above and worthy dukes and ministers below, I, in my ignorance, have none of Guo Wuzi’s apprehensions. Allow me to speak fully.
Our imperial ancestors founded the state upon benevolence and generosity. Prosperity accumulated and harmony deepened; sage succeeded sage, and the fullness of the realm’s primal vitality was like spring in the yearly cycle. By the preceding reign, however, peace had endured so long that people’s hearts had grown indolent and laws and institutions had fallen into neglect. Our present emperor, endowed with gifts rarely seen in an age, arose to inherit this state of affairs. How could he spend even a single day at ease above the people? In ferreting out vexatious abuses and removing sources of corruption, rousing and disciplining the realm, he was still thought by gentlemen to have acted late. He views what is near at ease [?] and listens to what is distant, with the result that officials great and small all cleanse their intentions to uphold his splendid virtue. The splendor of this restoration surpasses that of the Yin sovereign and makes the Han and Song restorations seem paltry. Yet from antiquity, although the spirit has indeed slackened after abuses have accumulated, primal vitality has conversely become exhausted in the wake of strenuous efforts at renewal. The correcting of what is bent…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
太過不見者或他出也聰明果斷者戒於
太察溫良慈厚者戒於無斷此人之性君
人之三德仁可不爲最要乎匡衡司馬光
雖槩舉之實各諷其君之所不足反而求
之不更有切於今日者乎舉其畧則忠邪
當辨也而大臣之細過勿詰可也事理當
審也而言官狂戇者勿遽震之威可也罔
上當懲也而事無首尾泛相沿及者勿槩
坐可也陽非陰是陽是陰非者可誅也而
===
所見不同本無意必者勿絕其生還可也
所以沛
皇仁扶國脉者豈皆在於百姓之身萬里之外
哉
朝廷之上輦轂之下無非元氣所在斲喪少
甚卽四方所聞而解體也仁明之長漢文
兼之而不盡人之情不居多乎宋仁劣於
武而刑以不殺爲威社稷靈長終必賴之
矣其政悶悶其民醇醇二君是也其政察
punctuated: 太過，不見者或他出也。聰明果斷者戒於太察，溫良慈厚者戒於無斷，此人之性。君人之三德，仁可不爲最要乎？匡衡、司馬光雖槩舉之，實各諷其君之所不足。反而求之，不更有切於今日者乎？舉其畧，則忠邪當辨也，而大臣之細過勿詰可也；事理當審也，而言官狂戇者勿遽震之威可也；罔上當懲也，而事無首尾、泛相沿及者勿槩坐可也；陽非陰是、陽是陰非者可誅也，而所見不同、本無意必者勿絕其生還可也。所以沛皇仁、扶國脉者，豈皆在於百姓之身、萬里之外哉？朝廷之上、輦轂之下，無非元氣所在，斲喪少甚，卽四方所聞而解體也。仁明之長，漢文兼之，而不盡人之情，不居多乎？宋仁劣於武，而刑以不殺爲威，社稷靈長，終必賴之矣。其政悶悶，其民醇醇，二君是也。其政察
translation_en:
…going too far in correcting abuses: consequences not apparent here may emerge elsewhere [?]. Those who are intelligent and decisive must guard against excessive scrutiny; those who are gentle, kind, and generous must guard against indecision. Such are human dispositions. Among the three virtues of a ruler, can benevolence fail to be the most essential? Although Kuang Heng and Sima Guang discussed these virtues in general terms, each was actually remonstrating indirectly against his own ruler’s shortcomings. If we turn back and examine ourselves in their light, do they not bear still more directly upon the present day?
To outline the essentials: loyalty and wickedness must be distinguished, yet it is permissible to refrain from investigating the minor faults of high ministers. The principles and circumstances of affairs must be examined, yet it is permissible to refrain from immediately intimidating outspoken and blunt remonstrance officials with imperial might. Deceiving the sovereign must be punished, yet where the full circumstances of a case are unclear and people are indiscriminately implicated through their connections [?], it is permissible to refrain from condemning them all alike. Those who openly condemn what they secretly approve, or openly approve what they secretly condemn, may be punished; yet those whose views differ, but who originally harbored no preconceptions or stubborn insistence, should not be denied the possibility of returning alive.
Can the means of spreading imperial benevolence and sustaining the lifeblood of the state lie entirely among the common people, ten thousand li away? Within the court and beneath the wheels of the imperial carriage, the state’s vital energy is present everywhere. If the harm done to it becomes even somewhat excessive, people throughout the realm will hear of it and lose heart. Emperor Wen of Han possessed the strengths of both benevolence and discernment; yet were not the occasions on which he refrained from probing people’s circumstances to the utmost more numerous [?]? Emperor Renzong of Song was less accomplished in martial prowess, yet in administering punishment he made refraining from killing the source of his authority. The dynasty’s enduring good fortune ultimately depended upon this. “When government is unobtrusive, its people are simple and sincere”: this describes those two rulers. “When government is exacting…”

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
察其民皞皞宣神是也我
皇上聰明神武仁孝慈聖固如天之陰陽寒暑
周流而未嘗息也苟臣子愛君無已之心
猶欲爲
聖德萬分有一之助者則亦曰崇寬大之體以
養和平之福而已寧有文帝之謙讓無寧
有宣帝之督察寧神宗之法有不盡無寧
可無仁宗四十年之恭儉惇德允元非帝
舜所以咨牧乎克寬克仁非成湯所以造
===
商乎執事處江湖之遠而憂其君者也一
得之愚得遇于巷焉則沉潜剛克高明柔
克願爲吾
君告也明作有功惇大成裕願爲吾相告也若
曰書生之見非所以
獻則愚之所甚惑焉
第三問
鄭守道
同考試官敎諭潘 批 諫諍一策正欲觀士
punctuated:
察，其民皞皞，宣、神是也。我皇上聰明神武，仁孝慈聖，固如天之陰陽寒暑，周流而未嘗息也。苟臣子愛君無已之心，猶欲爲聖德萬分有一之助者，則亦曰崇寬大之體，以養和平之福而已。寧有文帝之謙讓，無寧有宣帝之督察；寧神宗之法有不盡，無寧可無仁宗四十年之恭儉。「惇德允元」，非帝舜所以咨牧乎？「克寬克仁」，非成湯所以造商乎？執事處江湖之遠而憂其君者也。一得之愚，得遇于巷焉，則「沉潜剛克，高明柔克」，願爲吾君告也；「明作有功，惇大成裕」，願爲吾相告也。若曰書生之見非所以獻，則愚之所甚惑焉。

第三問
鄭守道
同考試官敎諭潘批：諫諍一策，正欲觀士
translation_en:
…scrutinizing, its people are unsettled: Emperor Xuan of Han and Emperor Shenzong of Song exemplify this. Our sovereign is intelligent and divinely martial, benevolent and filial, compassionate and sagely. These qualities are indeed like heaven’s yin and yang, cold and heat, circulating without ever ceasing. If his servants, in their unending love for their ruler, still wish to contribute even one ten-thousandth to his sagely virtue, they can only urge him to uphold magnanimity and thereby nurture the blessings of peace and harmony. Better to possess Emperor Wen’s humility and deference than Emperor Xuan’s searching scrutiny; better that Emperor Shenzong’s laws remain incompletely implemented than to lack Emperor Renzong’s forty years of reverence and frugality. Was not “honoring the virtuous and trusting the good” how Emperor Shun admonished his regional governors? Was not being “capable of magnanimity and benevolence” how Cheng Tang founded the Shang?

You, sir, dwell far away among the rivers and lakes, yet remain concerned for your ruler. Should this humble insight of mine find an encounter in the lanes [?], I would ask you to convey to our ruler these words: “For the reserved and retiring, mastery through firmness; for the lofty and brilliant, mastery through gentleness.” I would ask you to convey to our chief minister these words: “Intelligent action achieves merit; generous greatness brings abundance.” If it is said that a scholar’s views are unfit to present to the throne, I am deeply perplexed by that assertion.

Third Question
Zheng Shoudao
Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: This policy question on remonstrance was intended precisely to discern the candidates’…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
子忠義志氣只據先儒論說雖富於記誦何益此
策於進諫聽諫皆有獨見而以先儒之言合之子
豈因人成事者耶
同考試官敎授彭批議論侃侃詞采英發
負忠懷直久矣他日當路幸毋忘於斯言
考試官主事江批不迂不激曲盡事理子
而有言責執此以往
考試官署員外郎陸批士子平日無忠直識見
臨事終不能磊落過人吾得此策且拭目以視子矣
===
善聽者無擇言善諫者無定術邇察廣詢
君之道也擇言而聽則於善必有所遺陳
善閑邪臣之職也定術而諫則於機或有
所失明王不惡誹謗之言以納忠烈士不
憚死亡之誅以極諫爲是故耳愚嘗想夫
唐虞三代之時君臣道合其相倚也手足
腹心通爲一體其相親也家人父子混爲
一家君惟恐臣之不言多方以誘之臣惟
恐君之怠肆無事亦警之言斥乘輿而上
punctuated:
子忠義志氣，只據先儒論說，雖富於記誦，何益？此策於進諫、聽諫皆有獨見，而以先儒之言合之，子豈因人成事者耶？

同考試官敎授彭批：議論侃侃，詞采英發。負忠懷直久矣，他日當路，幸毋忘於斯言。

考試官主事江批：不迂不激，曲盡事理。子而有言責，執此以往。

考試官署員外郎陸批：士子平日無忠直識見，臨事終不能磊落過人。吾得此策，且拭目以視子矣。

善聽者無擇言，善諫者無定術。邇察廣詢，君之道也；擇言而聽，則於善必有所遺。陳善閑邪，臣之職也；定術而諫，則於機或有所失。明王不惡誹謗之言以納忠，烈士不憚死亡之誅以極諫，爲是故耳。愚嘗想夫唐虞三代之時，君臣道合，其相倚也，手足腹心通爲一體；其相親也，家人父子混爲一家。君惟恐臣之不言，多方以誘之；臣惟恐君之怠肆，無事亦警之。言斥乘輿，而上
translation_en:
…the candidates’ loyalty, righteousness, and strength of purpose. If they merely rely on the arguments of earlier Confucian scholars, what use is even extensive memorization? This policy essay offers independent insights into both giving and receiving remonstrance, bringing the words of earlier scholars into accord with them. Are you someone who depends on others to accomplish things?

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, an Instructor: Your arguments are forthright, and your literary expression brilliant. You have long cherished loyalty and uprightness. When you hold authority in the future, I hope you will not forget these words.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, a Secretary: Neither impractical nor intemperate, this fully explores the principles underlying affairs. If you come to bear responsibility for speaking out, hold to this and proceed.

Comment by Examiner Lu, an acting Vice Director: A candidate who ordinarily lacks loyal and upright judgment will never, when confronted with affairs, distinguish himself through exceptional integrity. Having read this policy essay, I shall watch your future with keen anticipation.

One who listens well does not pick and choose among statements; one who remonstrates well has no fixed method. Closely examining what is near and consulting widely constitute the ruler’s way. If he listens selectively, he will inevitably overlook some good counsel. Setting forth what is good and guarding against what is wrong constitute the minister’s duty. If he remonstrates by a fixed method, he may miss the opportune moment. It is for this reason alone that enlightened kings do not resent critical words, so that they may receive loyal counsel, and resolute men do not shrink from execution, so that they may remonstrate to the utmost.

I have often reflected on the age of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties. Rulers and ministers were united in the Way. In their mutual dependence, they were like hands and feet, belly and heart, joined in a single body; in their mutual affection, they were like members of a household, fathers and sons, united as one family. The ruler feared only that his ministers would fail to speak, and encouraged them in many ways. Ministers feared only that their ruler would become negligent and unrestrained, and warned him even when no trouble had arisen. Their words directly rebuked the sovereign, yet he …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
無怒色詞涉忌諱而下無畏心舜之責禹
曰予違汝弼汝無面從退有後言益之告
舜曰儆戒無虞罔失法度罔遊于逸罔淫
于樂其氣象何如哉周官師氏掌以媺詔
王而敎國子以德則凡守衞而居王之前
後左右者皆以德而詔王也保氏掌諫王
惡而敎國子以道則凡守衞而備王之顧
問應對者皆以道而諫王也夫師氏將順
於無事之時保氏匡救於有過之日法亦
===
備矣然又矇瞍以詩諫士師以言諫太史
以史諫庶人以謗諫貨物亂常商旅獻議
遊畋無節獸臣誦箴飲食荒淫膳夫揚觶
川澤失時虞臣斷罟諫無常職而人得以
諫降至春秋此意猶有存者諫議大夫之
名起於漢補闕拾遺之名起於唐司諫正
言之名起於宋歐陽脩曰諫官者天下之
得失一時之公議係焉諫官雖卑與宰相
等司馬光曰以天下之政四海之眾得失
punctuated:
無怒色，詞涉忌諱而下無畏心。舜之責禹曰：「予違汝弼，汝無面從，退有後言。」益之告舜曰：「儆戒無虞，罔失法度，罔遊于逸，罔淫于樂。」其氣象何如哉！周官師氏掌以媺詔王，而敎國子以德，則凡守衞而居王之前後左右者，皆以德而詔王也。保氏掌諫王惡，而敎國子以道，則凡守衞而備王之顧問應對者，皆以道而諫王也。夫師氏將順於無事之時，保氏匡救於有過之日，法亦備矣。然又矇瞍以詩諫，士師以言諫，太史以史諫，庶人以謗諫；貨物亂常，商旅獻議；遊畋無節，獸臣誦箴；飲食荒淫，膳夫揚觶；川澤失時，虞臣斷罟。諫無常職，而人得以諫。降至春秋，此意猶有存者。
諫議大夫之名起於漢，補闕拾遺之名起於唐，司諫正言之名起於宋。歐陽脩曰：「諫官者，天下之得失，一時之公議係焉。諫官雖卑，與宰相等。」司馬光曰：「以天下之政，四海之眾，得失
translation_en:
…showed no anger; when their words touched upon taboos, those below felt no fear. Shun charged Yu, saying: “When I err, correct me. Do not agree to my face and then speak against me after withdrawing.” Yi admonished Shun, saying: “Be watchful even when there is no cause for concern. Do not depart from the established standards; do not wander into idleness or indulge excessively in pleasure.” What a spirit prevailed among them!
In the Offices of Zhou, the Preceptor was charged with instructing the king through what was good and teaching virtue to the sons of the state. Thus all those who stood guard before and behind the king, to his left and right, instructed him through virtue. The Guardian was charged with remonstrating against the king’s faults and teaching the sons of the state the Way. Thus all those who stood guard, ready to answer the king’s inquiries, remonstrated with him according to the Way. The Preceptor supported and guided him when there was no trouble; the Guardian corrected and rescued him when he erred. These arrangements were indeed comprehensive.
Yet blind musicians also remonstrated through poetry, judicial officers through words, and the Grand Scribe through historical records; commoners remonstrated through criticism. When goods and wealth disrupted the proper order, traveling merchants offered their views. When excursions and hunts exceeded due bounds, officials in charge of beasts recited admonitions. When eating and drinking became extravagant and excessive, the Chief Steward raised his goblet in admonition. When rivers and marshes were exploited out of season, the officials responsible for natural resources cut the fishing nets. Remonstrance belonged to no fixed office, and people were free to remonstrate. Even as late as the Spring and Autumn period, something of this spirit still survived.
The title Grand Master of Remonstrance originated under the Han; the titles Reminder and Rectifier of Omissions originated under the Tang; and the titles Remonstrator and Exhorter originated under the Song. Ouyang Xiu said: “The successes and failures of the realm, and the public judgment of the age, depend upon the remonstrance officials. Though their rank is low, they stand equal to the chief councilors.” Sima Guang said: “With the government of the realm and the multitude within the Four Seas, its successes and failures…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
利病萃於一官使言之其爲任亦重矣是
言諫官有益於天下也致堂胡氏曰古者
人臣皆得進諫於君後世專設一職旣已
乖謬而居是職者又多撓亂政事是言諫
官不必設也愚獨以爲官以員定則所任
者或非其人諫以職盡則敢言者未必在
位石介剛正聞天下以范仲淹爲相恐其
牽裾折檻不使爲諫官其餘可知矣杜牧
憤藩鎭之變以身非諫官作罪言以私議
===
其餘又可知矣夫人君之尊天也其威雷
霆也人臣以卑微之身乃欲犯尊觸威強
其難爲之事沮其甚溺之情回其已行之
說發其深忌之詞豈易爲哉是故言及君
側則有投鼠之忌指摘宮闈則有齒馬之
嫌事未露而預發之則有宋人鄰父之疑
計方隱而偶及之則有關胡伐國之戮直
言抗詞則以爲謗訕而不飭旁諭曲說則
以爲游說而不實蓋君臣之間堂陛森嚴
punctuated: 利病萃於一官，使言之，其爲任亦重矣。」是言諫官有益於天下也。致堂胡氏曰：「古者人臣皆得進諫於君，後世專設一職，旣已乖謬，而居是職者又多撓亂政事。」是言諫官不必設也。愚獨以爲，官以員定，則所任者或非其人；諫以職盡，則敢言者未必在位。石介剛正聞天下，以范仲淹爲相，恐其牽裾折檻，不使爲諫官，其餘可知矣。杜牧憤藩鎭之變，以身非諫官，作《罪言》以私議，其餘又可知矣。夫人君之尊，天也；其威，雷霆也。人臣以卑微之身，乃欲犯尊觸威，強其難爲之事，沮其甚溺之情，回其已行之說，發其深忌之詞，豈易爲哉？是故言及君側，則有投鼠之忌；指摘宮闈，則有齒馬之嫌；事未露而預發之，則有宋人鄰父之疑；計方隱而偶及之，則有關胡伐國之戮。直言抗詞，則以爲謗訕而不飭；旁諭曲說，則以爲游說而不實。蓋君臣之間，堂陛森嚴
translation_en:
…benefits and harms are concentrated upon a single official, who is charged with speaking about them: his responsibility is indeed weighty.” This says that remonstrance officials benefit the realm. Master Hu, known as Zhitang, said: “In antiquity, all ministers could remonstrate with their ruler. In later ages, a special office was established for this purpose, which was already a departure from sound practice; moreover, those who occupied it often disrupted governmental affairs.” This says that there is no need to establish remonstrance officials.

In my humble view, when offices are confined to a fixed establishment, those appointed may not be the right men; when remonstrance is confined to the duties of a particular office, those who dare to speak may hold no such position. Shi Jie was renowned throughout the realm for his uprightness and firmness. When Fan Zhongyan was chief councilor, he feared that Shi would tug at the ruler’s robe or break the balustrade in remonstrance, and did not appoint him as a remonstrance official [?]. From this one can judge the other cases. Du Mu, indignant at the disorders caused by the regional military commands, considered that he himself was no remonstrance official and wrote Words of Censure (Zuiyan) to express his views privately. From this, too, one can judge the other cases.

The ruler’s exalted position is like Heaven; his dread authority is like thunder. How could it be easy for a minister, lowly as he is, to affront that exalted position and brave that authority—to press the ruler to undertake what he finds difficult, restrain the passions in which he is deeply immersed, reverse a proposal he has already put into effect, and utter words he profoundly resents? Thus, speaking of those at the ruler’s side entails the inhibition of throwing something at a rat for fear of damaging the vessel beside it; criticizing affairs within the palace incurs the suspicion associated with asking about a horse’s teeth. Exposing an affair before it has come to light invites the suspicion that befell the old neighbor of the man of Song; happening to touch upon a plan while it is still secret invites the execution associated with Guan Hu’s proposal to attack a state [?]. Speak forthrightly and argue forcefully, and one is judged slanderous and unrestrained; offer indirect admonition and circuitous explanations, and one is judged a glib persuader lacking substance. For between ruler and minister, the distinction between the hall above and the steps below is forbiddingly strict…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而誠意難以格心禮節煩多而簡牘難以
盡意積日而思蓄銳而發自以為周旋委
曲而咫尺尊嚴往往至于顛倒錯亂自致
罪戾勢之所拘威之所劫而亦或不能以
自達焉耳况臣之進諫於君者智或不足
以濟忠德或不足以養節見時事之乖謬
悻悻負忿不量可否不度進退而遽欲責
備于君剛不足以發奸射佞而粗或至于
侵上凌尊直不足以開誠布公而妄或至
===
于臆度附會夫面折以忠告相知猶或按
劔逆耳以責難父子不免動色而乃欲深
望于君臣之間哉夫亦各盡其道而已君
之於諫臣愚以為當取其大節而畧其小
過夫慷慨任事艱險不避而以身許國者
大節也聞見不審而言或至于失節學術
未至而詞或不能達意小過也必求小過
則言之可聽者鮮矣賈山曰開道而求諫
和顏色而受之用其言而顯其身陸贄曰
punctuated:
而誠意難以格心，禮節煩多而簡牘難以盡意。積日而思，蓄銳而發，自以為周旋委曲，而咫尺尊嚴，往往至于顛倒錯亂，自致罪戾。勢之所拘，威之所劫，而亦或不能以自達焉耳。况臣之進諫於君者，智或不足以濟忠，德或不足以養節，見時事之乖謬，悻悻負忿，不量可否，不度進退，而遽欲責備于君。剛不足以發奸射佞，而粗或至于侵上凌尊；直不足以開誠布公，而妄或至于臆度附會。夫面折以忠告，相知猶或按劔；逆耳以責難，父子不免動色，而乃欲深望于君臣之間哉？夫亦各盡其道而已。
君之於諫，臣愚以為當取其大節而畧其小過。夫慷慨任事，艱險不避，而以身許國者，大節也；聞見不審而言或至于失節，學術未至而詞或不能達意，小過也。必求小過，則言之可聽者鮮矣。賈山曰：「開道而求諫，和顏色而受之，用其言而顯其身。」陸贄曰：
translation_en:
…and sincere intentions can hardly reach the ruler’s heart; ceremonial formalities are so numerous that written submissions can hardly convey one’s meaning fully. A minister may ponder for days, muster his resolve, and then speak, believing that he has handled everything tactfully and with due consideration. Yet in the immediate presence of sovereign majesty, he often becomes confused and disordered, bringing punishment upon himself. Constrained by his position and overawed by authority, he may simply be unable to make himself understood. Moreover, a minister who remonstrates with his ruler may lack the wisdom to make his loyalty effective or the virtue to sustain his integrity. Seeing the perversities of current affairs, he indignantly harbors resentment, neither weighing what is possible nor judging when to advance or withdraw, but abruptly demanding perfection of his ruler. His firmness is insufficient to expose wrongdoing and assail flatterers, yet his coarseness may lead him to affront his superior and violate sovereign dignity. His forthrightness is insufficient to establish sincerity and impartiality, yet his rashness may lead him to conjecture and strained interpretations. When confronted directly with loyal admonition, even close friends may lay their hands on their swords; when urged toward difficult standards in words unwelcome to the ear, even fathers and sons cannot avoid showing displeasure. How, then, can one expect so much of the relationship between ruler and minister? Each need only fulfill the proper duties of his position.
As for a ruler’s response to remonstrance, your foolish servant believes that he should recognize a minister’s integrity in great matters and overlook his minor faults. To undertake affairs with spirited resolve, shun neither hardship nor danger, and pledge oneself to the state—these are marks of integrity in great matters. To speak improperly because one has not carefully verified what one has heard and seen, or to fail to express one’s meaning because one’s learning has not fully matured—these are minor faults. If one insists on searching out minor faults, little will remain that deserves a hearing. Jia Shan said: “Open the way and seek remonstrance; receive it with a kindly countenance; act on the speaker’s words and advance him to distinction.” Lu Zhi said: …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
天不以地有惡木而廢發生人主不以時
有小人而廢聽納是或一道也臣之諫君
愚以為平居當感之以誠意臨事則相度
乎機宜盖鞠躬盡力夙夜匪懈而日以忠
信道德輔之所以取信於君也不幸而有
過可以諷則諷不觸怒以沽名可以直則
直不畏威以縱惡斯善矣程子曰至誠以
感動之盡力以扶持之明義理以致其知
杜蔽惑以誠其意蘇子曰理而諭之雖蔽
===
必悟勢而禁之雖驕必懼利而誘之雖怠
必奮激而怒之雖懦必立隱而諷之雖暴
必容即此意也雖然進諫之難臣之仰望
於君者也在君者不可強而致聽諫之難
君之自盡於已者也在已者猶可以勉而
為然義之所激臣多甘心於不測之禍而
情之未通君常詰責於易從之言豈非尊
卑之分迥別難易之勢反異乎此三代而
下所以鳴陽之鳳猶聞其繼響止輦之風
punctuated:
「天不以地有惡木而廢發生，人主不以時有小人而廢聽納。」是或一道也。臣之諫君，愚以為平居當感之以誠意，臨事則相度乎機宜。盖鞠躬盡力，夙夜匪懈，而日以忠信道德輔之，所以取信於君也。不幸而有過，可以諷則諷，不觸怒以沽名；可以直則直，不畏威以縱惡，斯善矣。程子曰：「至誠以感動之，盡力以扶持之，明義理以致其知，杜蔽惑以誠其意。」蘇子曰：「理而諭之，雖蔽必悟；勢而禁之，雖驕必懼；利而誘之，雖怠必奮；激而怒之，雖懦必立；隱而諷之，雖暴必容。」即此意也。
雖然，進諫之難，臣之仰望於君者也，在君者不可強而致；聽諫之難，君之自盡於已者也，在已者猶可以勉而為。然義之所激，臣多甘心於不測之禍；而情之未通，君常詰責於易從之言。豈非尊卑之分迥別，難易之勢反異乎？此三代而下，所以鳴陽之鳳猶聞其繼響，止輦之風
translation_en:
…“Heaven does not cease bringing forth life because the earth has harmful trees; the ruler does not cease hearing and accepting counsel because his age has petty men.” This may be one way to proceed. As for a minister’s remonstrance with his ruler, in my humble view he should move the ruler through sincerity in ordinary times and, when affairs arise, weigh the circumstances and the appropriate moment. To devote himself with utmost diligence, never slackening morning or night, and daily assist the ruler with loyalty, trustworthiness, moral principle, and virtue—this is how he gains the ruler’s trust. If, unfortunately, the ruler commits a fault, the minister should admonish indirectly when that is appropriate, without provoking anger to purchase a reputation; when direct speech is appropriate, he should speak directly, without allowing fear of the ruler’s power to make him indulge wrongdoing. That would be good. Master Cheng said: “Move him with utmost sincerity; support him with all your strength; clarify moral principles to extend his knowledge; shut out obstructions and delusions to make his intentions sincere.” Master Su said: “Explain through reason: however benighted, he will understand. Restrain through the force of circumstances: however arrogant, he will feel fear. Entice through benefit: however indolent, he will exert himself. Stir him to indignation: however timid, he will take a stand. Admonish through veiled words: however violent, he will tolerate them.” This is precisely the meaning.
Nevertheless, the difficulty of presenting remonstrance concerns what the minister looks to his ruler to provide; what rests with the ruler cannot be obtained by force. The difficulty of hearing remonstrance concerns what the ruler must accomplish within himself; what rests with oneself can still be achieved through effort. Yet, impelled by righteousness, ministers often willingly face unforeseeable calamity, while rulers, because their ministers’ sentiments have not reached them, often rebuke even words that would be easy to follow. Is this not because the distinction between superior and subordinate is so great that their relative positions of ease and difficulty are reversed? This is why, since the Three Dynasties, the phoenixes calling on the sunny slope—the upright remonstrators—have still been heard in succession, while the practice of halting the imperial carriage to hear remonstrance…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
不可以多見也夫直節壯煩非量不容孤
忠臆見非明不察戇言狂態非仁不恕密
謀幾疏非剛不斷然則臣子之有志於盡
職納忠者惟恃我
天子之神聖焉耳若曰我善進諫我善進諫豈
不妄哉
第四問
謝炯
同考試官訓導李批知人一策場中答者
===
率多惑於擇術辨而有據正而不乖僅見此篇
同考試官敎諭易批觀人之術自是一種
道理此策援引切實議論明正蓋積學待問之士
取之
考試官主事江批探本之論
考試官署員外郎陸批抑術崇敎可謂知大體矣
人才可以術而知乎曰術可以知人不可
以盡人君子必定之以法人才可以法而
知乎曰法可以盡人不足以化人君子必
punctuated:
不可以多見也。夫直節壯煩，非量不容；孤忠臆見，非明不察；戇言狂態，非仁不恕；密謀幾疏，非剛不斷。然則臣子之有志於盡職納忠者，惟恃我天子之神聖焉耳。若曰「我善進諫，我善進諫」，豈不妄哉？

第四問
謝炯

同考試官訓導李批：知人一策，場中答者率多惑於擇術，辨而有據，正而不乖，僅見此篇。

同考試官敎諭易批：觀人之術，自是一種道理。此策援引切實，議論明正，蓋積學待問之士，取之。

考試官主事江批：探本之論。

考試官署員外郎陸批：抑術崇敎，可謂知大體矣。

人才可以術而知乎？曰：術可以知人，不可以盡人，君子必定之以法。人才可以法而知乎？曰：法可以盡人，不足以化人，君子必
translation_en:
…cannot often be witnessed. Firm integrity and forceful importunity [?] cannot be tolerated without magnanimity; solitary loyalty and personal opinions cannot be discerned without insight; blunt words and wild conduct cannot be pardoned without benevolence; confidential plans and incipient lapses [?] cannot be decisively handled without firmness. Thus, subjects intent on fulfilling their duties and offering their loyalty rely solely upon the divine wisdom of our Son of Heaven. If one were to say, “I am skilled at remonstrating! I am skilled at remonstrating!” would that not be presumptuous?

Fourth Question
Xie Jiong 謝炯

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: Most candidates answering the policy question on discerning men’s abilities were confused about the choice of techniques. This essay alone argues with evidence and is sound without departing from principle.

Comment by Associate Examiner Yi, Instructor: The techniques for assessing people have principles of their own. This policy essay cites pertinent, substantive evidence, and its arguments are clear and correct. Its author is evidently a scholar who has accumulated learning and awaits consultation. Select him.

Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: An argument that probes the root of the matter.

Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: By subordinating techniques and exalting moral instruction, he may be said to understand the larger principles.

Can human talent be discerned through techniques? I reply: techniques can reveal a person’s abilities, but cannot reveal them fully; the gentleman must assess them by established standards. Can human talent be discerned through established standards? I reply: standards can reveal a person’s abilities fully, but are insufficient to transform him; the gentleman must…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
本之以敎蓋化不以敎雖堯舜之民不免
於自棄試不以法雖盜蹠之行亦可以自
飾敎不行而後詳之以法法其盛於敎之
衰乎法不精而後濟之以術術其起於法
之廢乎愚請究敎之所以衰以及術之所
以盛蓋昔三代盛時上之人日以道德禮
樂倡率之士之於道若飢渴之於飲食寒
暑之於裘葛終其身習且安焉不復有他
道異端惑亂乎其志而日趨於正其有化
===
之不變敎之不改者且移之左移之右移
之郊與遠方矣安得上欺天子下混羣臣
以恣其不肖之行哉故觀人之術三代以
前未之有也自夫敎化不行於天下而選
舉考課之法又不足以察之士惟爵祿之
可以釣致襲取者以殫竭其心力而不復
知有聖賢之學或陽爲而陰叛或善始而
罔終是故敝車羸馬託之乎節儉巽牀循
墻託之乎恭讓毁璧揮金託之乎廉潔忍
punctuated: 本之以敎。蓋化不以敎，雖堯舜之民不免於自棄；試不以法，雖盜蹠之行亦可以自飾。敎不行而後詳之以法，法其盛於敎之衰乎？法不精而後濟之以術，術其起於法之廢乎？愚請究敎之所以衰，以及術之所以盛。蓋昔三代盛時，上之人日以道德禮樂倡率之，士之於道，若飢渴之於飲食、寒暑之於裘葛，終其身習且安焉。不復有他道異端惑亂乎其志，而日趨於正。其有化之不變、敎之不改者，且移之左，移之右，移之郊與遠方矣。安得上欺天子，下混羣臣，以恣其不肖之行哉？故觀人之術，三代以前未之有也。自夫敎化不行於天下，而選舉考課之法又不足以察之，士惟爵祿之可以釣致襲取者，以殫竭其心力，而不復知有聖賢之學。或陽爲而陰叛，或善始而罔終。是故敝車羸馬，託之乎節儉；巽牀循墻，託之乎恭讓；毁璧揮金，託之乎廉潔；忍
translation_en:
…ground it in instruction. For if people are transformed without instruction, even the people of Yao and Shun cannot avoid abandoning themselves to wrongdoing; if they are tested without established standards, even someone whose conduct resembles that of Robber Zhi can make himself appear worthy. Only when instruction ceases to operate are detailed standards applied: do standards flourish as instruction declines? Only when standards lack precision are techniques brought in to supplement them: do techniques arise when standards fall into disuse? I venture to investigate why instruction declined and, in turn, why techniques flourished.

In the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties, those above daily led the way through the Way, virtue, rites, and music. Scholars stood in relation to the Way as the hungry and thirsty do to food and drink, or as people in cold and heat do to furs and hemp clothing. Throughout their lives they practiced it and found repose in it. No other ways or heterodox teachings any longer confused their aspirations, and each day they advanced toward what was right. Those who did not change under transforming influence or reform through instruction were moved to the left, to the right, or to the outskirts and distant regions. How could they deceive the Son of Heaven above, mingle among his ministers below, and freely indulge their unworthy conduct? Thus, techniques for judging men did not exist in the Three Dynasties or earlier.

Once moral instruction ceased to operate throughout the realm, and the rules for selecting men for office and evaluating their performance were also insufficient to scrutinize them, scholars exhausted their mental energies solely on ranks and emoluments that they could angle for and seize. They no longer knew of the learning of sages and worthies. Some outwardly conformed while inwardly rebelling; others began well but failed to carry through to the end. Thus, they passed off battered carriages and emaciated horses as frugality; crouching beneath a bed and walking close against walls as deference and modesty; smashing jade disks and scattering gold as incorruptibility; enduring [?]…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
世嫉俗託之乎剛介姦足以殘民害物而
口不絕誦乎堯舜之道佞足以惑君蠹國
而手不停披乎周孔之書世方徇於所見
以為聖賢復生舉國以授之惟恐其不屑
而不知志得意滿且舉其所勉強者而盡
棄之以肆其故智矣此觀人之術所以不
可無也李克之告文侯曰居視其所親富
視其所與達視其所舉窮視其所不為貧
視其所不取夫以管寧而同處者甘心於
===
助逆以大斗而貸民者設志於篡國能薦
管仲而不可秉政避居於陵而反亂大倫
李克之術可盡信乎莊子曰遠使之而觀
其忠近使之而觀其敬煩使之而觀其能
卒然問焉而觀其智急與之期而觀其信
委之財而觀其仁告之危而觀其節醉之
酒而觀其則雜之處而觀其色夫以帝丘
之對其流也佞柱下之期其失也固管仲
富有三歸而不害其為忠晏子不死崔難
punctuated:
世嫉俗，託之乎剛介；姦足以殘民害物，而口不絕誦乎堯舜之道；佞足以惑君蠹國，而手不停披乎周孔之書。世方徇於所見，以為聖賢復生，舉國以授之，惟恐其不屑，而不知志得意滿，且舉其所勉強者而盡棄之，以肆其故智矣。此觀人之術所以不可無也。
李克之告文侯曰：「居視其所親，富視其所與，達視其所舉，窮視其所不為，貧視其所不取。」夫以管寧而同處者，甘心於助逆；以大斗而貸民者，設志於篡國；能薦管仲，而不可秉政；避居於陵，而反亂大倫。李克之術可盡信乎？
莊子曰：「遠使之而觀其忠，近使之而觀其敬，煩使之而觀其能，卒然問焉而觀其智，急與之期而觀其信，委之財而觀其仁，告之危而觀其節，醉之酒而觀其則，雜之處而觀其色。」夫以帝丘之對，其流也佞；柱下之期，其失也固。管仲富有三歸，而不害其為忠；晏子不死崔難
translation_en:
…resenting the world and detesting its ways, they pass this off as upright integrity. Their treachery is sufficient to injure the people and harm all things, yet their mouths never cease reciting the Way of Yao and Shun. Their flattery is sufficient to delude the ruler and corrode the state, yet their hands never stop turning the pages of the writings of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. People follow what meets their eyes, believing that sages and worthies have been reborn. They entrust the entire state to such men, fearing only that they might disdain to accept it. They do not realize that, once these men have attained their ambitions and are thoroughly satisfied, they will discard entirely even the conduct they had forced themselves to maintain, giving free rein to their old tricks. This is why methods of judging people are indispensable.
Li Ke told Marquis Wen: “In ordinary life, observe whom a man holds close; when he is wealthy, observe whom he gives to; when he has attained prominence, observe whom he recommends; in adversity, observe what he refuses to do; in poverty, observe what he refuses to take.” Yet one who lived alongside Guan Ning willingly helped a rebel; one who lent grain to the people using a large measure set his heart on usurping the state; one capable of recommending Guan Zhong could not himself take charge of government; and one who withdrew to live at Wuling instead violated the cardinal human relationships. Can Li Ke’s methods be trusted entirely?
Zhuangzi said: “Send him on a distant mission and observe his loyalty; employ him close at hand and observe his respectfulness; burden him with tasks and observe his ability; question him unexpectedly and observe his intelligence; give him an urgent deadline and observe his trustworthiness; entrust him with wealth and observe his benevolence; tell him of danger and observe his integrity; make him drunk with wine and observe his adherence to proper standards; place him in mixed company and observe his demeanor.” Yet the reply at Diqiu [?] tended toward flattery, while the appointment beneath the pillar erred in obstinate rigidity. Guan Zhong possessed the wealth of the Sangui estate [?], yet this did not detract from his loyalty; Yanzi did not die in the calamity brought about by Cui…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
而不害其爲賢莊子之術可盡驗乎蘇子
曰委之利以觀其節乘之猝以觀其量伺
之獨以觀其守懼之敵以觀其氣愚以爲
蘇子之言即二子之緒餘耳朱子推易書
陰陽之理以爲君子小人之辨其言曰凡
光明正大疏暢通達無纖芥可疑者必君
子也依阿澳涊回互隱伏不可方物者必
小人也蓋其考驗之術不於其迹而於其
心如鑑之於妍媸權之於輕重莫有能遁
===
其情者又豈三子之術所可同哉然人君
以有限之知慮而欲勝無窮之奸欺以一
人之聞見而欲盡億兆之變態力既不足
日亦不給況上用目則下飾觀上用耳則
下飾聲上用慮則下飾辭且奈之何哉夫
人無善惡惟世升降陸贄曰漢武好英風
故其時富瓌詭立名之士漢宣精吏治故
其時萃循良核實之能言士之係乎所率
也亦以見教之不以道乎蓋人心之變詐
punctuated: 而不害其爲賢。莊子之術可盡驗乎？蘇子曰：「委之利以觀其節，乘之猝以觀其量，伺之獨以觀其守，懼之敵以觀其氣。」愚以爲蘇子之言，即二子之緒餘耳。朱子推易書陰陽之理，以爲君子小人之辨。其言曰：「凡光明正大，疏暢通達，無纖芥可疑者，必君子也；依阿澳涊，回互隱伏，不可方物者，必小人也。」蓋其考驗之術，不於其迹而於其心，如鑑之於妍媸，權之於輕重，莫有能遁其情者，又豈三子之術所可同哉？然人君以有限之知慮，而欲勝無窮之奸欺；以一人之聞見，而欲盡億兆之變態，力既不足，日亦不給。況上用目則下飾觀，上用耳則下飾聲，上用慮則下飾辭，且奈之何哉？夫人無善惡，惟世升降。陸贄曰：「漢武好英風，故其時富瓌詭立名之士；漢宣精吏治，故其時萃循良核實之能。」言士之係乎所率也，亦以見教之不以道乎？蓋人心之變詐
translation_en:
…yet this did not detract from his worthiness. Can Zhuangzi’s methods invariably prove reliable? Master Su said: “Entrust a man with opportunities for profit to observe his integrity; take him by surprise to observe his capacity; watch him when alone to observe what he holds fast to; frighten him with an enemy to observe his courage.” In my humble opinion, Master Su’s words are merely remnants of the teachings of the preceding two masters. Master Zhu drew upon the principles of yin and yang in the Book of Changes to distinguish gentlemen from petty men. He said: “Anyone who is bright and upright, open and free of obstruction, with not the slightest cause for suspicion, must be a gentleman. Anyone who is obsequious and murky [?], evasive and concealed, and impossible to appraise, must be a petty man.” His method of examining and testing people thus attends to their hearts rather than their outward conduct. Like a mirror distinguishing beauty from ugliness or a balance distinguishing lightness from heaviness, it allows none to conceal their true nature. How could the methods of the other three masters compare with this?

Yet when a ruler seeks, with his limited knowledge and deliberation, to overcome endless treachery and deceit, and with one person’s observations to comprehend every changing disposition among his countless subjects, his strength is insufficient and his days do not suffice. Moreover, when those above rely on their eyes, those below embellish appearances; when those above rely on their ears, those below embellish sounds; when those above rely on deliberation, those below embellish their words. What, then, can be done?

People, whether good or evil, follow the rise and decline of their age. Lu Zhi said: “Emperor Wu of Han admired a heroic spirit, so his time abounded in men who established their reputations through extraordinary accomplishments. Emperor Xuan of Han was expert in the administration of officials, so his time brought together men capable of conscientious government and the scrutiny of actual performance.” This means that men of service depend upon the leadership they receive. Does it not also reveal that their instruction has failed to accord with the Way? For the shifts and deceptions of the human heart…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
伺之以智術則益競而不服感之以道德
或相觀而易化察之以一人則勢孤而易
欺公之以兼聽則思廣而難掩君能先以
道德倡率之使天下之人莫若自愧其不
善者而不能以自容然後嚴法以試覈之
必如陸贄所謂言事之得者勿卽謂是必
原其所得之由言事之失者勿卽謂非必
窮其所失之理必如蘇洵所謂某也廉吏
嘗以某事知其廉某也能吏嘗以某事知
===
其能則亦可以杜天下之欺詐矣而何以
術爲哉大抵天下有不可盡之情而亦無
必可盡之術以帝堯之明不免失之伯鯀
以孔子之聖不免失之宰予以及孔明之賢
不免失之馬謖勢固然也惟夫論官器使
之時欲任之以事不可不知其才欲責之
以忠不可不知其行欲托之以腹心不可
不知其情不然朱子之說其可用乎蓋晉
惠以執玉而徵惰晉文以肅命而啓覇郤
punctuated:
伺之以智術，則益競而不服；感之以道德，或相觀而易化；察之以一人，則勢孤而易欺；公之以兼聽，則思廣而難掩。君能先以道德倡率之，使天下之人莫若自愧其不善者而不能以自容，然後嚴法以試覈之，必如陸贄所謂：「言事之得者，勿卽謂是，必原其所得之由；言事之失者，勿卽謂非，必窮其所失之理。」必如蘇洵所謂：「某也廉吏，嘗以某事知其廉；某也能吏，嘗以某事知其能。」則亦可以杜天下之欺詐矣，而何以術爲哉？

大抵天下有不可盡之情，而亦無必可盡之術。以帝堯之明，不免失之伯鯀；以孔子之聖，不免失之宰予；以及孔明之賢，不免失之馬謖，勢固然也。惟夫論官器使之時，欲任之以事，不可不知其才；欲責之以忠，不可不知其行；欲托之以腹心，不可不知其情。不然，朱子之說其可用乎？蓋晉惠以執玉而徵惰，晉文以肅命而啓覇，郤
translation_en:
…If one watches for such deceit through clever stratagems, people only become more competitive and refuse to submit. If one moves them through moral virtue, they may observe one another and readily be transformed. If one scrutinizes them through a single person's efforts, one's position is isolated and easily deceived. If one opens the matter to broad consultation, one's deliberations become comprehensive and wrongdoing is difficult to conceal. If the ruler first leads them through moral virtue, making everyone under Heaven ashamed of their own wrongdoing and unable to tolerate it in themselves [?], and then applies strict laws to examine and verify their conduct, he must follow what Lu Zhi said: “When someone's statement about an affair is sound, do not immediately pronounce it correct; trace the grounds on which he arrived at it. When someone's statement about an affair is mistaken, do not immediately pronounce it wrong; investigate fully the reasons for his error.” He must also follow what Su Xun said: “So-and-so is an incorruptible official: I learned of his integrity through a particular affair. So-and-so is a capable official: I learned of his ability through a particular affair.” In this way, deception throughout the realm can be stopped. What need would there be for stratagems?

Generally speaking, there are circumstances in the world that cannot be fully fathomed, and no technique can be guaranteed to fathom them all. Even Emperor Yao, with his discernment, could not avoid misjudging Bo Gun; even Confucius, with his sagacity, could not avoid misjudging Zai Yu; and even Kongming, with his worthiness, could not avoid misjudging Ma Su. Such is the nature of things. When assessing men for office and employing them according to their capacities, if one wishes to entrust them with affairs, one must know their abilities; if one wishes to demand loyalty from them, one must know their conduct; if one wishes to trust them as intimate confidants, one must know their true dispositions. Otherwise, could Master Zhu's teaching be put into practice? Duke Hui of Jin revealed his negligence in the way he held the jade, while Duke Wen of Jin laid the foundation of his hegemony by reverently receiving a command; Xi…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
樊以燕享而兆亡冀缺以恭敬而昭德威
儀之可以識人乆矣草蟲見子展之恭大
明識子圍之亂旣醉占蘧罷之賢鶉奔卜
良霄之淫言語之可以識人乆矣況燕間
顧問肝膽畢露章疏奏對舉動悉見使人
君能少加之意則亦何患乎人才之難知
乎舍是而求諸他術縱可以盡得天下之
情亦非所以望於人君者而況開伺察之
門啓攻訐之風其弊恐不止於失人而已
===
也執事以爲然否
第五問
張槩
同考試官學正王批識時務在俊傑必是
古非今者俗儒也此策斟酌古今確有定見讀之
快人心目且隊仗錯落不羈超逸之才自非輿衞
可制也佳士佳士
考試官主事江批適用之才
考試官署員外郎陸批有學識
punctuated:
樊以燕享而兆亡，冀缺以恭敬而昭德。威儀之可以識人乆矣。《草蟲》見子展之恭，《大明》識子圍之亂，《旣醉》占蘧罷之賢，《鶉奔》卜良霄之淫。言語之可以識人乆矣。況燕間顧問，肝膽畢露；章疏奏對，舉動悉見。使人君能少加之意，則亦何患乎人才之難知乎？舍是而求諸他術，縱可以盡得天下之情，亦非所以望於人君者。而況開伺察之門，啓攻訐之風，其弊恐不止於失人而已也。執事以爲然否？
第五問
張槩
同考試官學正王批：「識時務在俊傑，必是古非今者，俗儒也。此策斟酌古今，確有定見，讀之快人心目。且隊仗錯落，不羈超逸之才，自非輿衞可制也。佳士！佳士！」
考試官主事江批：「適用之才。」
考試官署員外郎陸批：「有學識。」
translation_en:
…Fan [?], through his conduct at a banquet, foreshadowed his downfall, while Ji Que manifested his virtue through reverence and respect. That a person can be known through his bearing has long been established. “Grass Insects” revealed Zizhan’s respectfulness; “Great Brightness” disclosed Ziwei’s rebelliousness; “Already Drunk” foretold the worthiness of Qu Ba [?]; and “Quails Running” foretold Liang Xiao’s licentiousness. That a person can be known through his words has long been established. Moreover, when a ruler consults men in private, their innermost thoughts are fully revealed; in their memorials and responses at audience, their conduct is entirely apparent. If the ruler could give these matters a little attention, why should he worry that talented men are difficult to recognize? To abandon these means and seek other techniques—even if these could uncover the dispositions of everyone in the realm—is not what we should expect of a ruler. Still less should he open the door to spying and encourage a fashion for malicious accusations: the harm would surely extend beyond errors in judging men. Do you, sir, consider this correct?
Fifth Question
Zhang Gai
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “It takes outstanding men to understand the needs of the times. Those who insist on approving antiquity and condemning the present are commonplace scholars. This policy essay weighs past and present and has firm, well-grounded judgments. Reading it delights the mind and eye. Moreover, its ranks and formations [?] are varied: such unrestrained and exceptional talent certainly cannot be confined by the bounds of an escort formation. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!”
Comment by Examiner Jiang, Secretary: “A talent suited to practical employment.”
Comment by Examiner Lu, Acting Vice Director: “He possesses learning and discernment.”

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
先王之法不可必復於後世也譬則古方
然寒暑之所傷虛實之所受出古人料理
之外者十病而五也治之者必古方而後
用雖扁鵲必致人於不可藥以死善醫者
不惟其方惟其病善治者不惟其法惟其
意而惟其意也即其法少異同焉可也意
之不存而必於其區區者求之亦與亂同
事而已周禮聖人之方書也井田封建肉
刑方之大者也雖創於古而地官司寇之
===
載實始詳備焉自商鞅開阡陌李斯置郡
縣漢文易笞箠而其法澣盡矣彷古之畧
者於董仲舒見限田之議焉於李安世見
均田之制焉於唐太宗見口分世業之法
焉然皆議之而不能行或行之而不能乆
懲秦孤立大封同姓矣七國之釁高實釀
之子弟爲王三軍置焉首八王之難者晉
武也隋文命高熲更定新律而肉刑之廢
猶故反至于今便之執事嘗思而得其故
punctuated: 先王之法不可必復於後世也。譬則古方然，寒暑之所傷，虛實之所受，出古人料理之外者，十病而五也。治之者必古方而後用，雖扁鵲，必致人於不可藥以死。善醫者不惟其方，惟其病；善治者不惟其法，惟其意。而惟其意也，即其法少異同焉可也。意之不存，而必於其區區者求之，亦與亂同事而已。《周禮》，聖人之方書也；井田、封建、肉刑，方之大者也。雖創於古，而地官、司寇之載，實始詳備焉。自商鞅開阡陌，李斯置郡縣，漢文易笞箠，而其法澣盡矣。彷古之畧者，於董仲舒見限田之議焉，於李安世見均田之制焉，於唐太宗見口分世業之法焉。然皆議之而不能行，或行之而不能乆。懲秦孤立，大封同姓矣，七國之釁，高實釀之；子弟爲王，三軍置焉，首八王之難者，晉武也。隋文命高熲更定新律，而肉刑之廢猶故，反至于今便之。執事嘗思而得其故
translation_en:
The institutions of the former kings cannot necessarily be restored in later ages. They resemble ancient medical prescriptions: of illnesses caused by cold and heat or arising from deficiency and excess, five in ten fall outside what the ancients knew how to treat. If a physician insists on using only ancient prescriptions, even Bian Que will surely bring people to an incurable state and death. A good physician attends not merely to the prescription but to the illness; a good ruler attends not merely to the institutions but to their underlying intent. Provided that he attends to that intent, some departure from those institutions is permissible. If their intent is lost and one insists on seeking it in their petty particulars, one merely contributes to disorder.

The Rites of Zhou is the sages’ book of prescriptions. The well-field system, the establishment of hereditary fiefs, and mutilating punishments are its major prescriptions. Although these originated in antiquity, only in its accounts of the Ministry of Education and the Minister of Justice were they first recorded fully and in detail. Once Shang Yang opened up the field boundaries, Li Si established commanderies and counties, and Emperor Wen of Han substituted flogging, those institutions were entirely washed away [?]. As for broad attempts to imitate antiquity, we find Dong Zhongshu’s proposal to limit landholdings, Li Anshi’s equal-field system, and Emperor Taizong of Tang’s arrangements for land allotted per person and land held as a hereditary estate. Yet these were all either proposed without being implemented, or implemented without enduring.

Taking warning from Qin’s isolation, the Han extensively enfeoffed members of the imperial clan; yet it was Gaozu himself who sowed the seeds of the conflict of the Seven Kingdoms. Sons and younger brothers were made kings and furnished with armies; the initiator of the calamity of the Eight Kings was Emperor Wu of Jin. Emperor Wen of Sui ordered Gao Jiong to revise and establish a new legal code, yet the abolition of mutilating punishments remained unchanged; indeed, down to the present, people have found this advantageous. Have you, sir, ever reflected upon this and grasped the reason …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎堯舜之道使民宜之時異勢殊周公有
弗强焉故議井田於封建已廢之後者惑
也夫即使盡得天下之田而在官也固非
平澗谷夷丘陵破墳墓不可又使盡得平
原廣野而規畫之也必假以數十年之力
後世天下一國郡縣之吏數歲一代將使
誰爲之乎即爲之而數十年之內民將不
暇耕乎蘇洵葉適明若觀火橫渠之術非
夫人所得而喻也然則欲復井田必先復
===
封建天下爲家是法之難又有甚焉者矣
問鼎射王伐凡伯誅萇弘宣王而後周其
能振乎宗元之論要有窺測而胡明仲乃
謂封建可以支變故殊不知封建郡縣之
不足以支變故均也三代而後變故之大
獨封建爲能速之至於肉刑則古者教之
有素復重其法以懸之所以使之易避而
難犯後世之君既不能教而犯者接踵陳
群劉頌之徒不務輕重笞數使不至於殺
punctuated: 乎？堯舜之道，使民宜之。時異勢殊，周公有弗强焉。故議井田於封建已廢之後者，惑也。夫即使盡得天下之田而在官也，固非平澗谷、夷丘陵、破墳墓不可；又使盡得平原廣野而規畫之也，必假以數十年之力。後世天下一國，郡縣之吏數歲一代，將使誰爲之乎？即爲之，而數十年之內，民將不暇耕乎？蘇洵、葉適明若觀火，橫渠之術，非夫人所得而喻也。然則欲復井田，必先復封建。天下爲家，是法之難，又有甚焉者矣。問鼎、射王、伐凡伯、誅萇弘，宣王而後，周其能振乎？宗元之論，要有窺測，而胡明仲乃謂封建可以支變故，殊不知封建、郡縣之不足以支變故，均也。三代而後，變故之大，獨封建爲能速之。至於肉刑，則古者教之有素，復重其法以懸之，所以使之易避而難犯。後世之君既不能教，而犯者接踵，陳群、劉頌之徒不務輕重笞數，使不至於殺
translation_en: …have you? The Way of Yao and Shun was to make arrangements suited to the people. When times and circumstances differed, even the Duke of Zhou would not force matters. Thus, those who propose the well-field system after hereditary enfeoffment has already been abolished are misguided. Even if all the land under Heaven could be brought into government possession, implementing it would necessarily require filling ravines and valleys, leveling hills and ridges, and demolishing graves. Even if one obtained nothing but broad plains and open country to lay out, the work would still require several decades. In later ages, all under Heaven forms a single state, and officials of prefectures and counties are replaced every few years. Whom could one charge with carrying it out? Even if it were undertaken, would the people have no time to cultivate their fields during those decades? Su Xun and Ye Shi saw this as clearly as a blazing fire; Hengqu’s method is not something everyone can comprehend. Thus, to restore the well-field system, one must first restore hereditary enfeoffment. With all under Heaven treated as one family’s possession, the difficulties of this system are greater still. Questioning the possession of the tripods, shooting the king, attacking Fan Bo, executing Chang Hong—after King Xuan, could Zhou ever recover its strength? Zongyuan’s argument does, in essence, show insight; yet Hu Mingzhong claimed that hereditary enfeoffment could withstand upheavals. He entirely failed to understand that hereditary enfeoffment and the prefectural and county system are equally incapable of withstanding them. After the Three Dynasties, hereditary enfeoffment was especially apt to hasten great upheavals. As for mutilating punishments, in antiquity the people had long been instructed; severe laws were then also promulgated before them, making it easy to avoid transgression and difficult to commit it. Rulers of later ages failed to instruct the people, and offenders followed one another in an unbroken succession. Men such as Chen Qun and Liu Song did not endeavor to adjust the number of strokes of the rod according to the gravity of the offense, so that they would not result in killing…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
人乃汲汲於求墨劓荆者而復之以爲足
以永絕其淫放穿窬之路是欲使賢如孫
臏史遷者而常不得全肢體於世也孔融
諸人豈無見哉唐太宗固好名主也知周
禮真聖人所作而曰不井田不封建不肉
刑欲行周公之道不可得也信斯言也則
築阿房之宮發閭左之戍嚴刑峻法毒痛
四海假使井田封建較若畫一即能保秦
之不亡乎太宗缺於關雎麟趾之意而惟
===
欲竊其一二糟粕以爲粉飾太平之具吾
未見其能成康也謂周公之治而專在區
區法制間乎不然則我
祖宗聖知度越千古創制立法視周爲備丈量
天下之田矣而止於定三等之賦分天下
爲十三省矣而
宗藩不得治民而典兵頒
大誥與律令矣而黥剌之刑戒後世不得復用
豈其忽先王而崇季世哉誠勢有所不能
punctuated: 人，乃汲汲於求墨劓荆者而復之，以爲足以永絕其淫放穿窬之路，是欲使賢如孫臏、史遷者，而常不得全肢體於世也。孔融諸人豈無見哉？唐太宗固好名主也，知周禮真聖人所作，而曰：「不井田，不封建，不肉刑，欲行周公之道不可得也。」信斯言也，則築阿房之宮，發閭左之戍，嚴刑峻法，毒痛四海，假使井田封建較若畫一，即能保秦之不亡乎？太宗缺於關雎、麟趾之意，而惟欲竊其一二糟粕，以爲粉飾太平之具，吾未見其能成康也。謂周公之治，而專在區區法制間乎？不然，則我祖宗聖知度越千古，創制立法，視周爲備，丈量天下之田矣，而止於定三等之賦；分天下爲十三省矣，而宗藩不得治民而典兵；頒《大誥》與律令矣，而黥剌之刑戒後世不得復用。豈其忽先王而崇季世哉？誠勢有所不能
translation_en:
…people, but instead eagerly sought to restore tattooing, cutting off the nose, and other punishments [?], believing these sufficient to close off forever the paths of licentiousness and burglary. This would mean that even men as worthy as Sun Bin and Sima Qian would continually be unable to preserve their bodies intact in this world. Surely Kong Rong and the others had some insight!

Emperor Taizong of the Tang was certainly a ruler fond of reputation. He knew that the Rites of Zhou was truly the work of a sage, yet said: “Without the well-field system, the establishment of hereditary fiefs, and corporal mutilation, it is impossible to practice the Way of the Duke of Zhou.” If these words are true, then even with the building of Epang Palace, the conscription of poor households for garrison service, and harsh punishments and severe laws inflicting suffering throughout the realm, could Qin have been assured against destruction merely by implementing well-fields and hereditary fiefs with perfect uniformity? Taizong lacked the spirit of “The Ospreys” and “The Qilin’s Hooves,” yet wished only to appropriate a few remnants as ornaments of an age of peace. I cannot see how he could thereby have matched Kings Cheng and Kang. Can the Duke of Zhou’s government be said to have resided solely in such petty matters of laws and institutions?

If so, consider our imperial ancestors, whose sagely wisdom surpassed all antiquity. They created institutions and established laws more comprehensive than those of Zhou. They surveyed the land throughout the realm, yet went no further than fixing three grades of taxation. They divided the realm into thirteen provinces, yet the imperial princes were not permitted to govern the people and command troops. They promulgated the Grand Pronouncements together with the statutes and ordinances, yet forbade later generations to reinstate tattooing as punishment. Could they have slighted the former kings and exalted the practices of a declining age? In truth, circumstances make certain things impossible…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
時有所不可也執事以爲今之天下民日
益貧吏日益肆獄訟日益煩者是豈不井
田封建肉刑之過哉坐不能以今日之法
行先王之意耳周禮小司徒經土地而井
牧其田野而稅斂之事則曰施其職而平
其政大司徒建公侯伯子男之國而小宰
則以六計弊羣吏之治司刑掌五刑之法
以麗萬民之罪而小司寇之聽獄訟也必
曰用情訊之是知井田封建肉刑者周公
===
之法也平稅斂察吏治求民情者周公之
意也今天下之田獨病於兼併乎常賦之
外無名而征者相望也司國柄者盍亦爲
守令擇人乎如其人雖郡縣不害省力役
薄稅斂崇本抑末豪強有禁窮困有養田
不井而民可甦於貧矣今之用法者得無
有深鉤摭以爲聰明或恃姑息以惠奸慝
者乎小大之獄必以情此曹劌之所與一
戰也平其心索其實守其法使有罪者不
punctuated:
時有所不可也。執事以爲今之天下民日益貧、吏日益肆、獄訟日益煩者，是豈不井田、封建、肉刑之過哉？坐不能以今日之法行先王之意耳。《周禮》，小司徒經土地而井牧其田野，而稅斂之事則曰：「施其職而平其政。」大司徒建公侯伯子男之國，而小宰則以六計弊羣吏之治。司刑掌五刑之法，以麗萬民之罪，而小司寇之聽獄訟也，必曰：「用情訊之。」是知井田、封建、肉刑者，周公之法也；平稅斂、察吏治、求民情者，周公之意也。
今天下之田獨病於兼併乎？常賦之外，無名而征者相望也。司國柄者盍亦爲守令擇人乎？如其人，雖郡縣不害。省力役，薄稅斂，崇本抑末，豪強有禁，窮困有養，田不井而民可甦於貧矣。
今之用法者，得無有深鉤摭以爲聰明，或恃姑息以惠奸慝者乎？小大之獄必以情，此曹劌之所與一戰也。平其心，索其實，守其法，使有罪者不
translation_en:
…and there are things that the times do not permit. You, sir, consider that the people of the realm grow poorer by the day, officials grow more unrestrained, and lawsuits grow more numerous. But can this be blamed on the absence of the well-field system, hereditary enfeoffment, and mutilating punishments? It is simply because we fail to carry out the intentions of the former kings through the laws of today. In the Rites of Zhou, the Vice Minister of Education lays out the land and divides its fields into well-field and pastoral units; yet concerning taxation, the text says: “Assign their obligations and equalize their levies.” The Minister of Education establishes the domains of dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons, while the Vice Minister of State judges the administration of the officials by six criteria. The Director of Punishments administers the statutes of the five punishments to apply them to the offenses of the people; yet in the Vice Minister of Justice’s hearing of criminal and civil cases, the text expressly says: “Question them according to the true circumstances.” Thus we know that the well-field system, hereditary enfeoffment, and mutilating punishments were the Duke of Zhou’s institutions, while equalizing taxation, scrutinizing official administration, and ascertaining the people’s actual circumstances were his intentions.
Is the land of the realm today afflicted only by its accumulation in the hands of the few? Beyond the regular taxes, exactions without any legitimate designation abound everywhere. Why do those who wield the authority of the state not select suitable men to serve as prefects and magistrates? With the right men, even government through prefectures and counties does no harm. Reduce labor services, lighten taxation, promote agriculture and restrain secondary pursuits, curb the powerful, and provide for the destitute: then, even without dividing the fields into well-field units, the people can recover from poverty.
Among those who apply the law today, are there not some who pride themselves on their cleverness in probing deeply and picking out incriminating details, or others who rely on indulgence and thereby favor the wicked? “In lawsuits great and small, one must proceed according to the true circumstances”: this was what Cao Gui endorsed as grounds for fighting a battle. Keep the mind impartial, seek out the facts, and uphold the law, so that those who are guilty do not…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
得免而無罪者不得濫則惡者懲善者勸
刑罰清而萬民服矣豈必今日麗一民焉
斷其足明日麗一民焉截其鼻駭觀易聽
而後為皐陶哉合乎人情宜於土俗而不
失乎先王之意者則善法先王者也病告
絕而猶曰軒轅曰岐伯後之言治者皆不
免焉其甚也則王田市易亦曰本諸周禮
青苗均輸則曰非自我出以聖人致治之
書而反為萬世悞天下者之口實也豈曰
===
老生之常談已乎宜乎執事之不欲聞而
愚生之不樂道也
punctuated: 得免，而無罪者不得濫，則惡者懲，善者勸，刑罰清而萬民服矣。豈必今日麗一民焉，斷其足；明日麗一民焉，截其鼻，駭觀易聽，而後為皐陶哉？合乎人情，宜於土俗，而不失乎先王之意者，則善法先王者也。病告絕，而猶曰軒轅，曰岐伯，後之言治者皆不免焉。其甚也，則王田、市易亦曰本諸《周禮》；青苗、均輸則曰非自我出。以聖人致治之書，而反為萬世悞天下者之口實也，豈曰老生之常談已乎？宜乎執事之不欲聞，而愚生之不樂道也。
translation_en: …escape punishment, while the innocent are not indiscriminately punished, then the wicked will be chastened and the good encouraged; punishments will be justly administered, and all the people will submit. Must one subject a person to punishment today and cut off his foot, then another tomorrow and cut off his nose, shocking those who see and startling those who hear, before one can be a Gao Yao? Those who accord with human feelings, suit local customs, and preserve the intent of the former kings are the ones who follow those kings well. The illness is declared incurable, yet they still invoke Xuanyuan and Qibo: those of later ages who discuss government all fall into this failing. In its most extreme forms, even the policies of “royal fields” and state market trading were said to be founded on the Rites of Zhou; the “green shoots” loans and equitable transport policies were likewise defended with the claim, “These did not originate with me.” Thus a book through which the sages brought about good government has instead become a pretext for those who bring harm to the realm in every age. Can this be dismissed as merely an old scholar’s commonplace talk? No wonder you, Sir, do not wish to hear it, and I, your foolish student, take no pleasure in speaking of it.

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄕試錄後序
王官出主試事制乎曰制也前有
之乎曰無至自
王也曷言乎制也曰其允臧創也
制矣閩之役臣銓以司馬郎
臣以達以司寇郎寔聞
上命拜而出也胥及於河祝曰休
===
哉我
后之克艱厥事也所不與同心者
有如此河胥曰諾兼程而即
之無何以其錄
奏成事焉是役也或曰閩沠海
派江其俗嗇其人朴而惷其
性緩其爲文辭不務去陳言
punctuated:
福建鄕試錄後序

王官出主試事，制乎？曰：「制也。」前有之乎？曰：「無。」至自王也，曷言乎制也？曰：「其允臧，創也制矣。」閩之役，臣銓以司馬郎，臣以達以司寇郎，寔聞上命，拜而出也。胥及於河，祝曰：「休哉！我后之克艱厥事也！所不與同心者，有如此河！」胥曰：「諾。」兼程而即之。無何，以其錄奏成事焉。

是役也，或曰：「閩沠海派江，其俗嗇，其人朴而惷，其性緩，其爲文辭不務去陳言
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

Is the dispatch of court officials to preside over the examination an established regulation? The answer is: “It is.” Has there been a precedent? The answer is: “No.” Since it originates with the sovereign, why call it an established regulation? The answer is: “If it is truly good, even an innovation becomes an established regulation.” On this assignment to Fujian, your servant Quan, serving as a bureau director in the Ministry of War, and your servant Yida, serving as a bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, received His Majesty’s command, bowed, and set out. Together we reached the river and made a solemn invocation: “How admirable that our sovereign appreciates the difficulty of this undertaking! Should we fail to work with one heart, let this river bear witness!” Together we answered, “Agreed.” Traveling by forced stages, we reached our destination. Before long, we submitted the examination record to the throne and reported the completion of our duties.

Concerning this assignment, someone said: “Fujian is divided by sea channels and branching rivers [?]. Its customs are frugal; its people are simple and unsophisticated, and their disposition is slow. In composing prose, they make no effort to discard stale expressions …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
臣已而度分水闢劔門據龍
首之峯晞無諸之城崇山巨
谷隱嶙鬱律雲物之紛郁郁
難詳乃嘆曰於壯哉天地之
隩區也遵武夷訪雲谷謁考
亭苔碑蘚勒往往而在讀其
書想見其人乃嘆曰亮哉故
===
國也文獻足徵焉入其國青
衿白皙磬折而集容容如也
祁祁如也乃嘆曰都得非君
子之澤乎三進而試之言必
稽諸理劌而辯拙而有倫徐
而索之震撼擊撞有關中之
氣焉洋洋纚纚有兩浙之才
punctuated:
臣已而度分水，闢劔門，據龍首之峯，晞無諸之城。崇山巨谷，隱嶙鬱律，雲物之紛，郁郁難詳。乃嘆曰：「於，壯哉！天地之隩區也！」遵武夷，訪雲谷，謁考亭，苔碑蘚勒，往往而在。讀其書，想見其人，乃嘆曰：「亮哉，故國也！文獻足徵焉！」

入其國，青衿白皙，磬折而集，容容如也，祁祁如也。乃嘆曰：「都！得非君子之澤乎？」三進而試之，言必稽諸理，劌而辯，拙而有倫。徐而索之，震撼擊撞，有關中之氣焉；洋洋纚纚，有兩浙之才
translation_en:
I, your servant, then crossed Fenshui, made my way through Jianmen, took my stand upon the peak of Longshou, and gazed toward [?] the city of Wuzhu. Lofty mountains and immense valleys rose in rugged, densely massed folds; clouds and landscapes mingled in a profusion too rich to describe in detail. I sighed in admiration: “Ah, how magnificent! This is a secluded realm of Heaven and Earth!” I followed the paths of Wuyi, visited Yungu, and paid my respects at Kaoting. Steles and inscriptions covered in moss were to be found everywhere. Reading his writings, I imagined the man himself. I sighed in admiration: “Truly, this is a land of ancient traditions! Its writings and worthy men furnish ample testimony!”

Entering this land, I found fair-complexioned scholars in blue collars gathering with deeply bowed bodies, composed in bearing and orderly in their numbers. I exclaimed: “Ah! Can this be anything other than the lasting beneficence of the gentleman?” Three times I brought them forward and examined them. Their words invariably referred back to principle: incisive and discriminating, unadorned yet coherent. Examining them at leisure, I found a force that shook and struck, possessing the vigor of Guanzhong; flowing abundantly and continuously, they possessed the literary talent of Liangzhe…

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
焉冕弁巍峩有
畿內之制焉夫氣言之充也才
言之華也制言之官也充則
不靡華則不固官則不詭於
法而理以歸之莫之遷也臣
殫厥心用罔惑厥觀浹旬而
出無留良焉是日也諸大夫
盍二三子宴之賦鹿鳴臣作
而曰二三子是詩也非肄業
及之也豈旨酒是湛亦嘉賓
之心是樂將湏其勤勞不怠
以從王事四牡所以次鹿鳴
也子觀國之光服其身於
王匪言之徵惟行之徵行不顧言
punctuated:
焉。冕弁巍峩，有畿內之制焉。夫氣，言之充也；才，言之華也；制，言之官也。充則不靡，華則不固，官則不詭於法，而理以歸之，莫之遷也。臣殫厥心，用罔惑厥觀，浹旬而出，無留良焉。
是日也，諸大夫盍二三子宴之，賦《鹿鳴》。臣作而曰：「二三子，是詩也，非肄業及之也。豈旨酒是湛，亦嘉賓之心是樂。將湏其勤勞不怠，以從王事，《四牡》所以次《鹿鳴》也。子觀國之光，服其身於王，匪言之徵，惟行之徵。行不顧言，
translation_en:
…there. Their lofty bearing, like that of men in ceremonial caps, possessed the regulated form of the metropolitan region. Vital force gives substance to expression; talent gives it elegance; regulated form gives it discipline. With substance, expression is not feeble; with elegance, it is not rigid; with discipline, it does not depart from established standards. Principle brings all these into accord, permitting no deviation. Your servant devoted his whole mind to the task, so that his judgment would be free from confusion. After ten full days, the selections were released, with no worthy candidate left behind.
On that day, the assembled officials gathered the candidates [?] and feasted them, reciting “The Deer Call” (Lu ming). Your servant rose and said: “You gentlemen, this poem is not something that study alone enables you to grasp. Is it merely a matter of drinking fine wine to the full? It is also a matter of gladdening the hearts of honored guests. They will be expected to labor diligently and tirelessly in the king’s service: this is why ‘The Four Stallions’ (Si mu) follows ‘The Deer Call.’ You behold the splendor of the realm and dedicate yourselves to the king’s service. It is not your words that will furnish the proof, but your deeds. If your deeds take no account of your words, …

title: 嘉靖七年福建鄉試錄
text:
非夫也將罔克利於爾有躬
矧曰其耀我主司鹿鳴曰人
之好我示我周行我寔好子
誰能靳之四牡曰豈不懷歸
王事靡鹽周行也諸大夫僉
曰然書於錄
承直郎刑部福建清吏司主
===
事江以達謹序
punctuated:
非夫也，將罔克利於爾有躬，矧曰其耀我主司！《鹿鳴》曰：「人之好我，示我周行。」我寔好子，誰能靳之？《四牡》曰：「豈不懷歸？王事靡鹽。」周行也。諸大夫僉曰：「然。」書於錄。
承直郎、刑部福建清吏司主事江以達謹序。
translation_en:
…is no true man, and will be unable to bring benefit to your own persons, much less bring honor to us who preside over the examination! “Deer Calling” says: “Those who care for me show me the right path.” I truly care for you; who could withhold such guidance? “The Four Stallions” says: “How could I not long to return home? The king’s business permits no respite [?].” This is the right path. The assembled gentlemen all said, “Indeed.” Thus these words were written in the examination record.
Preface respectfully composed by Jiang Yida, Gentleman for Straightforward Service and Secretary in the Fujian Bureau of the Ministry of Justice.
